Executing a tool call logs at information level with the documented execution text. Measured addsNothingNew over 251 spans. Kept above P2 because level and message are both pinned, which is what a log consumer filters on, though the count is only at-least-once.

Ten event ids are asserted to fall in the numeric band reserved for their category - agent, middleware or provider. Measured greedy front at rank 32 with +53 spans and 53 exclusive spans. In the project P0 prefix and deliberately held there at P1: prefix membership nominates a candidate rather than conferring a tier, and the contract above is a component-level guarantee rather than the critical baseline a component-scoped P0 run is built from.

A null factory falls back to the null logger and logging through it does not throw. Measured coverage of zero spans. The fallback is written in the test itself with a null-conditional and a coalesce, so what is asserted is the test's own expression rather than any product behaviour.

A mock factory returns the logger it was configured to return. Measured coverage of zero spans. It asserts the behaviour of its own mock setup.

Logging four levels through the library's null logger does not throw. Measured coverage of zero spans, and the closing assertion is that a local it just assigned is not null.
Logging an exception at three levels through the library's null logger does not throw. Measured coverage of zero spans.
A log call carrying an event id constant arrives with that id. Measured coverage of zero spans - the only product symbol is the constant itself and the assertion is against a mock.
A message template with two placeholders renders both values into the state passed to the logger. Measured coverage of zero spans - the subject is the logging library, not this repository.
Create mints a distinct agentmsg-prefixed generation id per message and rejects blank message id, agent id, and name; a shared generation id would merge distinct messages under one client key.
A body carrying $type agent decodes to AgentMessage with every structured field and the enum type intact; the read half of the discriminated wire path.

Measured coverage places it in the greedy front at rank 63 with 17 new spans and 2 spans no other test reaches. Losing it silently downgrades every persisted agent message to a TextMessage, stripping sender identity and correlation from a recovered conversation. Lowered to P1 on the prefix rule: this declaration is outside the project P0 prefix, and the component already has a prefix-nominated P0 in Deserialize_WithDiscriminator_RoundTripsEverySection confirmed on its own contract. A body missing identity decodes to empty strings rather than throwing; rehydration runs unguarded over persisted history, so one malformed row must not brick recovery of the conversation.

The distinguishing negative for that guard: a plain text body must not be captured as an agent message. Question and DelegateTask set ExpectsReply and render a reply instruction naming the correlation, the reply target, the tool, and the expected reply type; a missing instruction leaves the sender waiting for an answer the receiver never knows to send.

Zero-width, RTL-override, bell, and BOM characters are stripped, asserted per character because the culture-sensitive string overload reports them present in any string; hiding a marker inside them is how the bracket count above would otherwise be evaded.

A sender name containing a quote, a forged reply-to, and a newline is escaped and folded, and the real reply-to still names the true sender; the caller-chosen attribute value is the one injection surface the body sanitiser does not cover.
A reply carries in-response-to naming the message it answers; the correlation a receiver threads answers by.

The same hostile bodies on a reply-expecting type leave exactly one reply instruction pointing at the real sender. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew against its sibling theory now at P0, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only test proving a forged instruction cannot be added alongside a genuine one, a redirection the bracket count on a no-instruction type cannot detect.

Measured coverage places it in the greedy front at rank 72 with 12 new spans, so it is also the fewest-tests way into the sanitiser. Fifteen hostile bodies - spacing, newline, casing, zero-width, fullwidth, bracket lookalike, and RTL-override variants - each leave exactly two angle brackets open and two closed, so the body contributes no structure at all. This is the injection boundary between untrusted model output and the envelope a receiver parses, and it is proven by counting rather than by matching a filter's own patterns. Lowered to P1 on the prefix rule: this declaration is outside the project P0 prefix, and the component already has a prefix-nominated P0 in Deserialize_WithDiscriminator_RoundTripsEverySection confirmed on its own contract. Exclusive spans are a floor rather than a nomination, so the reasoning above stands as the contract while the tier does not.
Ordinary prose with backticks, an em dash, percent signs, a path, and a newline survives verbatim; the distinguishing positive that stops the hardening from mangling every legitimate message.
An opening message renders type and sender attributes, no in-response-to, and a closing tag; the base envelope shape a receiver parses.
Steer, TaskUpdate, and Response expect no reply and render no instruction; the distinguishing negative that stops unbounded agent ping-pong.

A body containing a literal closing marker leaves exactly one real closer and appears escaped instead. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew against the hostile-body theory now at P0, which covers the same sanitiser spans with fifteen variants; it stays above P2 because it alone asserts the escaped form is present rather than only that no bracket survives.
A forged reply instruction in the body is escaped even on a type that appends none of its own; unescaped it could redirect the receiver's answer to a third party.
Serialize then deserialize preserves message id, type, sender, correlation, body, generation id, and reproduces an identical envelope; combines the two halves on the real converter set.

Pins the wire shape: the "agent" discriminator, snake_case identity fields, the user role, and the rendered envelope emitted as "text". Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew against the round-trip and inference tests, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only test asserting the text projection is present on the wire, whose absence makes agent messages invisible to the model without changing which lines run.
A stale or hostile persisted "text" is ignored because Text is a get-only projection of the fields; otherwise a stored envelope could claim a sender the fields deny.
Rendering Text leaves equality and hash unchanged; the cached-envelope regression this pins made a message unfindable in a hash set the moment it was rendered.
A with-copy renders from the copy's own message id and body, not a travelled cache; a stale envelope hands the receiver an id and body the copy's fields deny, including a dangling reply correlation.
With no current instruction the section is absent and standing instructions lead; an empty heading would present an instruction that does not exist.

The current instruction is quoted verbatim including its embedded newline and carries its seq in both the heading and the row; a paraphrase or dropped seq loses the one instruction the model must follow exactly.
An empty manifest renders only the narrative section; the omission rule plus the guarantee that a checkpoint is never content-free.
The recall hint appears only when the host supplies a tool name, and names that tool; hinting at a tool the host has not registered tells the model to call something that does not exist.

Asserts the exact heading sequence, the opening tag with version, id, covered seq range, and creation time, and the closing tag. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew over the 116 renderer spans its siblings share, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only test pinning section ordering, which a renderer emitting the same sections in a different order would pass everywhere else.
Two rows list both seqs in the heading in order; a multiplicity variation on the single-row rule already pinned.
Text equals RenderEnvelope under default options, so the mirror a client shows and the text sent to the provider cannot diverge.
Absent manifest sections decode to empty collections, a clean recovery state, and default stats rather than null; consumers enumerate these without null guards.

Every top-level field and all nine manifest sections plus the rendered text survive a round trip; a section silently dropped on decode is context the model permanently loses. Measured coverage ranks it 10th in the greedy order with 167 new spans and 5 exclusive - the largest checkpoint contribution, because one test drives the writer, the reader, and every manifest section type.

Pins the discriminator, user role, snake_case checkpoint fields, the nested manifest quote, and the rendered envelope carried as text; the wire shape a persisted checkpoint takes.
Every observation field is projected, utilization is computed as measured over window-minus-reserve, and the frame is transient; the whole projection this type exists for.

Decode back to the concrete type checking the measured tokens and active checkpoint id. Pins the context_pressure discriminator, the camelCase field names, and the absence of any rendered text; a content-free frame that started carrying text would leak conversation content to a live channel.

Serialized through the production converter, threadId is present as a non-blank string whatever the ignore conditions; the wire-level half of the same guarantee.

Decode back to the concrete type with totals, uncached input, cost, and completeness intact. One aggregate reports true. Measured addsNothingNew over 43 spans. The single-message form of the sequence predicate.
One text message reports false. Measured addsNothingNew over 5 spans. The negative half of the single-message predicate.

Over a mixed sequence the non-aggregate comes back as the same instance by reference while the aggregate is replaced by rendered text. Measured addsNothingNew over 137 spans. Kept above P2 for the selectivity contract - reference identity on the untouched message is a stronger claim than equality and is what proves the transform is not rewriting ordinary messages.

An aggregate whose tool call has a null function name and null arguments is transformed rather than rejected. Measured addsNothingNew over 121 spans. The graceful-degradation intent is real but the assertions do not reach it.
uncertainties: The name says the original message is returned while the body's own comment says it transforms and the assertion requires a TextMessage - the two disagree. The assertions are only not-null and a type check, so a transform that emitted an empty body or the literal text null for the missing function name would pass unchanged.

rationale: A text message passes through as the same instance. Measured addsNothingNew over 9 spans. The single-message case of the identity assertion the collection test already makes.
A null message throws. Measured addsNothingNew over 2 spans. An argument guard.

An aggregate renders to a text message containing both the named call tag and the named response tag with the result text, and carries the originating role and agent forward. Measured addsNothingNew over 128 spans. Kept above P2 because the role and agent assertions are the attribution the rendered text alone cannot carry.

The three-argument overload stamps run, parent run and thread onto four tool message shapes and leaves the execution target alone. Measured addsNothingNew over 94 spans. Kept above P2 because parent run, thread and execution target are asserted only here - the options overload test checks generation id and run id and nothing else.

When the run advertises no generation id the provider's own id survives. Measured addsNothingNew over 31 spans. Kept above P2 as the distinguishing case: every other test here supplies a run generation id, so an implementation that assigned unconditionally would pass them all while blanking the id for every caller outside a run.

A collaboration message gets run, parent and thread identity while its message id, generation id and body come through unchanged. Measured greedy front at rank 154 with +3 spans. Kept above P2 for the preservation half - a copy that stamped identity but lost the message id would arrive unanswerable, and no other arm carries an envelope worth preserving.

Thirteen message variants covering every switch arm - text, updates, tool calls, tool results, reasoning, usage and the collaboration message - each carry a provider-stamped opaque id in and must come out with the run's identity. Measured greedy front at rank 6 with +248 spans and 21 exclusive spans, the widest reach in this project outside the parser. Criticality is independent and the test states it: a forgotten arm falls through to the identity case, returns the message unchanged, and the client's merge-key grouping silently splits one turn into fragments. The type-preservation assertion is what turns a missing arm into a failure instead of a pass.

Three real messages carrying distinct provider opaque ids all come out with the run's generation id and run id. Measured greedy front at rank 42 with +39 spans and 14 exclusive spans. Kept high as the named regression pin for the defect the file's comment records, though the parameterized theory asserts the same override for every arm, so its independent warrant is the explicit multi-message scenario rather than a contract nothing else reaches.
Create mints a distinct notify-prefixed generation id per message and rejects a blank kind; a shared generation id would merge distinct notifications under one client key.
A $type-carrying body decodes to NotifyMessage with kind, source tool name and id, label, detail, and role intact; the read half of the wire path.

Persisted rows carry no $type, so the notify_kind guard must beat the generic text fallback; losing it downgrades every stored notification to a TextMessage and drops its kind and correlation on history recovery. Lowered to P1 on the prefix rule: this declaration is outside the project P0 prefix, and the component already has a prefix-nominated P0 in Deserialize_WithDiscriminator_RoundTripsEverySection confirmed on its own contract. Exclusive spans are a floor rather than a nomination, so the reasoning above stands as the contract while the tier does not.

The distinguishing negative for that guard: a plain text row must not be captured as a notification. Measured coverage puts it near the end of the greedy order at rank 231 with 1 new span and none exclusive, so it is not the fewest-tests choice for P0; it stays above P2 because it alone detects an over-broad notify guard capturing ordinary text rows.
With a source tool the envelope carries in-response-to as name:id; this is the correlation that ties a sub-agent completion back to the call that spawned it.
Without a source tool call the envelope renders kind and label and no in-response-to; the base shape for host-originated notifications.

A payload containing a literal closing marker leaves exactly one real closer and appears escaped. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew over the 37 envelope spans its siblings share, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only notify test that detects a breakout from untrusted tool output, which no span-equivalent envelope test asserts.

Serialize then deserialize preserves every structured field and reproduces an identical envelope. Measured coverage puts it at greedy rank 27 with 59 new spans - it drives the notify converter's write and read halves and the envelope renderer in one test, the fewest-tests route into that code.
Pins the "notify" discriminator, the snake_case notify_kind and source_tool_call_id, the user role, and the envelope emitted as text so backends reading ICanGetText see it.
A stale persisted "text" is ignored because Text is a get-only projection; otherwise a stored envelope could describe a notification the fields deny.
Two Deferred instances compare equal; a record-equality boundary on an intentionally empty variant.
FromError yields a Resolved with IsError true and the supplied error code; an error payload that lost its flag would be presented to the model as a successful result.
FromMultiModal keeps the caller's block list by reference alongside the text; a copy or rewrap here loses the image blocks providers need.
FromText yields a Resolved carrying the text with no content blocks and no error flag; the ordinary tool return path every handler uses.
Struct to record projection keeps the same fields; the opposite direction, and a distinct mapping function.
Both variants are distinguishable by type in a switch and expose their payload; the closed-hierarchy contract callers dispatch on.
Composes the two projections already covered individually; a round-trip combination case.
Record to struct projection keeps the deferral fields and identity; one direction of the conversion the middleware relies on.
A deferred handler result becomes an empty result flagged deferred with a positive timestamp; without the flag the empty string would be sent to the model as the tool's answer.
Multi-modal blocks pass through the builder by reference along with identity; the multi-modal path's only direct unit coverage of the mapping.
The error flag, code, and text survive the builder mapping; a dropped flag turns a tool failure into an apparent success.

The builder stamps the tool call id and name from its arguments rather than leaving them null. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew over spans the other builder cases share, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only test that would catch the hardcoded-null regression it was written for, which orphans every result from the call it answers.
Asserts only the values set by the object initializer on a resolved record; a state-shape check rather than a behaviour of the type.
uncertainties: Asserts properties the test itself assigned, so it can only catch a member being dropped or renamed.

rationale: IsDeferred and DeferredAt survive a JSON round trip on the record; a deferred result that decodes as resolved would be answered as if it had completed.
A plainly constructed result is not deferred and has null timestamps; a default that read as deferred would strand every ordinary tool call awaiting a resolution.
A with-expression sets the deferral fields and preserves the rest; a construction variation on the struct form.
The default-value side of the same wire shape: nullable deferral fields omitted, is_deferred always written; an absent-versus-present variation.
Pins the snake_case wire names is_deferred/deferred_at, the omission of a null resolved_at, and the values surviving decode; the struct's wire contract.
An unpaired surrogate is accounted as the replacement character's three bytes; a further encoding boundary on the byte-counting rule.
Apply bounds the result text, sets IsTruncated, and preserves the call id and tool name; the struct-level entry point callers actually use.

Oversized text blocks are bounded while the image block is returned by reference; bounding an image's base64 payload would corrupt it. Measured coverage puts it at greedy rank 36 with 50 new spans and 10 exclusive - the content-block walk is reached by no other test, so it is the fewest-tests choice for that code as well as the multi-modal contract.
A small result comes back equal and unflagged; the distinguishing negative for the flag, without which everything would be reported truncated.
Pins the default cap at 4 MiB and asserts it is below the 10,485,760-byte provider field limit; a default raised past that limit reintroduces the rejected request this bounding exists to prevent.

At the smallest legal cap the output still fits the cap, keeps a real 64-character prefix, and ends with the marker naming the original size; the boundary where a naive implementation emits only a marker.

Zero, negative, and one-below-minimum caps throw with the right parameter name; a construction-time argument boundary. Raised to P1 by the exclusive-span floor: it is a front member outside the P0 prefix holding 2 exclusive spans, so dropping it would leave those product spans with no exerciser at any tier. The contract assessment above is unchanged.

The reproduction case: a 15,231,668-byte result is cut to the cap, keeps its first 1024 bytes verbatim, and ends with a marker naming the original size. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew over the 27 truncation spans other cases share, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 as the only test using the exact payload size the provider rejected, and the only one asserting the verbatim 1024-byte prefix.

The distinguishing negative: a short result is returned as the same instance with no marker, so a bounder that truncated everything cannot pass unnoticed. Measured coverage marks it addsNothingNew over ten shared spans, so it is not P0; it stays above P2 because reference identity on the untouched path is asserted nowhere else.
Text exactly at the cap is returned unchanged; the off-by-one boundary between untouched and truncated.
The flag survives struct to record to struct; a projection combination over the already-pinned flag.
200 three-byte characters under a 256-byte cap: the output fits, the kept prefix contains only whole characters, and the marker reports 600 bytes. A char-based limit would overshoot the byte cap.
Surrogate-pair emoji stay whole across the cut, checked by both an even char count and a rune scan; a split pair produces invalid text a provider may reject.
A second pass over an already-bounded result reports no cut even though the input carries the flag; this is what lets a history-ingress bound stay a no-op instead of re-marking every replayed result.
The Unbounded configuration returns the same instance for a 15 MB input; the opt-out must genuinely opt out.

Theory over the six rule types asserting IsFiltered matches the type. Measured addsNothingNew over 27 spans; it is the exhaustive table behind the per-rule factory cases already represented, so P2 rather than P1.

The negative half of the same pair: IsFiltered true with RuleType ProviderDisabled and a reason naming the provider. Measured addsNothingNew over 14 spans, so not P0; kept above P2 because with Include it pins that IsFiltered actually varies with the factory used.
Pins RuleType GlobalAllowList and its reason wording. Measured addsNothingNew; per-rule variation.
Pins RuleType GlobalBlockList, matched pattern and reason wording. Measured addsNothingNew; per-rule variation.
Pins RuleType ProviderAllowList and its reason wording. Measured addsNothingNew; per-rule variation.

Pins RuleType ProviderBlockList, the matched pattern and the reason wording. Measured addsNothingNew over the same 14 spans as the other factories; a per-rule variation of the represented filtered contract.
The filtering-disabled factory yields an included result with RuleType None. Measured addsNothingNew; a variation of Include distinguished only by its reason text.

The positive half of the result contract: Include yields IsFiltered false with RuleType None. Measured addsNothingNew over 14 spans, so not P0; kept above P2 as one half of the distinguishing pair - a FilterResult that reported every decision as filtered would still pass every Filtered* test.
A custom reason string is carried through on an included result. Measured addsNothingNew; a variation of the Include contract already represented.
Diagnostic formatting of a filtered result. Measured addsNothingNew over 18 spans; formatting variation.
Diagnostic formatting of an included result. Measured addsNothingNew over 18 spans; formatting variation.

The only test reaching the branch of ToString that appends the matched pattern: measured coverage puts it on the greedy front (rank 125, +4 spans). It is not P0 because the contract is diagnostic string formatting - a regression degrades a log line, it does not change any filtering decision - so the coverage warrant alone does not meet the P0 criticality bar.

A fully matched set of contracts and handlers constructs successfully. Measured addsNothingNew over 44 spans; the positive of the guard, which every execution test in this file also depends on, so it adds no distinguishing power of its own.
An empty contract list and empty map construct successfully. Measured addsNothingNew over 22 spans; the emptiness boundary of the constructor guard.

A null map with non-empty contracts is rejected with functionMap as the parameter name. Measured greedy front at rank 183 with 2 exclusive spans; a null variation of the missing-entry guard already represented. Raised to P1 by the exclusive-span floor: it is a front member outside the P0 prefix holding 2 exclusive spans, so dropping it would leave those product spans with no exerciser at any tier. The contract assessment above is unchanged.

A contract with no matching map entry is rejected at construction, with the offending name in the message and functionMap as the parameter name. Measured greedy front at rank 191 with 2 exclusive spans; kept above P2 because the alternative to failing here is advertising a tool to the model that has no handler when it is called.
Null contracts are rejected with functions as the parameter name. Measured addsNothingNew over 6 spans; an argument-guard boundary.

Drives OpenClientAgent's streaming reply directly over a fake SSE transport and asserts at least one message came back. Measured coverage: rank 49 with 30 exclusive spans, the largest exclusive holding in this file, because it is the only test exercising the agent's streaming path without the middleware wrapped around it. Kept out of P0 because the single assertion is a count greater than zero - it proves the path runs, not that it produces anything correct.

Constructs the fake handler, HttpClient, OpenClient and agent in sequence and ends with Assert.True(true). Measured addsNothingNew over 38 spans, and the only failure it can detect is an exception during construction.
uncertainties: its assertion is tautological, so it proves only that construction does not throw
it also reads an API key from the environment, though it asserts only whether one is present

rationale: Two parallel tool calls arrive as SSE deltas through a fake transport, are merged by index, executed, and emitted as one ToolsCallAggregateMessage carrying at least two calls including the named one. Measured coverage ranks it first in the greedy order with +1227 spans - the single largest contribution in this project's capture, because it drives the whole streaming path from SSE parsing through the agent to aggregation. Criticality is independent: parallel tool calls in a streaming reply are the product's normal case, and a merge that dropped or fused a call would leave the model waiting on a result it never gets.
uncertainties: the fake handler serves the SSE body, so no network call is made, but LoadEnvIfNeeded and GetApiBaseUrlFromEnv still read env files and variables

rationale: The single-tool-call version of the streaming aggregate assertion. Measured addsNothingNew over 1222 spans, because the multiple-tool-call test that heads this project's greedy order already covers this path, and its assertions are a subset of that test's, so P2.

A deferral produced from an agent-generated tool call is wrapped in an aggregate with the same flags. Measured addsNothingNew over 282 spans; a wrapper variation of the input-tool-call deferral, with fewer assertions than it.

A deferred handler produces a result flagged IsDeferred with empty text, a set DeferredAt, no ResolvedAt, IsError false, a non-null ToolCallId and the tool name. Measured addsNothingNew over 234 spans; kept above P2 because a deferral read as an ordinary empty result would be replayed to the model as a completed call, and the ToolCallId assertion guards a specific historical null bug.

Two calls in one message: the synchronous one carries its text with no DeferredAt, the deferred one carries the flag and empty text. Measured addsNothingNew over 251 spans; kept above P2 because it is the only case proving the flag is per result rather than per message.

A 100,000 byte result is bounded to the configured 1024 bytes, keeps its first 256 characters, carries the truncation marker and the original size, and the IsTruncated flag survives a JSON round trip as is_truncated. Measured addsNothingNew over 267 spans, so not P0; kept high above P2 because an unbounded tool result is replayed into every later turn, and the round-trip assertion is what proves the flag survives persistence.

When no tool call is present the middleware forwards to the agent with every contract attached to the options, verified by capturing the options the agent received. Measured addsNothingNew over 121 spans; kept above P2 because a model cannot call a tool it was never advertised, and this is the only test inspecting what the middleware hands downstream.

A tool call on the input message executes its handler and the result text carries the location, the temperature and the unit. Measured addsNothingNew over 244 spans, so not P0; the primary non-streaming execution path, with content assertions rather than shape-only checks.
A second registered function executes and its result contains the computed sum. Measured addsNothingNew over 244 spans; a function-level variation of the execution path already represented.

An unknown function yields a result saying it is not available and listing the registered names. Measured addsNothingNew over 217 spans; kept above P2 because returning a tool result rather than throwing is what keeps the conversation alive after a hallucinated tool name, and the listing is what lets the model recover.

A normal-sized result is not flagged, carries no marker, and serializes without the is_truncated member at all. Measured addsNothingNew over 250 spans; the distinguishing negative - a limiter that flagged everything would satisfy the oversized case alone.

In a batch containing both targets, the aggregate carries only the local call and its result, and the provider-server id appears in neither. Measured addsNothingNew over 300 spans; kept above P2 because the mixed batch is the only case that can distinguish correct filtering from executing everything or nothing.

A tool call marked ProviderServer passes through unchanged with its id and target intact rather than being executed locally. Measured greedy front at rank 159 with +3 spans; the routing rule that stops the middleware executing a call the provider already ran.

The streaming path gives a deferred handler the same flags, empty text and non-null identity as the non-streaming path. Measured addsNothingNew over 246 spans; kept above P2 because path parity is the contract - a streaming implementation that lost the deferral flag would pass every non-streaming test.

The streaming path handles a tool call present on the input message and ends with a ToolsCallResultMessage carrying a non-empty result. Measured greedy front at rank 40 with +44 spans and 13 exclusive spans. Not P0 because the assertion is only that some result text exists, which the unknown-function error also satisfies.
uncertainties: the tool call names get_weather while the map registers getWeather, so this most likely exercises the unknown-function path rather than execution
the non-empty assertion cannot tell the two apart

rationale: The same split across streamed updates merged by index: only the local call is aggregated and its result carries the computed value. Measured greedy front at rank 166 with 3 exclusive spans; a distinct path from the non-streaming case because the target must survive update merging.

Builds contracts and handlers by reflecting over the McpSampleServer assembly, invokes CalculatorTool-Add through the middleware and asserts the deserialized sum to five decimal places. Measured coverage: rank 16 with +93 spans and 73 spans no other test reaches - the MCP assembly-to-function bridge is exercised only here. Criticality is independent: this is the path every MCP-hosted tool takes into the registry, and the precision assertion catches a result serialized through a lossy conversion.

A pre-cancelled token passed to InvokeAsync is observed as cancelled inside the handler. Measured addsNothingNew over 233 spans; kept above P2 because without propagation a long-running tool keeps running after the caller has abandoned the request, which no other assertion here would reveal.

The handler observes the call's ToolCallId through its ToolCallContext. Measured addsNothingNew over 233 spans; kept above P2 because a handler that cannot identify its own call cannot correlate a deferred answer, and nothing else asserts what the context carries.

The report names each colliding function, its count and its exact provider set. Measured addsNothingNew over 65 spans, so not P0; above P2 because it alone pins the per-collision provider lists that a host uses to explain the conflict.

Three descriptors sharing one name, two of them from the same provider, must report TotalFunctions 3, UniqueNames 1, one collision counted 3 with the provider list including the repeat. Measured coverage puts it on the greedy front at rank 35 with +50 spans, the largest contribution of any test in this file, and its criticality is that it is the only case proving the report counts occurrences rather than distinct providers - the count that tells a host how many tools collide.
No collisions yields CollisionCount 0 and an empty list with the totals still correct. Measured addsNothingNew over 51 spans; the empty boundary of the report contract.

Colliding names get provider-prefixed ("Provider1-getUser", "Provider2-getUser") while the non-colliding name is left bare. Measured addsNothingNew over 86 spans, so not P0; kept above P2 under the overlapping-spans exception, because it is the only test asserting the naming-map values themselves - a resolver that prefixed everything, or nothing, would execute the same spans and be caught only here.
Custom prefixes combined with prefix-everything across four descriptors. Measured addsNothingNew over 103 spans; a combination of settings each already represented.
A configured CustomPrefix replaces the provider name for that provider only; the other keeps its provider name. Measured addsNothingNew over 102 spans; a configuration variation.
An empty input yields an empty map rather than throwing. Measured addsNothingNew over 20 spans; an emptiness boundary.

Two hundred descriptors across a hundred providers: every colliding name is prefixed and every unique one is not. Measured addsNothingNew over 86 spans; a scale variation of the represented contract. Its elapsed-time assertion is wall-clock based and machine dependent.
uncertainties: contains a wall-clock assertion (elapsed under one second) that is environment sensitive and was not executed here

rationale: With three distinct names the map returns them unchanged. Measured addsNothingNew over 76 spans; the complementary half of the prefixing contract - without it, prefix-everything passes.

An empty provider name still produces one non-empty mapped name. Measured addsNothingNew over 74 spans; a robustness boundary, and the assertions only require non-empty, so no specific name contract is proven.
uncertainties: assertions prove only non-null/non-empty, not which name is produced for an empty provider

rationale: Thirteen descriptors across three simulated MCP servers with two and three way collisions. Measured addsNothingNew over 86 spans; a larger combination of the prefixing rules already pinned, valuable but not adding a distinct contract.

Dotted names from providers with special characters yield two entries whose every character is alphanumeric, underscore or hyphen. Measured addsNothingNew over 85 spans; the count assertion precedes Assert.All so the check cannot pass vacuously, but this composes sanitization and prefixing already represented.
With UsePrefixOnlyForCollisions false, non-colliding names are prefixed too. Measured addsNothingNew over 85 spans; a configuration variation on the represented prefixing contract.

A name beginning with a digit gets a leading underscore. Measured coverage: rank 142 with 3 spans no other test reaches, so this branch is unreachable through any other measured test. Criticality is independent of coverage - a tool name starting with a digit is rejected by provider function-name rules, so a regression here produces registrations that fail at the provider rather than locally. Lowered to P1 on the prefix rule: this declaration is outside the project P0 prefix, and the component already has a prefix-nominated P0 in AnalyzeCollisions_WithMultipleFunctionsFromSameProvider_HandlesCorrectly confirmed on its own contract. Exclusive spans are a floor rather than a nomination, so the reasoning above stands as the contract while the tier does not.
An empty name becomes "unknown". Measured addsNothingNew over 5 spans; an emptiness boundary.
Each invalid character is replaced with a single underscore at its position, including a trailing one. Measured addsNothingNew over 8 spans; above P2 as the mapping the sanitizer exists to perform.
Runs of underscores collapse to one. Measured addsNothingNew; a normalization variation extending the replacement contract.

A null name returns "unknown" instead of throwing. Measured rank 169 with +2 spans and no exclusive spans; the greedy contribution is marginal and the contract is a null boundary shared with the empty-string case, so P2.

An all-invalid name collapses to the sanitized_function default rather than an empty or all-underscore name. Measured coverage gives it 3 exclusive spans (rank 141), which warrants keeping it above P2, but the consequence is a fallback label rather than an invalid registration, so it stays below the digit-prefix case in P0.

An already valid name passes through untouched, underscores, hyphens and digits included. Measured addsNothingNew over 8 spans, so not P0; above P2 because it is the only identity guarantee - a sanitizer that rewrote valid names would break every tool name while still passing the replacement cases.

The collection-level entry point actually removes blocked descriptors: exactly two of four survive and both are named, so the assertion cannot pass on an empty result. Measured addsNothingNew over 103 spans, so not P0; a distinct primary behavior (the API consumers call) beyond the single-decision method.

Filtering is applied to the registered (prefixed) name from the naming map, not the descriptor's original name. Measured addsNothingNew over 85 spans; above P2 because it alone catches a filter that is silently bypassed once collision resolution renames a function.

Theory pinning the wildcard engine every filter rule depends on: prefix, suffix, contains, bare star, exact and case-insensitive matches, each with a non-matching counterpart, and the matched pattern echoed back. Measured coverage puts it on the greedy front (rank 73, +12 spans, 97 covered) - the largest single contribution in this component - and the criticality is independent: a broken matcher either blocks every tool or blocks none, and every block/allow list in the component routes through it. Held at P0 although outside the project P0 prefix: no declaration for this component is in the prefix, so the prefix nominated nothing here and the component would otherwise have no P0 pinning the contract named above.

Six descriptors across three providers exercised against a combined configuration, asserting only IsFiltered per case. Measured addsNothingNew over 131 spans; a combination of rules each already pinned individually, and its assertions are weaker (no RuleType), so P2.

Passing the provider allow list does not end evaluation - the global block list is still consulted and wins. Measured addsNothingNew for the same reason as above; it alone catches an early-return after the provider allow list that would let a globally blocked tool through.

Provider block wins over a global allow entry for the same name. Measured addsNothingNew, but coverage cannot see this contract at all: the competing orders execute the same spans and differ only in the returned RuleType. It alone catches a reordering of rule evaluation that leaves a provider-blocked tool exposed.

EnableFiltering false is the explicit kill switch and must produce the same pass-through as no config. Measured addsNothingNew over 39 spans, so not P0; above P2 because it is a separate supported configuration route to that outcome, not a variation of the null-config default.

A provider marked Enabled false filters its functions with RuleType ProviderDisabled and a reason naming the provider. Measured addsNothingNew over 49 spans, so not P0; a distinct primary behavior (whole-provider suppression) rather than a variation of name-based rules.
Empty block and allow lists must not behave like a deny-all allow list. Measured addsNothingNew; an emptiness boundary on the rules already represented.

The complementary half at global scope: a listed function passes with RuleType None. Measured addsNothingNew over 66 spans; kept above P2 for the same reason as the provider-scoped pair - it is the only case that can fail if the allow branch never passes anything.
Global allow list filters anything not listed, with RuleType GlobalAllowList. Measured addsNothingNew over 63 spans; distinct rule family.
The global block list is also matched against the provider-prefixed form of the name. Measured addsNothingNew; an additional pattern form extending the global block contract.
Global block list filters by exact name with RuleType GlobalBlockList and echoes the pattern. Measured addsNothingNew over 65 spans; distinct rule family (global scope) from the provider lists.

With no configuration at all the filter must pass everything through with RuleType None. Measured greedy front (rank 91, +8 spans). Criticality: this is the default every unconfigured host runs under - if it inverted, an unconfigured application would lose all of its tools with a filtering reason it never asked for. Lowered to P1 on the prefix rule: this declaration is outside the project P0 prefix, and the component already has a prefix-nominated P0 in a prefix member confirmed on its own contract. Exclusive spans are a floor rather than a nomination, so the reasoning above stands as the contract while the tier does not.
An empty provider name still falls through to the global block list rather than throwing. Measured addsNothingNew; a robustness boundary.

The complementary half: a function on the provider allow list passes. Measured addsNothingNew over 76 spans; kept above P2 because without it an allow list implementation that filtered everything would still satisfy the FiltersNonMatching case.
A non-empty provider allow list filters anything not on it, with RuleType ProviderAllowList. Measured addsNothingNew over 68 spans; distinct rule family with inverted default, so P1.
The same provider block list with a wildcard pattern. Measured addsNothingNew; wildcard semantics are already pinned by the matcher theory, so this is a variation of the represented rule.
Provider-scoped block list filters an exactly named function and reports the matched pattern. Measured addsNothingNew over 70 spans; distinct rule family, so P1 not P2.
The obsolete boolean-returning overload still filters. Measured addsNothingNew over 66 spans; a back-compatibility shim over the reasoned method already represented.

AddFunction through the builder interface returns the builder stage. Measured greedy front at rank 148 with 3 exclusive spans covering its explicit interface implementation; type-only assertion, so P1 rather than P0.

Calling AddProvider through an IFunctionRegistryBuilder-typed reference returns the providers stage. Not P0 because the assertion is a type check with no behavioural consequence beyond the fluent shape.
Asserts BuildMiddleware returns a non-null middleware carrying the name it was given. Measured addsNothingNew over 190 spans; it proves construction, not any middleware behaviour, so P2.

The whole fluent path end to end: two providers, conflict resolution, a global allow list and a custom prefix, then Build produces exactly the two allowed contracts and the handlers actually execute and return their provider's result. Measured addsNothingNew over 297 spans, so not P0; kept above P2 because it alone proves the built handler dictionary is invocable and keyed by the name filtering left behind - a registry that built contracts without working handlers passes everything else here.
Configure without a filter config still moves the builder to the configured stage. Measured greedy front at rank 143 with 3 exclusive spans over its explicit interface implementation.

Chains logger, explicit function, two providers, conflict resolution and filter config, then asserts Build returns 3 contracts and 3 handlers. Measured addsNothingNew over 165 spans; the composition it demonstrates is asserted more strongly by the complete-workflow test, and its own assertions are counts only.
Three IsType checks that the concrete registry implements all three builder interfaces. Measured addsNothingNew over 3 spans; a compile-time fact restated at runtime, with no behaviour of its own.

Substring checks that the generated markdown contains the heading, the provider name and the function name. Measured addsNothingNew over 134 spans; documentation formatting rather than a registry contract.

Returns both registered provider instances, asserted by identity rather than count alone. Measured greedy front at rank 105 with +6 spans and 3 exclusive spans; a real content assertion, so P1 rather than P2.

A CustomPrefix containing a space, forced past the property setter by reflection, is reported with the provider name and "invalid characters". Measured greedy front at rank 50 with +29 spans and 3 exclusive spans, so it is a strong coverage contributor; kept below P0 because the provider-name case already carries the same consequence into P0 and this one covers the configured-prefix variant of it.

A provider name containing a space, combined with UsePrefixOnlyForCollisions false, is reported as an issue naming the provider and saying it is not a valid prefix. Measured coverage: greedy front at rank 71 with 12 spans no other test reaches - the provider-name validation branch is executed only here. Criticality is independent: with prefix-everything configured, an invalid provider name would be baked into every registered tool name and rejected by the provider rather than caught locally. rationale: A result that arrives already flagged truncated but with no recorded original size keeps OriginalBytes null after a stricter second bound, rather than reporting the post-truncation 512 bytes as if that were the original. It is the honesty half of the re-bound rule: history written before the field existed must not be given a fabricated provenance number that a reader would then trust. P2 rather than P1 because it is the null variation of the axis A_stricter_second_bound_preserves_the_original_count already pins as the representative; that row proves the count is carried, this one proves an unknown count is not invented.

Bounding an already-bounded result to a stricter cap still reports 3,000 - the size of the text the tool actually produced - not the size of the intermediate 512-byte form, while the output honours the new cap. This is the production sequence, not a synthetic one: the executor bounds a result and history ingress may bound it again at a tighter limit, so a naive recompute would rewrite the provenance at every hop and the marker would end up claiming the truncated text was the original. P1: the primary correctness rule for OriginalBytes under the repeated bounding the loop actually performs, and the representative for the second-bound axis.

A persisted server_tool_result document deserializes through IMessageJsonConverter into a ToolCallResultMessage that still reports IsTruncated and OriginalBytes 1000, and re-serializing then re-reading it preserves both. That is the compatibility path for history already on disk: the legacy discriminator is converted into the current message type, and if the truncation metadata were dropped in that conversion an old conversation would reload looking untruncated while its text ends in a truncation marker. P1: the polymorphic read path is where old data actually enters, and it is the representative for the does-the-metadata-survive-JSON axis that OriginalBytes_round_trips_in_result_and_message_json revisits with the plain serializer.

The reported original size is the UTF-8 byte total of every original text field - a 200-snowman result at 600 bytes, a 4-byte emoji block and a 400-byte accented block - and the base64 image block contributes nothing, giving exactly 1,004. The single 1,004 figure is what makes this a real accounting assertion rather than a not-null check: it can only hold if every text field is counted in UTF-8 bytes and no image payload is. Truncation provenance is the only thing telling a reader how much was cut, so a count that silently omitted content blocks or measured UTF-16 chars would understate every multibyte result. P1, and the representative for the OriginalBytes accounting contract that the saturation and re-bound rows vary.

The plain serializer writes the field under the snake_case wire name with value 400 and reads it back on both ToolCallResult and ToolCallResultMessage, and omits it entirely for a small untruncated result. The omission half is the one worth having: an always-present null would add a property to every persisted tool result in history. P2: the same does-the-metadata-survive-JSON axis that Legacy_server_result_truncation_metadata_survives_conversion_and_json_round_trip already pins as the representative through the harder polymorphic path, revisited here with the direct serializer plus the omission case.

A tool-call delta carrying a half-written argument fragment followed by the provider's own finalized ToolCallMessage for the same call id yields exactly ONE tool call, and it is the finalized one - the assertion pins both the single-ness and the completed arguments. This is the tool-call arm of the duplicate-suppression rule the text rows in this class pin: a joiner that also emitted its synthesized copy would put two calls with the same id into history, so the call is executed or replayed twice and the fragment version is not even parseable JSON. P1: a distinct primary contract for this middleware, on the message type where duplication has a side effect rather than only a rendering cost.

Three reasoning deltas - two sharing messageOrderIdx 0 but differing in visibility, then one at idx 1 - join into three separate ReasoningMessages in order, each keeping its own visibility, and every result carries the ThreadId, RunId and ParentRunId it arrived with. The visibility half is the load-bearing one: an encrypted reasoning block is the signature the provider validates on replay, so merging it into the adjacent plain text would corrupt the attestation while looking like an ordinary concatenation. P1: the block-boundary contract for reasoning, which no text-side row can reach.

A thinking delta, an answer delta and a complete text message at successive order indices come out as three distinct text messages in that order, each keeping its own IsThinking flag and messageOrderIdx, and all three keep the thread, run and parent-run identity they arrived with. The tuple comparison is what makes it bite: joining across the thinking boundary would render the model's private reasoning as part of the answer, and losing the order index is what makes the live UI render a second bubble instead of merging. P1, and the representative for the identity-propagation half that the reasoning row asserts identically.

rationale: Fifteen status codes are classified, five server errors and an unrecognised 599 as retryable, and client errors, successes and redirects as not. Measured addsNothingNew over 3 spans. rationale: A fully clean run reports a degraded-verdict count of zero. Catches the new count reading as non-zero on healthy runs. P2: a single-assertion non-vacuity partner for the segmentation test, adding no contract of its own.

rationale: Negative, above-one and NaN floors are each refused at construction. uncertainties: A single assertion on the refusal enum; unlike its rubric-version sibling it does not also check that the deltas are null.

rationale: A candidate scored under a different rubric version is refused with RubricVersionDiffers, is not a regression, has a null delta, and the detail says the comparison can never be drawn. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the rubric version into comparability: the defect it catches is two runs judged by different rubrics being differenced into a number that reads as a candidate change.

rationale: A drop of a sixth on a six-item corpus is past the margin, has an interval upper bound above zero, and is still not declared. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates the two conjuncts of the trigger: it is the only case where the margin is met and the interval is not, so it is what stops the interval being decorative while the margin alone decides on thin corpora.

rationale: One fault in twenty is a fault rate of 0.05 and the comparison is not refused. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the negative control for the fault gate: without it the outage refusal would pass for a comparer that refuses on any fault at all, which would make the whole comparison unusable against normal transport noise.

rationale: Four of twenty items faulted puts coverage exactly on the floor so the floor waves it through, and the comparison still refuses with FaultRateAboveMaximum, carries no triggers and yields a null delta. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the fault-rate refusal as a separate gate from the coverage floor: the defect it catches is an unreachable judge provider being reported as a candidate regression, which is the most consequential wrong answer this component can give.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records, so no provider, network or filesystem dependency

rationale: With the evaluator hash moved and the pass rate falling from nine of ten to three of ten, the comparison refuses, reports no regression and carries no triggers at all. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that a refusal suppresses the trigger set rather than sitting alongside it: the defect it catches is a moved evaluator producing a refusal and a PassRateDrop flag together, which a reader acts on as a candidate regression.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records, so no provider, network or filesystem dependency

rationale: A candidate that decided everything against a baseline half undecided has a no-decision delta of minus one half and does not fire NoDecisionRise. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the direction of the third trigger: the defect it catches is the comparison being written over an absolute value, under which a panel that got materially better at deciding is reported as a regression.

rationale: Half the corpus turning undecided is not refused but fires NoDecisionRise with a delta of one half. Catches a panel that has stopped being able to judge passing as an ordinary run. P1: the third trigger's positive case, distinct from the two score-based ones.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records, so no provider, network or filesystem dependency

rationale: An item that is both undecided and produced by an unavailable panel counts zero in the exclusion-based degraded count, two in the no-decision count and one in the verdict-based degraded count. Catches the segmentation losing the coincident case, so a reader cannot tell the panel disagreeing from the panel being down. P1: it pins a deliberate ordering of exclusion arms plus the second independent count that compensates for it.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records, so no provider, network or filesystem dependency

rationale: One item of movement on a twenty-item corpus does not fire PassRateDrop. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the noise floor: the defect it catches is a detector that reports any negative delta, which would make the report cry wolf on every run until nobody reads it.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records, so no provider, network or filesystem dependency

rationale: On the refusal path the two coverages are still reported distinctly, 0.6 and 1.0. Catches the refusal result being built at a separate site that reads the wrong coverage, which no test on the comparing path can see. rationale: A run scoring five of ten against a floor of 0.8 is refused as CoverageBelowMinimum, reports its coverage as 0.5 and is not a regression. rationale: With eight of twenty faulted the run breaches the fault bound and the coverage floor together, and the single reported refusal names the fault rate. rationale: A run of three undecided items cannot be frozen as a baseline; the refusal names that it scored none. rationale: A seeded drop from ten of twenty to one of twenty fires PassRateDrop with a delta near minus 0.45 and a confidence interval entirely below zero. rationale: Ten items at eight become nine at 8.22 and one at six: the mean is unmoved, P10 falls two points, TailCollapse fires and PassRateDrop does not. requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A run whose fault rate sits exactly on the default bound freezes, with a guard asserting the rate really equals that constant. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the comparison as exclusive: tightened to at-or-above, the single transport failure in twenty that the default is documented to tolerate becomes a run that can never be frozen, so the construction check and the comparison check would disagree about the same run.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A run that scored nothing under a positive floor is refused for the floor, with guards asserting both arms genuinely apply. Redundant by coverage, but it alone distinguishes the last adjacent pair: a run that scored nothing has zero coverage and so breaches every positive floor, and the floor is the fact that generalises, so a reader gets the same detail from freezing that they would get from comparing.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: Coverage exactly at the floor clears it, with a guard asserting the coverage really sits on the floor. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins this comparison as inclusive, the opposite convention from the fault bound directly above it: a run that would compare cleanly against a baseline must be able to become one, and getting the strictness backwards here silently excludes every run that lands exactly on a round floor value.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A run genuinely breaching both the fault bound and the gate bound is refused for the faults, with guards asserting both bounds really break. Redundant by coverage, but it alone distinguishes the ordering of that adjacent pair: a faulted item holds no verdict at all where a gate-impaired item still produced one, so the judge outage is the strictly larger loss, and naming the gate would report the smaller cause for the same run.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A faulted run under a floor it also breaches is refused for the faults. Redundant by coverage, but it alone distinguishes that ordering pair: both other fault tests set a floor their run clears, so a two-position move of the fault check below the coverage check went green across the whole suite. A faulted run is thin by construction — a faulted item yields no score — which makes the floor the check most likely to preempt the fault refusal in practice, and it would report the run as thin without saying a judge outage is why.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A clean run freezes a baseline. Catches the fault check being written to fire on any run. P2: a one-line non-vacuity partner whose claim the boundary and enforced-bound tests both make on stricter inputs.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: The same thin run is accepted under a lenient floor and refused under a strict one, and the accepted baseline carries the floor it was accepted under. Redundant by coverage, but the stored-parameter claim is per bound: deleting it for coverage leaves the fault-bound equivalent green, and a construction check reading a constant instead of this baseline's own floor makes freezing and comparing disagree for every caller who set a non-default floor.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: One impaired run is accepted under a widened fault bound, refused at the default and refused again under a tightened one, and the accepted baseline carries the bound it was accepted under. Redundant by coverage, but it alone ties the construction check to the stored parameter rather than to a second literal that can drift from it: otherwise a caller who widens the bound is refused a baseline its own comparison would accept, and one who tightens it can freeze a source run its own bound would reject.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: With the floor set to zero, so it cannot fire, a run that scored nothing is still refused for scoring nothing. Redundant by coverage, but it alone keeps that arm reachable: with the floor checked first and every other test setting a positive floor, the scored-nothing arm could become dead code and nothing in the suite would say so, leaving a floorless caller able to freeze a baseline over no scores at all.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records

rationale: A one-item corpus whose reference field is crafted to look like a second record does not hash as the honest two-item corpus, and its size is asserted to be one so the forgery is genuinely one item claiming to be two. Redundant by coverage, but it alone closes the record boundary: the unit separator stopped a field forgery and nothing stopped a record forgery, so two different corpora hashed identically and the refusal that keeps a comparison from spanning them never fired. Rejecting newlines is not available here, since task inputs legitimately contain them, so this is the test that pins length-prefixing as the fix.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: Identical items under two corpus ids hash apart. Redundant by coverage, but it alone hashes the corpus identity rather than only its contents: two deliberately separate corpora that happen to hold the same items are different populations, and folding them together lets a baseline frozen over one silently govern comparisons over the other.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: Two items sharing a candidate id are refused, with the id named. Catches a corpus whose per-item results cannot be keyed back to their candidates: the second row either overwrites the first or double-counts it in every rate, and the run completes reporting a size the results do not match. P1: a construction invariant with two exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: An empty corpus is refused at construction. Catches every rate the run reports being computed over a zero denominator, which either throws deep in aggregation or produces a NaN that compares false against every bound and disarms the refusals silently. P1: the empty boundary of the corpus, with two exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: Editing one item of two moves the corpus hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone shows the digest is sensitive to a change in any record rather than only in the sole record: the field table below hashes single-item corpora, so a digest that folded only the first item would satisfy it while letting an edited corpus compare as unchanged against its own baseline.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: Rephrasing the task input moves the hash. Catches that field going unhashed, which would let two corpora posing different questions compare as one. P2: TaskInput is one of the six rows of the per-field table below, which makes the same claim on the same construction.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: A six-row table moves exactly one candidate field per row and asserts the hash moves for each. Redundant by coverage, but it alone isolates the individual appends: three of them can be replaced with an empty string and every other test in this file stays green, and two of the six fields are otherwise never set by any test in the assembly, so without this table they are structurally unexercised while the comparability refusal is built on them.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: Annotating an item with host metadata leaves the hash unchanged. Redundant by coverage, but it alone states the blindness half of the contract: metadata cannot reach a judge or move a score, so hashing it would refuse a comparison between two runs over the identical corpus merely because one carried a pull request id, and the refusal would name an evaluator difference that does not exist.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: A corpus mixing two task types is refused. Catches a corpus whose items are gated and rubric-scored under different rules being averaged into one pass rate, which is a number about no population at all. P1: a construction invariant with two exclusive spans of its own, and gate applicability is scoped by task type, so a mixed corpus silently applies different gates to different rows.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: A three-item snapshot reports a size of three. Catches the size drifting from the item list. P2: a property projection whose value every rate test in the runner exercises through its denominator.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: The same two items supplied in either order hash identically. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the digest as order-insensitive, and row order is not a property of a corpus: a hash that moved with it would refuse comparisons between two runs over the same corpus whenever the source enumerated its rows differently, which is a spurious refusal nobody can diagnose from the refusal itself. No prefix member exists in this file, so P0 is not available.
requirements: in-process only; the snapshot is built from in-test candidates

rationale: A NaN weight is refused the same way, with no judge billed. Redundant by coverage, but it alone catches a range check written as a pair of comparisons: NaN compares false against both bounds, so it passes such a guard and then poisons the weighted mean rather than pushing it off the rubric's scale. The out-of-range case cannot detect that.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A cancellation raised from inside a gate, mid-item, propagates instead of being caught by the per-item fault handler. Catches a swallowed cancellation becoming a Faulted row in a run that then reports aggregates as though it had completed. P1: this is the only path that reaches the runner's cancellation filter, and its three exclusive spans confirm nothing else in the project executes it.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: When one judge faults on one item, that item's verdict is marked SingleJudge, carries the Degraded exclusion and leaves the pass rate at one half. Catches a degraded single-judge row being pooled with full-panel rows, which silently mixes two different measurements. P1: a distinct exclusion class, and its one exclusive span means nothing else in the project reaches it.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A gate-rejected item is a Fail with a null score, carries the GateRejected exclusion, is not scored, and still leaves the pass rate at one half over two items. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the accounting identity for a rejection: a covering run cannot detect a rejected item quietly leaving the denominator, because that changes only a ratio the covering test never computes on this shape.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A gate scoped to a different task type records no decisions and rejects nothing, even though one candidate carries the marker it would reject. Redundant by coverage, but it alone exercises the gate scoping field, which the class doc records every other gate fixture in the assembly left empty. The defect it catches is a scoped gate running anyway and short-circuiting an item into a fail that stays in the denominator.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency
uncertainties: The gate-decision assertion uses OnlyContain, which passes on an empty collection, but the accompanying ScoredItems count of two rules that out.

rationale: The same gate scoped to the corpus's own task type records a decision on every candidate and its rejection lands, halving the pass rate. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the positive half of the scoping pair: without it the negative case would pass for a gate that never runs at all, so it is what makes the scoping field behaviourally pinned rather than merely present.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Two runs over one corpus with a scripted panel agree on both hashes and on pass rate, mean and P10, and the baseline comparison then reports no refusal, no regression and three zero deltas. Catches any nondeterminism in the pipeline, which would make every regression this system reports unfalsifiable.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Running a rubric whose task type differs from the configuration throws an ArgumentException naming the task type. Catches a corpus scored against a rubric written for different work, which produces numbers that look ordinary and mean nothing. P1: a distinct configuration guard whose two exclusive spans are reached by no other test in the project.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A run that scored nothing, compared against a baseline whose minimum coverage is zero, is refused as CoverageBelowMinimum with a detail naming the empty result rather than dereferencing a null mean. Catches a crash path, not only an unpinned number, and the test first asserts the two evaluator hashes match so the refusal cannot be coming from a config difference. P1: two exclusive spans confirm no other test in the project reaches it.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: An item the arbiter resolved into a Pass is still counted as a straddle, and the resolved and unresolved straddle counters split one and zero. Catches the straddle rate being computed from outcomes rather than from disagreement, which would hide judge unreliability exactly when the arbiter is masking it. Prefix candidate at greedyRank 11 dropped to P1: it is one rule inside the straddle metric rather than the runner's component baseline, which is the denominator contract.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Two judges scoring ten and two under weights of one and a quarter produce 8.4 rather than the unweighted 6.0. Catches the reliability map being accepted and never handed to the reduction, which every other test in this class would miss because they all pass an empty map that travels at the 1.0 default. P1: the non-vacuity proof for the whole weighting parameter.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: An item whose generator family is null passes but carries the UnknownGeneratorFamily exclusion and is kept out of the scored pool. Catches unknown being treated as not-a-match, which would pool a row the exclusion filter never actually ran on with rows that were checked. P1: a distinct exclusion class with three exclusive spans, so nothing else in the project exercises it.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A weight above one throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException named for the reliability parameter, and no judge sees any candidate. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins where the check belongs: the specific defect it catches is the gauntlet's own check firing per item so a caller error is recorded as an unscoreable corpus, telling the operator their data is bad when their configuration was rejected.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: With no arbiter, a disputed item is a Split carrying the Straddled exclusion, nothing is scored and the mean is null rather than zero. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the unresolved arm: the specific defect it catches is a split reported as a zero-scored item, which would pull a mean down instead of declining to state one.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency
uncertainties: StraddleCount is asserted as 2 over a two-item corpus in which only one item is described as disputed, so the second judge pair is evidently straddling the agreed item too; the number is pinned but the scenario reads as narrower than it is.

rationale: A token cancelled before the run causes the run to throw rather than returning a run full of faulted items. Catches a swallowed cancellation producing aggregates over work nobody completed. P2: the sibling test's own doc records that this case is stopped by the loop's pre-item check and never reaches the runner's cancellation filter, so it would pass with that filter inverted or deleted.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: With no cost source the item's cost is null. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the absent-versus-zero distinction: the specific defect it catches is a null-coalescing default of zero, under which an unpriced run reports as free and every other cost test in this class, all of which supply a source, stays green.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Two items priced differently total to their sum and average to their mean. Catches cost being dropped or double counted. P2: the accounting claim here is subsumed by the mean-cost test, which uses a corpus where the per-corpus and per-scored denominators actually differ; this one cannot separate them.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Over four items where one is gate-rejected and one abstains, coverage and pass rate are both one half rather than two over two. Catches every rate being divided by the processed subset, which flatters a run precisely when it declined the hard items. P1: the class documents the denominator as the runner's central contract, and this is the widest statement of it, but it is outside the measured prefix so it is not nominated for P0.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Four items priced at a hundred each, one abstaining, total four hundred and average one hundred rather than a hundred and thirty three. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates the two cost denominators: every other cost test scores everything it prices, so the division could be swapped there with nothing going red, and the defect this catches is abstention making a run look cheaper per item.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Two runs differing only in a gate's maximum length, with both bounds admitting every item so the rate and the rejection count are identical, still refuse to compare with EvaluatorConfigDiffers. Catches gates dropping out of the evaluator hash, after which retuning a bound silently moves a reported rate with nothing about the candidate having changed.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A gate that throws leaves its item scored with no exclusion and records a single Inconclusive gate decision, and the run faults nothing. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins where a gate fault is absorbed: the specific defect it catches is the candidate being lost entirely, leaving the numerator while staying in the denominator, which reads as an unmeasurable item rather than an unavailable gate.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A reducer that throws on one item faults only that item, which keeps its place in the denominator, while the items before and after it are still evaluated and scored. Catches one bad corpus row destroying a whole run's work, and the after-item assertion is what distinguishes isolation from a short-circuit. P1: the runner's fault-isolation contract, with five exclusive spans reached by nothing else.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Over ten scored items the tenth percentile is the lowest value, matching nearest rank at ceil(0.1*10)-1, with the mean asserted alongside so a constant would not satisfy both. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the percentile definition: an interpolating or off-by-one percentile is invisible to every other test here, all of which read mean and pass rate only.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency
uncertainties: Ten equal-spaced scores put nearest rank and several interpolation rules close together; the case pins the index but is not chosen to separate every percentile convention.

rationale: One judge's model id changes while the corpus, rubric and resulting pass rate stay identical, and the comparison refuses with EvaluatorConfigDiffers and a null delta.
