Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the model id into the evaluator hash: the defect it catches is a comparison drawn across a swapped judge model, and the unchanged scores are what show the refusal is not merely a reaction to a moved number.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: The run's corpus hash, evaluator hash, rubric version and task type each equal the value on the input it ran against. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins provenance at the source: the specific defect it catches is a run recording a hash from somewhere other than the objects it executed, which every comparison refusal downstream would then evaluate against the wrong fact while still looking correct.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Four items with one straddle and one abstention give a straddle rate of a quarter, not a half. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates the straddle denominators: a straddle is itself excluded from the scored set so the two can never agree on a corpus containing one, and every other test here reads the count rather than the rate.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: Two judges on the same side of the line produce the Consensus tie-break rule, a scored item, a zero straddle count and the mean of the two scores. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the positive control for the straddle family: without it every straddle assertion in this class would pass for a runner that marked every item a straddle.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A run whose reliability weights differ from the frozen configuration's throws naming the freeze, and no judge is billed on the way to finding out. Catches a hash that describes a configuration other than the one executing, under which every refusal built on it checks the wrong fact. Prefix candidate at greedyRank 9 dropped to P1: this is important failure handling protecting the hash contract, while the hash baseline itself is pinned separately and the two comparison refusals hold P0 on that path; promoting it would stack a third P0 on the same evaluator-identity path.
requirements: in-process only; judges are scripted delegates, so no provider, network or transport dependency

rationale: A fingerprint carrying a newline or a unit separator is refused. The guard is invoked per field, so deleting the fingerprint call site leaves the judge-id test green: this is a distinct call site, not a second input to a shared one. P1 rather than P2 for that reason, and because the fingerprint is the host-supplied field of the two, so it is the one an untrusted value most plausibly reaches.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A gate not implementing the fingerprint interface is refused by name at construction. Catches an undescribable gate being hashed under a constant, after which retuning that gate is invisible to every comparability check downstream. P1: refusal at the freeze point, with two exclusive spans reached by no other test.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A judge on the default renderer builds without a declared template hash. Catches the refusal being written universally, which would make every ordinary judge unconstructable. P1: the non-vacuity partner to the custom-renderer refusal, with one exclusive span of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A judge declaring no transport fingerprint is refused rather than hashed under a constant. Redundant by coverage, but it alone forces the transport to be declared at all: without the refusal the transport field is optional in practice, and the sensitivity its sibling proves applies only to callers who happened to fill it in.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Two judges with the same custom renderer but different declared template hashes build successfully and hash apart. Confirmed against its contract: it is the only test closing the loop on the declared-fingerprint escape hatch, proving both that a declaring judge is accepted and that the declared value actually enters the digest. A declaration accepted but not hashed is worse than a refusal, because two different prompt templates then pass comparability as the same evaluator and a prompt change reads as a candidate movement.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A judge handed an opaque host-supplied renderer with no declared template hash is refused. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the refusal on the judge side: such a judge genuinely does not know which bytes it will send, and substituting a constant hashes two entirely different prompts identically, which is the strongest form of the forgery this component exists to prevent.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A task type containing the comma that joins the list is refused, and the honest pair on either side of the collision still hashes apart. Catches the field guard covering the newline and unit separator but not the delimiter one level down, which let a gate scoped to the single type a,b render the same bytes as one scoped to a and b. P1: a forgery case that carries its own non-vacuity pair, proving the ambiguity being closed was real.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A weight of 1.5 is refused where the configuration is frozen rather than at scoring time. Catches the validation living only on the per-item path, where a misfitted refit surfaces as a corpus that scored nothing instead of as a configuration that was wrong. P1: it pins where the check runs, which no assertion on the aggregator's own range rejection can establish.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Adding an arbiter to the options moves the hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the arbiter's absence as a hashed fact rather than a nothing: whether an arbiter exists changes how every straddle in the corpus resolves, so a hash that only records an arbiter it has calls the escalating run and the non-escalating run the same evaluator.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: An arbiter carrying a panel judge's id is refused at construction. Redundant by coverage, but it alone guards the identity the reduction partitions on: a shared id makes a genuine straddle record as a consensus, which silently suppresses the straddle rate the runner reports as its headline judge-reliability diagnostic, and no assertion downstream can recover the distinction.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A judge id carrying a newline or a unit separator is refused. Redundant by coverage, but it alone guards the id field against forging a record or field boundary in a newline-delimited digest that escapes nothing, which lets two different configurations hash the same and defeats the refusal outright. Both delimiters are covered, so a guard written for only one is caught.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Two identically-built configurations produce the same hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone establishes determinism, and every other test in this file asserts only that two hashes differ — all of which would pass against a hash that was random per call. Without it the whole comparability suite is vacuous.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Moving only the abstain floor moves the hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that field, and the floor decides which ballots are counted at all, so retuning it moves scores and outcomes across the corpus while the candidate side is untouched.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Moving only the dispersion alarm moves the hash. Catches that append being dropped. P2 rather than P1: unlike the abstain floor and the arbiter, the alarm changes only the review flag and moves no score or outcome, so a hash blind to it makes two runs comparable that genuinely are comparable on every scored field.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Two configurations differing only in a judge's prompt fingerprint hash apart. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that field: a reworded rubric prompt moves scores across the whole corpus while every identity in the run stays fixed, which is exactly the change a comparability check must refuse rather than score.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A different reliability snapshot id moves the hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the declared snapshot identity, and a refit alone changes every weighted score in the corpus with nothing on the candidate side moving — the exact confusion the comparability refusal exists to prevent.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: The same two human signal sources declared in the opposite order hash identically. Catches the field being hashed order-sensitively. P2 rather than P1: the source list is caller-supplied and stable within a caller, and over-sensitivity here produces a loud spurious refusal rather than a silent wrong comparison — unlike the weights ordering case, where the collection is a dictionary whose enumeration order can differ between processes.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: A four-row table moving exactly one hashed field per row — gate scoping, judge family, arbiter model and arbiter family — with every other field held fixed. Redundant by coverage, but it alone isolates those four appends: each can be replaced with an empty string and the rest of the suite stays green, because the wholesale swap tests vary more than one field at a time. P1: the field-level completeness claim the comparability refusal rests on.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Retuning one gate's maximum length while holding everything else fixed moves the hash. Redundant by coverage, but it alone covers the headline case the hash exists for: the same corpus, rubric and candidate output with one bound retuned moves the reported pass rate with nothing on the candidate having changed, and a hash blind to it lets the comparison read that as a candidate regression.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Two different weightings declared under the same snapshot id hash apart. Redundant by coverage, but it alone closes the gap the snapshot id left: a caller who refits and reuses an id such as latest, or one derived from a date that has not rolled, hashed two materially different weightings identically, and the one refusal that stops a refit reading as a candidate regression never fired.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: The same two gates in the opposite order hash differently. Catches the gate list being hashed as an unordered set: gates short-circuit, so the same set in a different order rejects on a different gate and records a different reason, and the two runs are not comparable. P1: order sensitivity for the gate list, with one exclusive span reached by no other test.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Two configurations differing only in a judge's model id hash apart. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that field: the model behind a judge is the single largest determinant of the ballots it casts, and this append can be deleted with the rest of the suite staying green, since no other test varies the model id alone.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: The same two weights inserted in the opposite order hash identically. Catches the weights being digested in dictionary enumeration order, which is not guaranteed stable between processes: the same configuration would then hash differently on different runs and comparability would refuse at random, a failure whose cause is nearly impossible to read from the refusal itself.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: The gauntlet built from the configuration runs the judge that was declared, and that judge saw the candidate. Redundant by coverage, but it alone ties the digest to the object actually executed: every other test here compares hashes to hashes, so a builder that hashed one configuration and constructed another would leave the entire file green while the recorded evaluator identity described a run that never happened.
requirements: in-process only; the gauntlet runs an in-test scoring judge

rationale: Two judges differing only in their transport fingerprint hash apart. Redundant by coverage, but it alone reaches the transport: it is an opaque delegate holding no field the judge could report, so two judges at different temperatures, different sampling settings or different deployments behind one model id used to fingerprint identically while producing different ballots.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Adding a second human signal source moves the hash. Catches that field going unhashed, which would let a run drawing on more human signal compare directly against one drawing on less. P1: a hashed field with its own append that no other test varies.
requirements: in-process only; the configuration is built from in-test fakes and hashed synchronously

rationale: Freezing a baseline from an outage run is refused, and the refusal names the broken gate. Redundant by coverage, but it alone protects the baseline side: the comparison refusal guards only the candidate, and an outage run scores everything, so it walked through the scored-nothing check and froze a pass rate measured with the gates off as the bar every later run is judged against. A poisoned baseline distorts every comparison after it and is refused by nothing.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run where every gate went inconclusive shows a flat pass rate, full coverage and a zero fault rate, and is refused by name rather than compared, with no regression trigger and a null delta. Catches the central defect of this family: with the deterministic layer off for a whole run, every existing aggregate looks pristine and the comparison reports no regression. Highest greedy rank in this file at 17 with 8 marginal spans, but outside the measured prefix, so P0 is unavailable — recorded as a rubric-displaced P0 candidate.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A source run that both breached the gate bound and scored nothing is refused for the outage, with guards asserting both conditions genuinely hold. Redundant by coverage, but it alone supplies the input that distinguishes the two orderings at construction, mirroring the comparer: without it a reader freezing a baseline is told the run scored nothing about a run whose gates were the reason, and freezing and comparing name different causes for the same run.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run that recorded no gate decision still mints a baseline. Redundant by coverage, but it alone applies the null sentinel at the construction call site: the comparison-side sentinel test cannot reach it, and a refusal here would mean a gateless harness could never freeze a baseline at all, turning a safety check into a hard block on a legitimate configuration.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run whose rate sits exactly on the default bound still freezes, with a guard asserting the rate really equals that constant. Redundant by coverage, but it alone sits on the construction-side boundary: tightening the check to at-or-above would make the very run the comparer insists on comparing impossible to freeze, so the two predicates would silently disagree about the same run.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run breaching both the fault bound and the gate bound is refused for the fault. Redundant by coverage, but it alone supplies an input that can tell the two orderings apart, and ordering is the whole of the behaviour: a faulted item holds no verdict at all where a gate-impaired item still produced one, so naming the gate would report the smaller loss as the cause.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run genuinely under the coverage floor and over the gate bound, with no faults to preempt, is refused for the gate bound. Redundant by coverage, but it alone constructs the input that distinguishes the two orderings — a pure gate outage leaves coverage at 1.0, so the floor never fires whichever way the checks sit. The floor names only the symptom, equally true of a hard corpus; the gate bound names the cause a reader can act on.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run that recorded no gate decision reports a null rate, an empty id list, and is still compared rather than refused. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the sentinel: a rate of zero on a run where no gate ever ran reads to a skimmer as the gates checked this and it was clean, silently widening unknown into fine. The paired non-refusal is what keeps the sentinel from making a gateless harness uncomparable.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A run whose gates all concluded reports exactly 0.0. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the case the null sentinel must stay distinguishable from: an implementation returning null whenever the count is zero satisfies every other test here while erasing the difference between the gates ran and found nothing and no gate ran at all, which is the whole content of the sentinel.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A healthy gated run freezes a baseline. Catches the construction refusal being written to fire on any recorded gate decision. P2: a one-line non-vacuity partner whose claim the boundary and enforced-bound tests both make on stricter inputs.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: Two runs of the same configuration, one with the checkout present and one without, are driven through the real runner; the outage scores every item cleanly and the comparison against the healthy baseline refuses by name. Redundant by coverage, but it alone joins containment, aggregation and refusal end to end through the runner rather than through hand-built records, and it asserts both identity hashes match so no other refusal is reachable — which is what makes the gate signal demonstrably the thing doing the work.
requirements: in-process only; the runner drives in-test gates and judges with no network

rationale: Impaired rows are counted across the scored, undecided and undecided-and-degraded arms, with a guard asserting two rows genuinely matched a non-None arm. Redundant by coverage, but it alone reaches rows whose exclusion is not None: every other test here scores its items, so a count that also read the exclusion would stay green while a compound failure — gates down and the panel undecided, which is what a bad deploy actually produces — vanished from the outage signal precisely when it coincided with another one.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: One inconclusive gate in twenty items is compared, not refused. Redundant by coverage, but it alone bounds the refusal from the other side: an occasional transport failure is normal, and a bound that fired on it would refuse ordinary runs and make the whole comparison unusable, which is the failure mode that gets a safety check disabled rather than fixed.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: One impaired run is accepted under a widened bound, refused at the default, and refused again under a tightened one. Redundant by coverage, but it alone ties the construction check to the bound this baseline will impose rather than to the constant default: otherwise a caller who deliberately widens the bound is refused a baseline its own comparison would have accepted, and one who tightens it can freeze a source run its own bound would reject.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: NaN, a negative and an above-one bound are refused both through the factory and through a with expression. Redundant by coverage, but it alone closes the record-rewrite path: a record built by a validating factory is still rewritable, and NaN is the reachable value that does the most damage because every comparison against it is false, leaving the refusal permanently disarmed with no output anywhere to notice.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: Under a 0.9 coverage floor, a pure gate outage still leaves coverage at 1.0 and is refused for the gate bound. Catches an argument that the coverage floor makes the gate bound redundant. P2: both of its assertions are already made on the same construction by the headline refusal test, which asserts coverage 1.0 and the same refusal; the only thing this adds is a stricter floor setting that the outage still does not trip.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: Three inconclusive gates on one item count as one impaired item, and the rate over a two-item run is 0.5. Redundant by coverage, but it alone fixes the unit of the count: counting gate executions makes the numerator exceed the corpus size and the rate exceed one, which puts the signal on a different scale from the fault count it is meant to be read beside and breaks any bound expressed as a fraction. No prefix member exists in this file, so P0 is not available.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: The same run is refused against a strict baseline and compared against a lenient one. Redundant by coverage, but it alone proves the bound is read from the baseline rather than from the run or a constant: a run that could relax the bar it is judged against defeats the refusal entirely, which is the reason the coverage floor and fault bound live there too.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A gate impaired on two items is named once, and both impaired gates appear in first-seen order. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the identity list: the environmental faults this signal exists to catch — a missing checkout, a wrong path template, an undeployed schema — are each identified by which gate stopped working, and a detail saying only that some gates were inconclusive leaves nothing to act on.
requirements: in-process only; runs are hand-built records and the comparer is pure

rationale: A declared task-type list is carried on the gate. Catches the constructor argument being dropped. P2: property plumbing, with the behaviour it feeds asserted at the gauntlet.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: All three starter gates default to an empty task-type list, the encoding for applies to everything. Catches a default that scopes a gate to nothing and silently disables it. P2: a default-value claim on a property whose behaviour is asserted by the gauntlet's own scoping tests.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A well-formed JSON object passes the default gate. Redundant by coverage, but it alone keeps the not-json rejection from being universal: with no pass case a gate rejecting every candidate satisfies its sibling, and a structured-output corpus would score nothing with the gate reported as working.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Content carrying both declared properties passes. Redundant by coverage, but it alone keeps the required-property check from being written as a blanket rejection: without it the rejection test passes against a gate that refuses every candidate the moment any property is declared, which silently empties the corpus for exactly the tasks that configured a schema.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Content that parses as JSON but omits a declared required property is rejected, with the missing property named in the reason. Confirmed against its contract: the required-property check is the substantive half of this gate — without it JsonSchemaGate degrades to a parse check, and structurally incomplete candidates reach the paid judges and get scored, defeating the reason gates run before any model at all. It is the only test reaching that path, and the reason assertion is what lets an operator see which property was missing.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Markdown prose is rejected by the schema gate. Catches the gate treating unparseable content as acceptable, which is the base case for a task declaring structured output. P1: the parse-failure arm, holding three exclusive spans reached by no other test in the project.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A rejection reason built from a candidate carrying a secret-shaped token does not contain that token. Redundant by coverage, but it alone guards this gate's reason writer, and the reason reaches persistence: quoting the candidate copies whatever the candidate held into the stored record, which is the one place a gate can leak content it was only meant to measure.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model
uncertainties: Asserts the absence of one literal token in one reason string. It does not establish that the reason is built from lengths alone; a reason that quoted a different part of the candidate would pass.

rationale: Candidates at exactly the minimum and exactly the maximum both pass. Redundant by coverage, but it alone sits on both boundaries and is the only pass case for this gate: without it the two rejection tests are satisfied by a gate that rejects everything, and an exclusive comparison at either edge would silently discard candidates that are precisely at the configured limit.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A minimum above the maximum is refused at construction. Catches an unsatisfiable band being accepted and rejecting the entire corpus. P2: a construction-time argument guard whose failure mode is loud and immediate rather than a silently wrong score.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A candidate one character over the band is rejected and the reason carries both the actual length and the bound. Redundant by coverage, but it alone covers the control the gate exists for: a repetitive-list attack fooled two of three frontier judges most of the time, and the length band settles that shape without asking a model anything. The reason assertion is what makes the rejection diagnosable rather than an unexplained drop.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A candidate under the minimum is rejected. Catches a band implemented as an upper bound only. P2: the mirror arm of the rejection its sibling establishes, asserting outcome alone with no reason claim.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: With a minimum of two, one citation is rejected and two pass. Catches the minimum being ignored and treated as one. P2: parameterisation of the threshold the single-citation cases already establish.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Two paths differing only in case count as two citations. Redundant by coverage, but it alone fixes distinctness as ordinal: a case-insensitive comparison collapses them, which both mis-scores a case-sensitive filesystem where they are genuinely different files and reopens the repetition attack to anyone who re-cases the same path.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: One citation repeated three times does not satisfy a minimum of three. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates occurrences from distinct citations, and the parameter is documented as distinct citations: counting occurrences credits precisely the repetitive-list shape the anti-verbosity rule exists to refuse, so the gate would reward the attack it was built to stop.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: This gate's rejection reason does not contain a secret-shaped token from the candidate. Redundant by coverage, but redaction is a property of each reason writer, not of the gate interface: deleting this gate's redaction leaves the LengthBounds equivalent green, and this is the gate most tempted to quote the candidate, since its rejection is about what the text did not contain.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model
uncertainties: Asserts the absence of one literal token in one reason string; a reason quoting a different part of the candidate would pass.

rationale: Prose citing a path and a line number passes. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the accept case for this gate: the three rejection tests are all satisfied by a gate that credits nothing, which would reject every review in the corpus while reporting a working citation requirement.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A file path mentioned with no line number is rejected. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the anchor as path and line together: a pattern matching bare paths would credit any prose that happens to name a file, which is most review prose, and the gate would then pass essentially everything while still failing the no-citation test.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Confident prose citing nothing is rejected. Redundant by coverage, but it alone states the gate's core claim, the shallow structural half of the per-finding citation check: an uncited review is the shape a verbose judge rewards and the shape this gate exists to stop before a model is ever asked.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: Two different lines in one file, with one of them repeated, satisfy a minimum of two. Catches distinctness being taken per file rather than per citation, which would refuse an honest review that cites several problems in the same file — the common case for a focused review. P1: the non-vacuity partner that stops the repetition rule from being satisfied by a gate that credits nothing repeated at all.
requirements: in-process only; gates are deterministic and call no model

rationale: A cancellation raised from inside a real judge's transport delegate propagates instead of being caught as a judge fault. Catches the per-judge fault handler swallowing a caller's cancellation, which would turn a deliberately stopped run into a PanelUnavailable verdict. P1: the only path through that catch, confirmed by three exclusive spans reached by nothing else in the project.
requirements: in-process only; the judge's transport is an injected delegate, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A cancellation raised inside a gate propagates instead of being absorbed as an inconclusive decision. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates cancellation from gate failure at the gate stage: the defect it catches is the fault containment swallowing a caller's cancellation, which puts a gate record on a run nobody tried to complete and leaves aggregates over it looking finished.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A judge fault whose message contains a hostname and a token records the exception type and neither of those strings. Redundant by coverage, but it alone holds the degradation reason to the persisted-field rail: the defect it catches is a provider exception message, which routinely carries a URL and credentials, being written into a stored diagnostic.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency
the secret-shaped strings are literals defined in the test itself; no credential or environment value is read

rationale: A gate scoped to another task type is never called, records no decision, and the judge still runs. Catches a scoped gate rejecting candidates it was never meant to see. P2: the gate scoping contract is pinned as a distinguishing pair in EvalRunnerTests; this is the same rule observed at the gauntlet level.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A gate that throws is recorded as an Inconclusive decision naming the exception type, the gate after it still runs, the judge is still called and the verdict is a Pass. Catches the gate stage losing the candidate entirely when a real gate fails by throwing, which is how a missing tool or an absent checkout actually surfaces.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A negative abstain floor is refused at construction. Catches a floor no confidence can fall below, which silently disables the abstention filter. P2: the second arm of the same range check its percentage sibling covers, with no distinct mechanism behind it.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A negative dispersion alarm is refused at construction. Catches an alarm compared against a population standard deviation, which is never negative, so it would fire on every verdict that has one and make the diagnostic meaningless. P1: a distinct option's validation, with two exclusive spans reached by nothing else in the project.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A single-judge configuration constructs without throwing. Catches the family and count validations being widened until the deliberately supported single-judge shape is rejected. P2: a one-line non-vacuity partner for the configuration refusals, adding no contract of its own.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: Running a candidate whose task type differs from the rubric's throws naming the task type. Catches a candidate graded against criteria written for other work, which produces a score that looks ordinary and means nothing. P1: a distinct precondition at the gauntlet boundary, with two exclusive spans no other test reaches.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: With one judge and an arbiter configured, the arbiter is never called, the verdict is SingleJudge with a null dispersion and the judge's score stands. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the deployed single-judge shape: the defect it catches is escalation firing where no straddle is possible, which bills an arbiter call on every item of a corpus for a disagreement that cannot exist.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A Split produced by a degraded single-judge panel, injected through a stub reducer, makes no arbiter call. Redundant by coverage, but it alone reaches this guard: the production reducer never emits that state, so the injected seam is the only way to exercise it, and the defect it catches is an arbiter breaking a tie that was never fully cast because one voice was missing.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A straddle whose configured arbiter shares the generator's family makes zero arbiter calls, stays an unresolved Split and is marked None rather than unavailable. Redundant by coverage, but it alone breaks if escalation checks configuration alone: the arbiter here is configured, so a condition that only asks whether one exists would call it, and the defect that hides is the generator's own family being handed the deciding vote on its output.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A straddle with no arbiter configured is an unresolved Split carrying no degradation. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the other half of the escalation discriminator: without it the ArbiterUnavailable tests would pass for an implementation that marks every unresolved split as a failed escalation, erasing the distinction between choosing not to escalate and trying and failing.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: The recorded reason for a thrown gate does not contain the exception's message text. Redundant by coverage, but it alone holds the gate diagnostic to the persisted-field rail: the defect it catches is an exception message reaching storage, where it can carry a URL, a token or an excerpt of the candidate, and the containment test that produces the same record asserts only that the reason names the type.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency
uncertainties: The assertion is a single NotContain on one literal message, so it detects that specific leak rather than proving the reason is built from the type alone.

rationale: Two judges from one model family are refused at construction, with the message naming the family. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins panel independence: the defect it catches is a panel of two judges from one family, whose correlated errors look like agreement, so every consensus and every straddle rate it produces overstates how much independent evidence there is.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An empty judge list is refused at construction. Catches a gauntlet that evaluates nothing while reporting verdicts. P2: a degenerate-input boundary over the configuration validation the family and id checks carry.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An abstain floor of 34, the percentage spelling of 0.34, is refused at construction with a message naming confidence. Catches a floor above every possible confidence, under which every ballot is excluded, every candidate becomes NoDecision with a null score, and a whole corpus run produces nothing while reporting success. P1: important failure handling on the one option whose misreading is silent across an entire run.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An arbiter whose confidence falls below the floor is also marked ArbiterUnavailable, with the reason naming the floor. Catches the below-floor exclusion channel not counting as unavailable. P2: a third input reaching a marking already pinned by the abstention and fault cases.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An arbiter whose judge id matches a panel judge's is refused at construction. Catches the reduction partitioning ballots by id alone, under which that panel judge's ballot reads as the arbiter's, the panel is left with one ballot that can never straddle, and a genuine nine-versus-three disagreement records as a consensus while the straddle rate reads silently low. P1: a distinct identity invariant guarding the headline diagnostic.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An arbiter that ran and abstained is called once, leaves a Split, and is marked ArbiterUnavailable with a reason naming the abstention. Catches an escalation that happened and failed being recorded as None, which is the marking reserved for deciding not to escalate at all, making the two indistinguishable in the persisted record. P1: it pins the discriminator between attempted and not-attempted escalation.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: An inconclusive gate still calls the judge and its decision is carried into the verdict. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates Inconclusive from Reject: the defect it catches is an infrastructure failure short-circuiting into a Fail, or being dropped entirely so the verdict reads as a clean bill of health the gate never actually gave.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A straddle whose arbiter faults still calls the arbiter once, ends as a Split, and is marked ArbiterUnavailable. Catches an attempted escalation that failed being recorded as one that was never attempted, which is the persisted discriminator a reader needs to tell an unreliable panel from an unreachable arbiter.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: When every judge faults the verdict is NoDecision marked PanelUnavailable. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the total-outage arm: the defect it catches is an empty ballot set reducing to a default outcome, and a Pass on a candidate no judge ever saw is the worst wrong answer this component can produce.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A token cancelled before the run causes the gauntlet to throw rather than returning a PanelUnavailable verdict. Catches a caller's cancellation being recorded as a provider outage. P2: the sibling test's own doc records that this case is settled by the entry check and never enters a judge, so the cancellation catch it is named for is not reached here.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: When the generator's own family is excluded the remaining judge runs, the excluded one is never called, and the verdict degrades to SingleJudge at the surviving score. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the self-grading exclusion at the point it costs something: the defect it catches is the harness either admitting a judge from the generator's family, which is a model grading itself, or throwing rather than degrading and losing the item.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: When the only judge shares the generator's family it is never called and the verdict is NoDecision marked PanelUnavailable. Catches the exclusion being abandoned when it would empty the panel, which is exactly when self-grading would otherwise slip through. P1: a distinct eligibility outcome, with four exclusive spans no other test in the project reaches.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: With one judge returning and one faulting the verdict is marked SingleJudge, its dispersion is null rather than zero, it still passes at the surviving score, and the reason names the unreachable family. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the null dispersion: a zero would read as a panel in perfect agreement, which is the opposite of what a lone judge means, and no other test in the class asserts that field.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: A straddle calls the arbiter exactly once, the arbiter's own score becomes the verdict rather than being blended, the tie-break names the arbiter and family, and three ballots are recorded. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the escalation's arithmetic and its call count together: the defect it catches is a second reduction re-entering escalation, or an arbiter score averaged into the panel's, which would leave the arbiter unable to overturn a disagreement it was called to settle.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: Two judges on the same side of the threshold produce a consensus Pass with the arbiter's call count at zero. Redundant by coverage, but it alone carries the cost claim for the common case: the defect it catches is escalation on any score difference rather than on a straddle, which bills a third model call on most of a corpus, and only the zero counter can see it.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: Floors of exactly zero and exactly one both construct. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the range as inclusive at both ends: without it the two refusal tests would pass for a validator that rejects every floor, which would make the option unusable, and an exclusive bound would refuse the two configurations that mean never abstain and always abstain.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: The candidate's reference answer arrives at the judge unchanged. Redundant by coverage, but it alone proves reference-guided grading is actually happening: the defect it catches is a reference accepted and dropped before the judge sees it, after which every score is computed without the accepted answer and looks entirely ordinary. No other test in the class sets or reads that field.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: The first rejecting gate leaves the judge's call count at zero and the later gate's at zero, and the verdict is a Fail with a null score, no ballots, two gate decisions and the gate-reject tie-break. Redundant by coverage, but it alone carries the cost claim: the Fail outcome by itself would also be produced by a panel that ran and spent tokens, and only the zero counters distinguish the two.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: Two panel judges sharing an id are refused at construction. Catches the same id-as-identity assumption breaking inside the panel, which makes every reliability weight, every exclusion record and every arbiter partition ambiguous. P1: the panel-side arm of the identity invariant, with two exclusive spans reached by nothing else.
requirements: in-process only; judges and gates are fakes, so no provider or network dependency

rationale: Families differing only in case still collide. Redundant by coverage, but it alone fixes the comparison as case-insensitive on the throwing path: with an ordinal comparison a caller who writes one family capitalised gets a panel of two same-vendor judges that reports as independent, and nothing downstream can tell it from a genuinely disjoint panel.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: One judge and a candidate whose generator family is unknown composes to Degraded. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that a null family skips the exclusion step and not the classification step, and it is the exact shape the daemon adapter produces: shortcutting on a null family reports a single-judge panel as Full, so every candidate of unknown provenance records one opinion as a full panel decision.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: Two judges and an unknown generator family compose to Full. Catches a null family being matched against a judge and dropping one. P2: the benign arm of the null case, reaching the same Full classification the disjoint-families test establishes with the null as its only new input.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: One configured judge composes to Degraded rather than throwing. Redundant by coverage, but it alone establishes that a single-judge harness is a legal configuration classified honestly: refusing it would block a real deployment, and classifying it Full would report one judge's opinion as a panel decision.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: Neither judge is called during composition. Redundant by coverage, but it alone asserts composition is free: every other test here reads the returned classification and none would notice a Compose that probed the judges first, which would spend a model call per candidate on judges it is about to exclude and turn a pure configuration decision into a network-dependent one.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: One judge sharing the generator's family composes to Unavailable. Redundant by coverage, but it alone reaches the third classification: without it the exclusion could silently keep the ineligible judge rather than admit the panel is empty, which is precisely the self-judging case, and it is the state the reduction needs in order to record a panel outage instead of a decision.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: A candidate whose generator shares a judge's family drops that judge, keeps the other, and names the excluded family in the reason without throwing. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates the two rules this component deliberately keeps apart: eligibility is a property of the candidate and varies run to run, so throwing here would fail every candidate a configured judge happens to have generated, while the self-judging it prevents is the strongest bias in the whole harness.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: A generator family in a different case is still excluded. Catches an ordinal comparison on the filtering path, which would let a model judge its own output. P2: a case variation of the exclusion its sibling establishes, on the same two-judge construction.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: Three judges of disjoint families still throw. Catches the panel size being unbounded above. P2: the upper boundary of the same configuration guard, asserting the exception type only.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: Two judges of different families with no generator exclusion compose to Full. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the healthy accept case for composition: every throwing test here is satisfied by a Compose that refuses everything, and every degradation test by one that never returns Full, so without it the classification could never report a complete panel.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: Two judges of the same model family throw at composition with a message naming the collision. Catches a panel of two judges that are not independent: same-family models share training and failure modes, so their agreement is not evidence and the consensus outcome the reduction reports is worth less than it appears. P1: the configuration rule of panel composition, with one exclusive span of its own. No prefix member exists in this file, so P0 is not available.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: An empty judge list throws. Catches an empty panel composing to something the reduction then treats as a real result. P2: the empty boundary of the same configuration guard, asserting the exception type only.
requirements: in-process only; composition uses in-test fake judges

rationale: A canonical two-criterion reply yields both criterion scores, the weighted mean, the reasoning and the confidence, and is not an abstention. Redundant by coverage, but it alone asserts the whole ballot shape at once on the format the harness actually asks judges for: every other test here varies one field of a degraded reply, so a parser that produced a correct field in isolation but an incoherent ballot as a whole would go unseen. No prefix member exists in this file, so P0 is not available.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply wrapping its JSON in a fenced code block with prose above it parses to the scored ballot inside. Catches the unwrap being lost, after which the single most common real reply shape from a chat model abstains as unparseable. P1: the unwrap path, holding eight exclusive spans — the most of any test in this file and reached by nothing else in the project.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: The legacy flat score-and-rationale shape parses to a scored ballot on a single-criterion rubric. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the legacy accept case verbatim, and the daemon's adapter maps this shape back to its v1 behaviour: losing it turns every reply in the old format into an abstention, which reads downstream as judges declining rather than as a format the parser stopped accepting.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: The flat scalar form abstains when the rubric has more than one criterion. Redundant by coverage, but it alone bounds the legacy shape to the rubric it is valid for: a scalar score does not say which dimension it scored, so accepting it means guessing, and the guess attributes one judgement to a criterion the judge may never have considered while leaving the others silently unscored.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A JSON-shaped span that does not parse abstains as unparseable rather than throwing, keeping the raw text. Catches a deserialization exception escaping the parser, which turns one bad reply into a judge fault and a degraded panel instead of one abstention. P1: the parse-throw path, distinct from a reply containing no JSON at all, with three exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply stating no confidence defaults to 1.0. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins that default, and the consequence of getting it wrong is total: defaulting to zero puts every reply in the legacy flat format below any abstain floor, so the whole panel is excluded and every item reduces to NoDecision with nothing in the record pointing at the parser.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply scoring one of two criteria abstains with reason schema-violation and contributes no scores at all. Catches a partial ballot being completed with zeros and entering the tally as a genuine worst-case score, which is a fabricated judgement rather than a missing one. P1: the schema boundary of the parse, with two exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A score delivered as the string 8 abstains rather than being read as eight. Redundant by coverage, but it alone guards against type coercion on model-supplied input: a coerced string is the one malformed shape that produces a scored ballot rather than an abstention, so it enters the tally as a real judgement and no downstream signal distinguishes it from a well-formed reply.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A numeric rationale is ignored and the raw text is used, with the score still counted. Catches a type assumption on the rationale field throwing or stringifying a number into the record. P2: a second field-type variation of the raw-text fallback the missing-rationale case already establishes, and the score it preserves is asserted there too.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply carrying a rationale but no score abstains with the rationale, not the raw JSON, as its reasoning. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins which of the two candidate strings survives, and the adapter maps this abstention back to v1's score-zero-with-rationale: preferring the raw text here silently changes the persisted rationale for every partially-structured reply, so the stored record stops matching what v1 recorded for the same input.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply with a score and no rationale scores rather than abstaining, and falls back to the raw text for its reasoning. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the complementary legacy case to its sibling — score present, rationale missing — and the pair is what makes the two fallbacks non-symmetric by design rather than by accident. Treating the missing rationale as a schema violation would discard a usable score.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply with no JSON at all abstains as unparseable and keeps the trimmed raw text as its reasoning. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the legacy default the daemon adapter reproduces: the raw text is exactly what v1 persisted as the rationale, and dropping it leaves an abstention with nothing recorded about what the judge actually said, which is the only evidence available when a model stops honouring the format.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A reply declaring an abstention abstains with reason declined and keeps its stated reasoning. Catches a deliberate decline being mapped onto the same reason code as a parse failure, which is the distinction an operator needs to tell a judge that would not answer from a judge that could not. P1: the deliberate arm of abstention, with two exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: Confidences of 4.2 and -1 are clamped to 1.0 and 0.0. Catches an unclamped model-supplied value reaching the record. P2: both clamped values fall on the same side of any abstain floor as their unclamped originals, so the behaviour this changes is the persisted number rather than which ballots count.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A bare JSON object surrounded by conversational prose parses to the ballot inside. Catches the extraction being written for fenced blocks only. P2: it makes the same two assertions as the fenced case on a second wrapper shape, and holds no exclusive spans — the fenced test carries the extraction path's own coverage.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: The parsed ballot carries the judge id, model id and model family, and its applied weight is null. Catches provenance being dropped at the point the ballot is minted, and pins the producer half of the invariant the aggregator owns: a judge cannot know its own weight, so a non-null value here would be a number nothing computed surviving into the persisted record. P1, with one exclusive span of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: Scores of 8 and 4 under weights 3 and 1 give 7, not the unnormalised 28, and the result is asserted to stay within the rubric's maximum. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins normalisation by total weight, which is what keeps the ballot on the rubric's own scale and directly comparable to the pass threshold: an unnormalised score compares against a threshold on a different scale, so every weighted rubric passes everything.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the reply is a literal

rationale: A bare file name with a line number and no directory separator yields no finding. Redundant by coverage, but it alone sets the lower bound on what counts as a citation: without it ordinary prose naming a file inflates every citation count, and the inflation is invisible because the extra findings look exactly like real ones.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A severity written as bold markdown rather than in brackets is recognised. Catches the severity match being tied to one syntax. P2: a second notation for the severity the canonical case already recovers, asserting only that field.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: One review line yields exactly one finding whose path, line number and severity are each asserted to their exact values. Confirmed against its contract: it is the canonical shape of everything this parser produces and the only test asserting all three recovered fields together, so it is the baseline every other case here is a variation of. The findings it produces feed both the anchor-resolution measure and the citation-surface comparison between two reviews, so a wrong base parse is wrong everywhere downstream with nothing to signal it. Its assertions are exact values rather than shape checks.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A citation with no severity tag records a null severity. Redundant by coverage, but it alone refuses a default: filling in a value such as info puts a severity in the data that no reviewer wrote, and a caller segmenting findings by severity counts it as a real one, so the invented rows are indistinguishable from stated ones in every later analysis.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A bracketed citation reference is not read as a severity. Redundant by coverage, but it alone bounds the severity match to known severity words: matching any bracketed token turns every specification reference, ticket id or footnote marker in ordinary review prose into a severity, which both fabricates severities and would rank findings by them.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A line number too large for an int keeps the finding with its path and severity and a null line. Redundant by coverage, but it alone separates a malformed citation from an absent one: the overflow made the whole finding disappear, so a review citing an impossible line scored identically to one citing nothing there, and those are different review defects at exactly the measure that grades anchor resolution.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: Two cited files on one line yield two findings in order, a path mentioned without a line yields none, and both carry the line's severity. Redundant by coverage, but it alone shows the scan continuing past the first match: stopping there silently halves the citation surface of any review that cites more than one place per sentence, which is most of them, and the count is what the anchor measure reads.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A single tag sitting after both citations still applies to both. Redundant by coverage, but it alone stops the nearest-preceding-tag rule from being written as tags apply only forwards, which would drop the severity from every review that states it at the end of a sentence. P1: the non-vacuity partner that keeps the anti-smearing fix from over-correcting into lost severities.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: The same file and line cited three times yields three findings. Catches a distinct-by-default collapse. P1: the parser feeds a comparison between two reviews' citation surfaces, and a review citing one line three times is a different review from one citing it once — collapsing them makes a repetitive review indistinguishable from a focused one at exactly the measure meant to tell them apart.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: Null, empty, whitespace and citation-free prose each yield no findings. Catches both a null dereference on the entry point and a pattern loose enough to invent findings from ordinary text. P1: the four-case empty boundary of the parser, holding two exclusive spans reached by nothing else, and null is a reachable input because a judge reply can carry no content at all.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A severity stated on the first line does not carry to a citation on the second. Redundant by coverage, but it alone bounds the tag's scope to its own line: a severity that leaks forward tags every later citation in the review with the first severity a reviewer happened to write, which both fabricates severities and makes the blocker count meaningless.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: Two tags on one line attach to their own citations rather than both taking the first. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins the nearest-preceding-tag rule: computing the severity once per line and reusing it promotes every citation sharing a line with a blocker to a blocker, which inflates the most consequential severity in the data and does so silently, since each finding still looks well formed.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A backslash-separated path with a line number is recovered. Catches a path pattern written for forward slashes only. P2: a second separator form reaching the same extraction as the canonical case and asserting the same two fields, with no exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the parser is pure and the review text is a literal

rationale: A host-supplied renderer's output reaches the transport byte for byte, with no rubric prompt wrapped around it. Redundant by coverage, but it alone pins verbatim substitution: the host may already own a rendered prompt, and appending or re-rendering changes the bytes that reach the model, which changes the scores while every identity in the run stays fixed. P1, with one exclusive span of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the transport is an in-test delegate

rationale: A transport exception propagates out of the judge. Redundant by coverage, but it alone fixes where a provider outage is classified: swallowing it here returns an abstention, which the aggregator counts as the judge having declined — a different fact about a different cause, and one that hides the outage from the fault rate and the degradation reason that exist to surface it.
requirements: in-process only; the transport is an in-test delegate

rationale: A reply the parser cannot read becomes an abstention keeping the raw text, not a scored zero. Catches an unreadable reply entering the tally as a genuine worst-case judgement, which is a fabricated opinion rather than a missing one and drags the panel mean down with no signal that anything failed. P1: the judge-level degradation path, with three exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the transport is an in-test delegate

rationale: Over an injected transport, the judge renders a prompt carrying the candidate and the criterion, and the parsed ballot holds the score and the judge's identity. Redundant by coverage, but it alone asserts the render, send and parse steps as one loop with the prompt captured: the renderer and parser are tested separately, so a judge that rendered correctly and then handed the transport's reply to the wrong parse would go unseen in both.
requirements: in-process only; the transport is an in-test delegate

rationale: Built over a real multi-turn agent, the judge sends exactly one prompt containing the candidate and parses the agent's reply into a scored ballot with its reasoning. Confirmed against its contract: every other test in this file injects a delegate transport, so this is the only test exercising the transport every deployment actually uses — the seam between the judge and the agent abstraction is otherwise entirely unexercised, and a break there fails at runtime with all six of its siblings green. It also pins exactly one turn, so a judge that drove a conversation would be caught: extra turns multiply cost per candidate and let the judge's own earlier output contaminate its score.
requirements: in-process only; the agent is an in-test scripted double with no network

rationale: A reference set on the judge context appears in the prompt the transport receives. Redundant by coverage, but it alone covers the seam between the judge and the renderer: the renderer's own test proves it renders a reference it is given, and this proves the judge actually gives it one. Dropping the context leaves the reference silently absent from every judged item, which turns off the largest accuracy lever the harness has with no error anywhere.
requirements: in-process only; the transport is an in-test delegate

rationale: A reference supplied on the context appears in the prompt. Catches the reference being accepted and then dropped, which silently disables the single largest accuracy lever the harness has: the run completes, the scores move, and nothing in the record says the judges were working without the reference they were configured with.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: The first criterion appears before the second. Redundant by coverage, but it alone fixes criterion order to the versioned rubric: order is the one residual sequence a pointwise judge can prefer, and a renderer that sorted or enumerated a dictionary would reorder criteria between runs of the same rubric, moving scores with nothing in the recorded identity having changed.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: No reference heading is emitted when the context carries none. Catches an empty section being rendered unconditionally. P2: the absence partner of the reference case, whose failure mode is a stray heading in the prompt rather than a lost or wrong score.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: The generator's model id, its family, a variant label naming a model, and host metadata naming one are all absent from the prompt. Redundant by coverage, but it alone enforces the self-recognition control, and it covers four separate carriers rather than one: self-preference is causally tied to a model recognising its own output, so any surviving cue biases every score the judge produces in a direction no downstream check can detect. The metadata case matters most, because host metadata is arbitrary and would otherwise flow into the prompt by default.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure
uncertainties: Four absence assertions against a prompt whose positive content is asserted only by the sibling test; a renderer returning an empty string would satisfy this one on its own.

rationale: The rendered prompt carries the task instruction, the candidate content, both criterion ids and an anchor's text. Redundant by coverage, but it alone asserts the prompt's substance: every other test here is about ordering or absence, all of which a renderer emitting a template with no candidate in it would satisfy, and a judge handed a prompt missing a criterion scores it from nothing while the ballot still looks complete. No prefix member exists in this file, so P0 is not available.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: The prompt contains the rubric's minimum and maximum. Catches the scale being omitted from the prompt entirely. P2 rather than P1: the assertion is a substring search for the digits 0 and 10, which almost any prompt text satisfies incidentally, so it does not establish that the rendered scale is the rubric's rather than a constant.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure
uncertainties: Contain("0") and Contain("10") match incidental digits anywhere in the prompt, including inside the anchor text the fixture rubric already carries, so the test would pass against a renderer that hard-coded a different scale.

rationale: The reasoning field precedes the scores field in the response schema handed to the judge. Redundant by coverage, but it alone enforces reason-before-score structurally rather than by instruction: a schema that puts the score first invites the model to commit to a number and then justify it, which is the ordering the rubric spec exists to prevent, and no assertion on the returned ballot can see which order the model was asked in.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: With the rubric's flag turned off, the scores field precedes the reasoning field. Catches the ordering being hard-coded rather than driven by the rubric, which would make a rubric that deliberately turned the control off silently keep it on. P1: the non-vacuity partner that proves the flag is read at all, with one exclusive span of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the renderer is pure

rationale: A criterion anchored only at its floor and ceiling is refused with one error naming the missing midpoint. Catches a criterion whose middle of the scale is undefined, so judges asked for a score between the extremes have nothing to calibrate against and the middle band means whatever each model decides. P1: a structural drafting rule with two exclusive spans of its own, and the error names the specific missing score.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A criterion using reward-for-volume language with no capping anchor is refused with exactly one error naming the term. Redundant by coverage, but it alone states the anti-verbosity control this validator exists for: uncapped volume language is an instruction to prefer the longer candidate, which biases every score the rubric ever produces, and naming the offending term is what makes the refusal actionable for the author.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: Two criteria sharing an id are refused. Catches a rubric whose criterion ids collide in the score dictionary the parser builds, where the second silently overwrites the first: the ballot then reports fewer scores than the rubric declared and the missing-criterion check fires against the author's own rubric. P1, with two exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A criterion weighted zero is refused with an error naming the non-positive weight. Redundant by coverage, but it alone guards the denominator of the weighted mean: a rubric whose weights sum to zero divides by zero at every ballot, and a single zero weight silently removes a criterion the author believed was being scored.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A pass threshold of 42 on the rubric's own scale is refused with an error quoting it. Redundant by coverage, but it alone relates the threshold to the scale: a threshold above the maximum fails every candidate and one below the minimum passes every candidate, and in both cases the run completes normally and reports a rate that looks like a finding about the candidates.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A rubric with an empty criteria list is refused. Catches the degenerate rubric that gives the weighted mean no denominator at all, which either divides by zero or scores every candidate identically depending on how the reduction guards it. P1: the empty boundary of the rubric, with three exclusive spans of its own.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A well-drafted rubric passes validation. Redundant by coverage, but it alone is the accept case: every other test here asserts a refusal, all of which are satisfied by a validator that rejects every rubric, and that failure would make the harness unusable while the suite stayed green.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A rubric whose minimum equals its maximum is refused. Catches a zero-width scale, on which every candidate scores the same value and no comparison between candidates can ever move. P1: a structural precondition of scoring, with three exclusive spans reached by no other test.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test

rationale: A rubric carrying a volume term, a missing midpoint anchor and a negative weight reports more than two errors. Catches a validator that returns on its first problem, which turns fixing a rubric into as many round trips as it has defects. Prefix candidate at rank 5 with 47 marginal spans, DECLINED for P0: the assertion is a lower bound on the error count with no claim about which errors were produced, so a validator emitting the same generic message three times satisfies it. Its marginal spans come from being the first row in greedy order to validate a multi-fault rubric rather than from the strength of its contract, and coverage from a weak assertion is not a P0 justification. P1 by its own contract.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test
uncertainties: HaveCountGreaterThan(2) does not identify the three distinct defects the rubric was built to carry, so a regression that replaced one specific error with a duplicate of another would not be caught.

rationale: Six volume terms are each refused, including both spellings of in-depth. Catches a term being dropped from the list. P2: parameterisation over the term table whose behaviour the uncapped-volume case already establishes.
requirements: in-process only; the validator is pure and the rubric is built in the test
