P0 as the single worst-silent-failure contract of the identity work; the compaction row extends it to the envelope view. No coverage capture exists for this row.
requirements: in-process only; mocked provider, no run executed
component: LmMultiTurn.Collaboration (identity preamble in the loop prompt)
uncertainties: No coverage capture exists for this branch's rows; the P0 stands on the contract, not on rank or prefix.

rationale: A loop constructed without a collaboration holds exactly the base prompt it was given. The non-collaborating loop is every legacy conversation, and a prompt that gained a preamble there would change model behaviour with no error anywhere. P1: the distinguishing partner of the P0 row at the loop boundary.
requirements: in-process only; mocked provider, no run executed

rationale: A child spawned through the real manager at the default depth limit sends a message that reaches a peer under its own name. A leaf used to be handed no sub-agent options at all, so its loop built no tool provider and it was registered, addressable and unable to answer — with the default limit of 1 that is every sub-agent there is. Going through the manager rather than building the child's manager by hand is the only way to see it. P1.

A usage sink that throws inside the monitor loop faults the run and the directory publishes the child as Error. Left at running the whole hierarchy believes the child is live: a steer to it passes admission and a completion barrier waits on a run that can never answer. Injecting through the usage relay is deliberate — it runs before any completion handling, while the entry still says running. P1.

A delegate spawned under a workflow-style host spawns an ordinary helper with a name no authored unit matches, and the helper carries the delegate's own role and description; the delegate's manager has no name gate and no per-spawn model resolver, while the mode-wide type policy and the model catalog are inherited. Handed down verbatim those hooks would reject ordinary helpers, override their model, and publish them wearing the controller's authored role. Going through the real spawn path is the only way to observe what is passed down. P1, and it holds 6 exclusive spans.

A tool that acts as exactly one agent is built per participant: the child gets its own instance bound to the child, that instance is absent from the child's inheritable snapshot, and the factory still travels to a grandchild which gets its own. An inherited instance hands a descendant its ancestor's reach; registering only on the root leaves deeper ancestors unable to read the children they spawned. Both failure modes are asserted. P1.

At MaxDelegationDepth 2 a child gets its own separate manager that advertises Agent, and its spawn lands at DelegationDepth 2 with the child as parent and both ancestors recorded in order. Recursive delegation across independent managers sharing only the collaboration is the structural claim; ancestor order is what a reader of the directory navigates by. P1.

Driving a real loop whose Agent tool was withheld, the call comes back as an error carrying the DepthLimit code on both the result and the JSON body, with text that avoids "Unknown function", names SendMessage as the next valid action, and lists GetAgents among the available functions. A bare unknown-function answer tells the agent neither that it hit a rule nor what to do instead. P1.

With both withdrawal reasons holding at once the permanent one wins: the code is DepthLimit and the text avoids "for this turn". Reporting the temporary reason would promise a retry guaranteed to fail forever. A precedence combination over the refusal the teaching-refusal case already pins. P2.

Both published fields warn about secrets and customer data in their parameter descriptions, since a warning added after the fact cannot un-share what a model already wrote into a directory everyone reads. Substring checks on prompt text extending the metadata contract. P2, and not lower: the exposure it guards against is real.
Under collaboration the Agent tool advertises a role parameter and makes description required. The schema shape whose enforcement the three admission refusals already pin behaviourally. P2.

The same loop and harness with only the tool name changed to one nothing ever advertised gets the plain unknown-function error, no error code and no code property. This is the discriminator that makes the teaching refusal evidence about withdrawal rather than about every unregistered name. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

The legacy WaitAgent and the collaborative WaitForAgents both warn against passing workflow ids and both embed the shared WorkflowIdRedirect constant, which names WaitWorkflow. Pinning both in one test is what stops the guidance existing only on the surface the affected model never loads. Description text, so P2.

Once a question is answered the outbound block disappears entirely. The list exists to be acted on, so a view that kept answered questions would grow all session and bury the entries that matter. P1 as the closing half of the obligations view.

Three targets — no endpoint, a refusing endpoint, and a live one — produce an outbound list distinguishing delivery_failed with a non-retryable reason, delivery_failed with a retryable one, and delivered with both fields null. A delivery failure closes the ledger entry, so an open-only view hides the message exactly when the sender most needs it, and collapsing retryable makes a sender either abandon a recoverable message or retry a hopeless one forever. Each failed row also carries to_name, the name the accepted-send receipt used, so the sender acts in the vocabulary it uses for its peers rather than the ordinal alone. This sender-obligation projection is independently P0: changing only the observation query or retryable mapping makes it fail while typed message delivery remains green. Coverage records greedy rank 31 with 12 exclusive spans; rank is supporting evidence only.

A peer that the caller never spawned is observed by name and status rather than reported not_found. Collaboration made every agent addressable, so observation has to reach as far as addressing does — being told an agent you are waiting on does not exist is a dead end. P1.

Two ids in one call return requested 2, not_found 0 and two observed agents. Batch observation is the primary behaviour of the tool that replaced the singular CheckAgent. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

An unsettled obligation toward an agent the call did not name is absent from the answer, while the ledger is asserted to still hold it. The scoping keeps the answer proportional to the question; the ledger assertion is what stops this passing on an implementation that simply lost the obligation. P1.

Three admitted spawns, two of them still queued behind a saturated gate, all give their root-wide leases back on disposal and both queued rows read Stopped and not live. Two are used deliberately so each of the manager's two shutdown drain loops retires an entry. The other pre-start exit from the cancellation case: manager teardown rather than caller cancellation. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

Disposing a manager frees the root-wide slot its child held, proven by a fresh manager successfully spawning afterwards under a cap of one, and the spawning agent's own directory row survives. Proving the reclaim through a real admission rather than a counter is what makes it meaningful. P1.

GetAgents returns the caller's own id, both agents, exactly one marked is_you, and the spawned peer by name. Without the self-marker an agent cannot tell which row is itself and may message or wait on itself. P1 for the discovery surface.

With three retired agents over the cap the listing reports total 6, returned 3, truncated true with a note naming finished agents, and every listed row is live. A retired row is never deleted, so an unbounded listing charges every turn for the whole history; a silent truncation invites the model to conclude an agent it cannot see does not exist. P1.

Each row carries structural_depth and delegation_depth separately plus transcript_readable, true for a child of the caller, read with detail=detailed where those fields now live. One "depth" cannot mean two things — only the delegation one says whether an agent may spawn — and publishing readability saves a caller a turn spent discovering a refusal it could have foreseen. P1.

With a cap of one and three live agents all three are still listed and only the retired one is dropped. The cap bounds the retained tail only; hiding a live agent would make the caller spawn a duplicate of one it can already address, which costs far more than the tokens saved. P1 as the boundary the cap must never cross.

Under the cap the listing reports returned equal to total, truncated false, and omits the truncation note entirely. The unconditional counts save a reader inferring completeness from array length. The negative side of the cap the two truncation cases pin. P2.

At MaxDelegationDepth 0 only Agent is withheld; CheckAgents, WaitForAgents, GetAgents and SendMessage all remain. Hiding the observation tools too would leave an agent able to ask a question it could never notice the answer to. P1 for the boundary that decides what a leaf can still do.

With collaboration the surface becomes Agent, CheckAgents, WaitForAgents, GetAgents and SendMessage, and the singular CheckAgent and WaitAgent are gone with no alias left behind. Leaving both generations advertised would let a model split its waits across two tools with different semantics. P1.

With no collaboration the provider exposes exactly Agent, SendMessage, CheckAgent and WaitAgent, Agent has no role parameter, description is optional, and SendMessage keeps its legacy parameter set. Absence of collaboration is the feature gate, so this is what proves the new surface did not leak into hosts that never opted in. P1.

msg_type is advertised as an enum of exactly the five kinds that exist. An open string invites a kind the handler can only reject after the fact, spending a turn on a mistake the schema could have prevented. On its own contract this is schema shape, arguing P2; the exclusiveSpans floor places it at P1.

msg_type's description says task_update needs an open delegated task, and in_response_to's says its id comes from the DelegateTask envelope. The schema is built once per loop so the enum cannot narrow per turn, leaving prose as the only channel. Text checks extending the gate the behavioural tests pin. P2.

A provider built from a setup that is retired out from under it refuses with InvalidSender and text saying the sender is no longer active. The bundle-level refusal is covered elsewhere; this is the same refusal through the tool a retired agent's loop still holds, where the model sees only the text. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

For question, delegate_task and steer an empty-string in_response_to normalizes to absent and the send succeeds. The persisted bug: omitted and JSON-null already collapsed to null but a blank string survived, skipping the reply-only guard and reaching the messenger, where the ledger refused it as unknown_correlation. P1 as the named regression; its whitespace shape is pinned separately.
The three non-reply types succeed with an explicit JSON null correlation. The second already-working baseline shape. P2.
The three non-reply types succeed with in_response_to omitted entirely. The already-working baseline the blank-string normalization had to match. P2.
The same three non-reply types with a whitespace-only in_response_to also succeed. The second blank shape of the normalization the empty-string case pins. P2.
The same real-but-unknown id on a non-reply type is also refused as UnknownCorrelation — the exact path the normalization touches. The second type through the scoping the response case pins. P2.

The same question sent twice with no idempotency key leaves two open obligations. The half that keeps the key an opt-in: asking twice on purpose is legitimate and nothing may quietly collapse it. Without it the deduplicating implementation the replay test rewards could silently swallow deliberate repeats. P1.

Demoted by the lane-daemon audit, accepted in full by the lead. Daemon's finding: its paired case is P1 and collaboration messaging is already pinned elsewhere, so this row's P0 rested on rank rather than on being the component's unpinned baseline. Zero exclusive spans. Its component keeps SendMessage_ToARealSubAgent_ArrivesAsTheTypedAgentMessage at P0.
response and task_update with an empty-string correlation still return MissingCorrelation rather than being normalized into a valid send. The blank shape on the reply side of the same fix. P2.
response and task_update with an explicit JSON null correlation still return MissingCorrelation. A shape variant confirming the blank-normalization did not weaken the reply-side guard. P2.
response and task_update with a whitespace-only correlation still return MissingCorrelation. The third shape through the reply-side guard. P2.

A well-formed but unrecognised in_response_to on a response is refused as UnknownCorrelation. This is what scopes the blank-normalization to blanks only: collapsing a real-but-wrong id to "no correlation" would admit a reply to nothing. P1.

A response with no in_response_to is refused with missing_correlation before admission. An uncorrelated reply is admitted as an obligation nobody can match to a question, so the guard has to sit in front of admission rather than after it. P1 as the primary reply-side guard; its null, empty and whitespace shapes are pinned separately.

A steer to a completed agent is refused with TargetNotActive at admission. A steer redirects work in flight; accepted for an idle agent it either restarts it — the opposite of redirecting — or is dropped after the sender was told accepted. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

A task_update with no correlation, against a seeded open delegation so the refusal under test is the missing id rather than the absent delegation, is refused with missing_correlation. The second message type through the guard the response case pins. P2.

Correlating to a delegation whose answer has already landed returns CorrelationAnswered listing the still-open delegation and specifically not the answered one. An agent holding several delegations names the one it just finished far more readily than one that never existed, and repeating its own wrong id back tells it nothing. The answer is settled through the messenger with delivery awaited so the state under test really is answered. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

A task_update correlated to a real open delegation is accepted and arrives with the TaskUpdate kind and the delegation id intact. The positive case the whole #689 gate is built around; without it a gate that refused every task_update would satisfy all the negatives. P1.

An invented correlation against a real open delegation returns UnknownCorrelation listing the open id, and nothing reaches the target. The answered-delegation case pins the same listing with the sharper exclusion assertion. P2.

With no delegation at all — correlation null, 'none', or an invented id — the refusal is NoOpenDelegation naming response and question as the types that do apply, and nothing was admitted: the ledger count is unchanged, no outbound obligation exists and the target received nothing. Telling the agent only that the id was not received invited guesses like 'none'. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.
A task_update with no correlation but a real open delegation returns MissingCorrelation and names the id it should have used. A third entry point into the same id-listing behaviour. P2.

A child confirmed Completed is woken by a delivered message and the directory then reports it Running. A woken child still reading completed is unaddressable to a steer and invisible to anyone deciding whether to wait. P1 for the status the whole hierarchy reads.

A message sent to a finished child restarts it and arrives in its own run as an AgentMessage carrying the dispatch's message id, its type, the sender id and Role.User — not flattened to text. Flattening strips the sender, kind and correlation that the UI and persisted history read back, leaving a rehydrated conversation unable to distinguish an agent message from user text. This typed-delivery contract is independently P0: changing only message construction or persistence makes it fail while sender-obligation projection remains green. Coverage records greedy rank 3; the tier does not rest on the span count.

A retired peer returns UnknownTarget with text saying it finished. A wrong name is the sender's mistake to correct; a retired agent is a real one whose work is over, and conflating them sends the model hunting for a typo that does not exist. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

An agent tombstoned by restart reconciliation — with the reconciler's Invalidated set asserted non-empty first, so the refusal is not vacuous — returns TargetNotLive with text naming restarted, telling it to spawn the agent again with Agent, and ending in the same no-other-agents roster sentence every other refusal ends with. This is the only unreachability whose recovery is "make a new one", which the model cannot derive from a generic no-match. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

An unknown target returns a NotFound error whose text is asserted exactly: it names the miss and, with nobody else registered, says there is no other agent to address. That sentence replaced a pointer at GetAgents, which sent the model to read a roster containing only itself. One of three distinct unreachability answers whose whole value is that they differ. P1, and it holds a span no other declaration reaches.

Addressing your own agent id is refused with SelfDelivery. Admitted, a self-message creates an obligation only the sender can discharge and can wake the sender's own wait. On its own contract a boundary arguing P2; the exclusiveSpans floor places it at P1.

A question to a registered peer that is not a child is accepted, names the target, reports expects_reply, and actually arrives at the peer's endpoint with the sender id and the typed kind. Any-to-any addressing is the primary behaviour collaboration adds, and asserting the arrival rather than only the receipt is what proves admission is not the whole story. P1.

Invoked with an already-cancelled token the send is accepted and the message still arrives at the peer. The tool-call token signals the end of the sender's turn; letting it drop an accepted message leaves the receiver waiting for something nobody is carrying. P1 for the ownership handover at admission.

An unrecognised msg_type returns invalid_msg_type whose text names a real kind. Listing the alternatives turns a rejected call into a corrected one. P1, and it holds 4 spans no other measured declaration reaches.

With MaxTotalAgents 1 the second spawn is refused with CapacityExhausted even though this manager's own concurrency gate would admit it. The root-wide cap is exactly what per-manager concurrency cannot express, and queueing instead of refusing would hide the limit from the caller indefinitely. P1.

A foreground spawn queued behind a saturated local gate is shown holding both root-wide resources (capacity 2, status Queued), and after cancellation the lease comes back and the row reads Stopped and not live. Admission happens before the local gate is consulted, so this pre-start exit is distinct from a construction failure; unreclaimed, a cancelled retry permanently shrinks capacity. The wait-for-reclaim is deliberate: the caller's release and the pump's reclaim are genuinely concurrent. P1.

A grandchild manager built from a child that cannot delegate throws SubAgentCollaborationException with DepthLimit when it spawns directly. Hiding the tool is guidance for the next turn, not enforcement — a model can call a tool it saw earlier — so the depth rule has to be re-checked at admission. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

A successful spawn publishes the child with its role, description, parent id, DelegationDepth 1 and agent type into the directory shared with the root. This is the whole point of collaboration-aware spawning; an unpublished child is unaddressable by everyone but its parent. P1 rather than P0 only because measured coverage shows every span it reaches is reached by other declarations in the prefix.

A template whose factory throws leaves capacity at zero and the root row intact, and the next spawn really is admitted. Capacity is taken before the agent is built, so a bad model id or dead provider throws while holding a permit; forgetting it shrinks the collaboration by one agent for the rest of its life with no error anywhere. P1.

A caller-supplied role that contradicts a Fixed-role template is refused with InvalidRole rather than silently overridden, which would leave the model believing it had labelled the child one thing while every other agent saw another. P1, and it holds 2 spans no other measured declaration reaches.

A spawn with a role but no description is refused with InvalidDescription — a distinct code from the missing role, which is what tells the model which field to add. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

With a Fixed-role template a spawn omitting role succeeds and the directory shows the template's role. The positive counterpart of the missing-role refusal: without it a provider that demanded role unconditionally would satisfy every negative case and break every host that pins roles. P1.

A spawn with no role under collaboration is refused with InvalidRole. The directory entry is what every other agent reads, so an unlabelled child is addressable but unidentifiable; an actionable code is what lets the model add the field rather than retry blind. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.

The WaitForAgents description contains both a WHEN TO USE IT and a WHEN NOT TO USE IT section, because waiting is the one collaboration tool that costs the caller its turn. Two substring checks on prompt text. P2.

The description describes not_waitable as every named agent being real but none of them a child, and specifically does not describe it as "nothing you named is one of your own children" — an outcome a set of typos never produces, since those refuse the whole call. Prose precision on an already-pinned status. P2.

A wait that ends on a completion reports no question and the claim it took is returned, so a later wait on a still-running child is interrupted by that same question. The sweep claims before the race is decided, so without the give-back the question can never wake any wait again and the agent goes on waiting with no way to notice it was asked. Both waits are decided by what is already complete, so the ordering is structural rather than a timing bet. P1.
In any mode the answer still carries the last_result of the child that finished before the barrier was even built. Losing it would make any mode cost exactly the work it saved. P1.
A question interrupt also carries msg_type on its interrupt block, since the status alone no longer identifies the kind. The second branch of the discriminator the delegation case introduces. P2.

A delegation to the waiter ends the wait with status interrupted, the interrupt block carrying the message id, the sender name and msg_type delegate_task, the pre-rename question field still filled, and the delegation still open. A delegation blocks its sender exactly as a question does, so waking only for questions parks the delegator behind a wait that cannot end. The capped timeout makes the defect read as a failure rather than a hung suite. P1, and it holds an exclusive span.

A question delivered to the waiter before the wait begins ends it with question_received naming the asker. A waiting agent that cannot be reached is a deadlock waiting to happen, since whoever needs an answer from it blocks until a wait that may need that answer finishes. P1.

A question admitted after the wait starts is caught by the subscription rather than the opening sweep and still reports question_received. The mirror ordering of the interrupt case already pinned, exercising the second of the two notification paths. P2.

A steer admitted while the wait is listening does not end it; the wait times out. The interrupt set is exactly the kinds whose sender stays blocked, and a steer closes on delivery owing nothing back, so waking for one makes every wait unpredictable without unblocking anybody. The negative that bounds the interrupt set. P1, and it holds 9 spans no other measured declaration reaches.

After one interrupt the next wait times out instead of rediscovering the same open question, and the question is still owed a reply. Without the one-shot claim an agent that chose not to answer would spin instead of waiting and could never wait for its children again. P1.

A child that asked its parent something and then finished — asserted terminal and still owing an answer — is reported completed with its result, not as a cycle. SendMessage returns on admission and a finished run is not retired, so this is the normal shape rather than an edge case; reading the cycle off the sender alone turned every later wait on such a child into wait_cycle and told the coordinator to answer an agent that had already finished, which restarts it. In all mode one such target would suppress the outcome for every healthy sibling. P1.

A list mixing a real child with a name matching nothing refuses the whole call with unknown_agent naming the bad one. Partially waiting would leave the caller believing it had waited on everything it asked about. P1.

An expired wait reports timeout and the agent is still peekable in the manager: the wait abandons the observation, never the agent. A destructive timeout would kill a running sub-agent because its parent grew impatient. P1.

An agent naming its own id is refused with unknown_agent naming that id. Without the guard the directory resolves it into the peer partition and the caller is told to send itself a message. A self-reference boundary on the target-partitioning the peer cases pin. P2.

Waiting on peers alone returns a non-error not_waitable listing them rather than an error. A refusal here counts as a retry storm in run-level analysis when what happened is an observation that names its own next action. P1, and it holds 2 exclusive spans.
Waiting on one finished child returns status completed with requested 1. The primary success path of the barrier every other case is a deviation from. P1.

When the child being waited on is itself blocked on an unanswered question to the waiter, the call reports wait_cycle with cycle_kind unanswered_inbound, the blocking message's id, sender and kind, and a next action naming that id — and a second wait says the same thing rather than blocking, with the question still open. The one-shot interrupt cannot fix this deadlock: after one wait every later one would block in silence. P1, and it holds 7 exclusive spans.

A list mixing a child with a peer completes on the child and returns the peer under not_waited with its agent id, the reason peer_not_child and a non-empty next action, while only the child is counted as waited on. Refusing the whole call for a real agent that simply is not yours teaches the model nothing. P1.

While a reply is admitted but not yet delivered the question it answers is still open but spoken for, and the wait neither reports a cycle nor interrupts — it times out. Both readers of the open-inbound set have to honour that claim, or the wait advises answering a message a second reply would be refused for. The pending-response id is asserted first so the window really exists. P1.

An open question from an agent this wait is not blocked on interrupts once and then lets the wait time out, rather than reporting a cycle. This is the narrowness of the cycle check: any obligation at all turning every wait into wait_cycle would make the feature useless. P1.

A wait is parked, a question arrives and is provably claimed, the caller then cancels, and the claim must come back: the question stays open, WaitInterruptClaimed returns to false, and — the half that makes it more than a flag check — a SECOND wait is then able to spend the same interrupt and receive that question by id. The determinism is structural, not timed: a PumpingSynchronizationContext installed only for the handler call queues every continuation, so the test decides exactly where the async method is suspended when the cancellation lands, rather than trying to hit a window a few thread-pool hops wide. The remarks state why this path is the dangerous one — every other abandonment route is covered elsewhere, and this is the one that leaves by throwing, where losing the claim is PERMANENT because the question stays open and no later wait can be woken by it again. Catches one cancelled wait silently disarming every future wait in the conversation. P1: the claim-release contract on the throwing path.
requirements: in-process only; mocked parent and provider, pumped synchronization context, bounded teardown
uncertainties: Strong enough to nominate on its own consequence — a permanently lost claim — but the SubAgents component already carries two candidates in this slice (the recursion guard and the ListAgents snapshot). Held at P1 rather than adding a third; raised here so the lead can substitute it for one of those if they judge it stronger.

rationale: Ancestry is DIRECTIONAL. The distinguishing case against a policy that merely checks shared lineage: a child reading its parent's transcript would expose every other branch of the parent's work that the child was never party to. P1.

The disclosure boundary this whole file exists for: contact and read are SEPARATE privileges, so a sibling that may address a peer may not read its transcript, which can carry reasoning and content the peer's own caller never meant to publish. Denied with the typed NotAnAncestor reason. P1.

Widening is only ever an explicit configuration choice: under Open a sibling read is allowed with the OpenCollaboration reason. Also the non-vacuity partner for :67 — without it a policy that denied everything would pass the denial rows. P1.
Self-read is allowed under both modes with the Self reason. The trivially-permitted base case, and the non-vacuity floor under the denials below. P2.
uncertainties: No row in this file is an inP0Prefix member, so no P0 is proposed here.

rationale: An ancestor may read a descendant AT ANY DISTANCE — a grandparent, not merely a parent. The chain above a target already sees its material through its own children, so this discloses nothing new; a policy that checked only the immediate parent would deny legitimate reads across a deep hierarchy. P1.

The caller is routinely a model-driven tool invocation carrying an arbitrary string, so an unknown reader or target is DENIED with its own typed reason rather than throwing — an exception here becomes an error surface that distinguishes existing agents from absent ones. Rank 149 with 8 marginal spans. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The refusal that must be checked BEFORE anything that could allow: a reader whose id appears in another collaboration's ancestry must still be refused across the boundary, under both modes, so Open widens ONE collaboration rather than all of them. Ordering the check after the allow rules turns a shared identifier into a cross-tenant read. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The denial reason must not echo the target's role or description. A refusal that quotes what it refused discloses exactly the material the policy exists to withhold, and these reasons are surfaced to the model and written to logs. P1.

The numbers the compaction loop makes its trigger decisions from: hidden rows, tail rows and estimated tokens, with checkpoint rows counted as neither. Asserted with explicit seq lists and against the raw view as well. Thirty-five exclusive spans — the widest sole-cover in this file. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 35 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Checkpoint rows are never sent to the provider — not the superseded one, not the active one, not the rolled-back one — and the surviving tail is pinned by exact sequence numbers. A leaked checkpoint row hands the model a second, contradictory summary of its own history. P1.
The store's own seq, id and run survive into the sequenced view, and rows arrive SORTED whatever order the store returned them in. Order here is the order of the conversation the model reads. P1.

Legacy rows with no seq and rows whose JSON will not parse are left out rather than throwing — one unreadable row must not make a conversation unloadable — and the unreadable one is REPORTED through the callback rather than vanishing silently. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 4 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Positional numbering for an in-memory snapshot, with no store ids. A constructor-level detail beside the persisted path below. P2.
Render options are threaded through to the envelope text. Plumbing on the envelope pinned above. P2.

The same equality across a reopened durable store: after a restart the model must be handed the identical conversation, not a differently ordered or differently rendered one. A distinct hazard from the same-process replay above — reopen paths are where seq assignment and ordering drift. P1.

The whole chain through real stores of every flavour — persist, reload, sequence, project — is deterministic on the WIRE FORM, not on record equality, and produces the expected shape with no checkpoint rows. This is where the unit-level rules above are shown to survive persistence round trips. P1.

The compaction claim itself: one user-role envelope stands for everything up to the boundary and the tail follows exactly, asserted as an equality against the rows past the boundary rather than as a count. A boundary off by one silently deletes a turn from the model's view or replays one it was told was summarised. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The uncompacted baseline: system prompt then every row, and the rows are dispatched AS THEY ARE — asserted by reference identity, so a projection that copies or re-serialises them fails. Everything the model ever sees passes through this method. P1.
uncertainties: No row in this file is an inP0Prefix member, so no P0 is proposed here.

rationale: The null and empty prompt variations of the baseline above. P2.
The no-active-checkpoint combination of the drop rule held at :97. P2.

The build-without-commit path: valid checkpoint, default trigger, watermark unmoved and no state row. Its distinctive claim — a rejected or unstarted run leaves the store untouched — is already asserted by :210, :258 and :304 as part of their own rejections. P2.

The only row covering board and roster propagation: the live todo tasks and the sub-agent roster are copied into the manifest as TaskRef/AgentRef and validated against. A compacted context that forgets the board and the running agents leaves the model rediscovering both from nothing. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The anti-fabrication guarantee: a summarizer that PARAPHRASES the human's instruction ('repair the unstable test' for 'fix the flaky test') fails validation rule V3, and the rejection is total — no row appended, watermark unmoved, nothing activated, and the typed reason recorded in history. A checkpoint is the only memory of the rows it hides, so a paraphrase is a silent rewrite of what the user asked for. Rank 47 with 49 marginal spans. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 1 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The interesting shape of a rejection: with a checkpoint ALREADY active, a failed second one must leave the first active and last-known-good rather than clearing the pointer. A rejection that dropped the active checkpoint would expand the context view back to the full history at exactly the moment compaction was needed. P1.

The concurrency window that matters: another handle appends while the summary is in flight, and the checkpoint must reject with stale_watermark rather than commit. Committing would activate a boundary whose summary never saw the newest rows — the agent's own memory would silently omit them, with only the other writer's rows visible in the watermark afterwards. P1.

Caller rows already behind the store are detected BEFORE anything is prepared — asserted by the summarizer recording no request at all and no history entry. Detecting the drift afterwards costs a model call and writes a rejection entry for a checkpoint that should never have been attempted. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Chaining: the second checkpoint carries the first's instructions and goals forward, appends its own index range beside the earlier one, names what it supersedes, marks the first Superseded, summarizes only the rows after the previous boundary, and — because this summarizer makes no model call — records no usage attempt id. Without the carry-forward every compaction loses everything the previous one preserved. P1.

A provider outage during the summary is a different rejection origin from a validation failure: no checkpoint object exists at all, and the recorded reason is the typed summary_call_failed, which is what a caller reads to decide whether a retry is even sensible. P1.

The whole commit path on every store flavour: the checkpoint row is appended at the expected seq, the watermark follows, the state projection activates it at the cut boundary, the manifest carries the instruction quote, the artifact and the index headline, and the summary pass's usage and latency are attributed on the checkpoint. Then the persisted row round-trips and the rebuilt view hides exactly the covered rows behind one envelope. P1.
uncertainties: No row in this file is an inP0Prefix member, so no P0 is proposed here.
Zero exclusive spans over 1803 covered — this row shares nearly all of its reach with the rejection rows below, which is why it is not a coverage argument for P0.

rationale: The one accepting fixture in a file of twenty-one rejections, and therefore the whole suite's non-vacuity anchor: a validator that rejected everything would satisfy every other test here and fail only this one. It also fixes the shared valid checkpoint each rule then mutates in exactly one place. P1.
A checkpoint written by a future schema version is refused rather than read under today's field meanings. Reading one anyway is how a downgrade silently reinterprets a manifest. P1 for rule V1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The boundary names both a seq and a message id, and the id must be the one actually at that seq. The id is what makes the boundary survive a renumbering, so a checkpoint whose id points elsewhere would silently cut a different span of the conversation. P1 for rule V2.
uncertainties: Holds 3 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: A boundary one row past the end is refused. A checkpoint claiming to summarise rows that do not exist would drop the whole tail on the next projection. A distinct exit from the id-mismatch case, on the same rule. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Rows reconstructed positionally, without persisted message ids, cannot satisfy V2 at all — the validator says so instead of falling back to a seq-only check. That fallback is exactly the weaker comparison V2 exists to prevent. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: An empty current instruction is refused when the run has one. The projection leads its envelope with this field, so omitting it hands the resumed agent a summary with no statement of what it was asked to do. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The current instruction must be the WHOLE row, not a prefix of it: 'fix the flaky' is refused for 'fix the flaky test'. Elsewhere a quote may be an excerpt, so this is a strictly stronger rule for the one field the agent is told to obey verbatim. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Two human rows in one run must appear in seq order, and the same body then asserts the reordered manifest VALIDATES — so the rule is pinned in both directions rather than by a rejection that any other defect could also produce. Out-of-order instructions read to the resumed agent as a correction followed by the thing it corrected. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: An empty quote is refused rather than treated as trivially matching whatever row it cites. An empty-string containment check succeeds against everything, so this is the degenerate input that would otherwise make the entire R5 comparison vacuous. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: A quote may only cite a row at or before the boundary. Citing a row from the retained tail would let a checkpoint claim to summarise text that has not been compacted yet, and the quote would then be checked against a row nobody kept. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The same R5 quote check applied to the Decisions collection, with a mutation of capitalisation alone. It is a finer boundary than the instruction case — it pins that matching is exact rather than case-insensitive — but it is a second field under one rule already held at P1. P2 as a variation.

The R5 anti-paraphrase rule and the central honesty guarantee of the whole checkpoint: a quoted instruction must be the row's own words, so 'repair the unstable test' is refused for 'fix the flaky test'. Without it the manifest is a model's restatement of what the user asked for, which is precisely the drift compaction must not introduce. P1.
A manifest task citing an id that is not on the todo board is refused. An invented id survives into the resumed agent's board view as a task nothing can resolve. P1 for rule V4.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Both halves of V4's board rule in one body: an id cited with no board present is refused, while a model-extracted task carrying a NULL id validates. The second half is what keeps the rule from banning checkpoints for conversations that never had a board — the ordinary case — and it is the half a stricter reading would break. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 3 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: An agent id absent from the run's roster is refused, so the manifest cannot attribute work to a sub-agent that never existed. P1 for rule V5.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: An entirely empty index is refused. This is the degenerate input a coverage check written as a scan over entries would pass without ever executing its body, which makes it a distinct exit rather than a smaller version of the gap case. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The index stopping one row short of the boundary. Same rule and same failure — the compacted span is not fully described — with the hole at the end rather than in the middle. P2 as a variation of the gap case held at P1.
uncertainties: Whether this is a separate exit from the gap fixture depends on how the coverage check is written — a single contiguity scan catches both at one exit, a scan plus an endpoint check catches them at two. Classified as a variation without reading the validator; if the product proves two exits, this belongs at P1.

rationale: The index must cover the compacted span with no hole. A gap means a stretch of the conversation that is neither in the tail nor described by any index entry — silently gone, with nothing pointing at it for the recall tool. P1 for rule V6.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The narrative cap is enforced, and the same body asserts a short narrative passes under the same options — so the rejection is attributable to size and not to the fixture. The narrative is the free-text part of a checkpoint and the part most able to grow without limit. P1 for rule V7.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: A checkpoint whose own recovery state reports a parked wait is refused: cut-blocking state at the boundary means the cut should never have been taken. This is the validator's independent check on the selector's decision, so both would have to be wrong at once for a blocked cut to be committed. P1 for rule V8.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The envelope size cap rejecting an oversized checkpoint, with the cap forced low. The rule's load-bearing claim — that the size measured is the envelope actually dispatched — is held at P1 by the fixture below, which subsumes this one's assertion. P2.

The claim that makes V9 mean anything: the cap is measured against the rendered envelope the projection actually dispatches, recall hint included. The cap is set to the baseline render exactly, so adding the recall tool name pushes it over and the same checkpoint under the default render validates — a validator sizing the wrong string passes the plain cap test and still ships an envelope over budget. P1.

The recall instance is bound to a thread, so the parent's must not be in the inheritable snapshot and the child must register its own — asserted on both sides, with domain tools still inherited. An inherited instance would let a sub-agent recall the PARENT's conversation. P1.

The mode's whole contract in one place: the summary runs once on the loop's own model, the applied event carries the economic reason, checkpoint id and boundary, the first requests go out raw, the request that follows is measurably smaller than the one that triggered it, the view stays in force afterwards, and the persisted checkpoint and state agree with the event. P1.

The operator's escape hatch, asserted on both halves: after the switch is pulled every later decision is Skipped/Disabled, and the ALREADY-ACTIVE checkpoint transitions to RolledBack with reason Killed so the provider receives the raw history again. Undetectable defect if this row is dropped: an operator pulls the kill switch, new compactions stop, telemetry looks clean, and the checkpoint installed before the switch keeps rewriting provider input, so the model silently keeps reading a summarized conversation with no way to notice. No P0 in the lane asserts a rollback of an active checkpoint. P0 outside the prefix under the bounded both-directions exception.
uncertainties: Holds 6 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Off emits no decisions, no compaction events and no state — while #681's context observation still happens, with a null decision and null checkpoint stamped on it. That pair is exactly what 'Off changes nothing' means and what a regression enabling measurement-plus-policy would break. P1.

The policy is just-in-time and nowhere else: a threshold crossed by the closing reply produces nothing while the thread sits idle — clock advanced an hour, decision count unchanged, no checkpoint row — and fires on the first request of the next run. A background job would summarise conversations nobody returns to, at cost. P1.

A reflection check that three provider-owned loop types take no CompactionSetup in any public constructor. A structural guard against a future wiring mistake rather than a behaviour of the running system, and coverage records it executing no product spans at all. P2.

A thread mapped to a provider-owned session is skipped with the typed reason, no summary, no envelope. The provider holds that conversation's context itself; compacting locally would send a view of a history the harness does not own. P1.

With no known window the policy skips as capacity-unknown until the provider rejects the request, then compacts and retries the SAME input exactly once, marked reactive in both the event and the persisted row. This is the path for every provider that does not publish a context size — the majority case in the wild. P1.

The other half of the bargain compaction makes: a row hidden behind the checkpoint comes back VERBATIM by keyword, as an ordinary tail row past the boundary, and is carried into the next provider request. If recall could not return the original text, compaction would be lossy rather than deferred. P1.

The recall tool's offering gate: present on every call in Warn, absent on every call in Off, and answering with the typed nothing-compacted result when no checkpoint exists. Offering it in Off puts a tool in the model's list that can never do anything; withholding it in Warn leaves the model unable to reach what compaction is about to hide. P1.

The termination bound on compact-and-retry: when the retry overflows too, the run fails with the typed OverflowAfterCompaction reason, the summarizer ran exactly once and the provider saw exactly eight requests, never a third attempt. The request-count assertion is what makes it a bound rather than a happy-path check. INDEPENDENCE, mechanism named: remove the second-attempt bound from the reactive-overflow path so the loop compacts and retries again instead of failing. This row goes red on the request count and the typed reason. Its component's surviving P0, KillSwitch_SkipsDisabled_AndRollsTheActiveCheckpointBackOnTheNextRequest, stays GREEN — its harness is EchoThenDone(7), which returns normally and never throws the context-length 400 that a second overflow requires, and it asserts IsError is false on both of its runs. It cannot reach the retry path at all. Re-submitted under the refined bound: this row's P0 never rested on rank or prefix standing, and its warrant cites neither. Outside the greedy prefix (rubric line 48), as it was when first promoted; LmMultiTurn.Tests is not a prefixRuleApplied project, so no guard declaration is needed. The defect named above is the one no P0 row detects.
uncertainties: Holds 8 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Shadow does run the summary pass — the point of the mode — while still sending the raw input, appending no checkpoint row, activating nothing, and recording the built checkpoint as Rejected in history. It is the dry run operators use to judge compaction before enabling it, so 'builds' and 'does not apply' must both hold. P1.

Q1: a connection reset is not evidence that the context is too long. Treating any provider exception as overflow would compact — permanently discarding history behind a checkpoint — because a socket dropped. The discriminator that keeps the reactive path from firing on every transport error. P1.

Warn mode observes and never acts: one decision per provider call, no summary pass, no envelope, the raw history growing monotonically, no checkpoint row, and the observation projection stamped 'warn'. The mode a host turns on first, where any mutation of the provider input would be an unasked-for change to what the model sees. P1.
uncertainties: This file's rows each cover 2,500-4,700 spans — the widest in the project — yet none is an inP0Prefix member, because the greedy prefix reaches its target through narrower rows first. Recorded so the absence of a P0 here is visible as a prefix outcome rather than a judgement that the compaction loop does not matter.

rationale: AC 7: with the summary model down the loop refuses rather than sending anyway. Every request it did send is within the usable window, both failure reasons are published, and no checkpoint row is written from the failed attempt. It carries its own anti-vacuity guard, requiring Summarizer.Requests to be non-empty, so the reserve claim cannot pass by the loop never attempting compaction. INDEPENDENCE, mechanism named: when the summarizer throws, let the loop proceed with the un-compacted request instead of refusing. This row goes red on the usable-window assertion and on the published failure reasons. Its component's surviving P0, KillSwitch_SkipsDisabled_AndRollsTheActiveCheckpointBackOnTheNextRequest, stays GREEN — it never sets Summarizer.Fail, so its summarizer always succeeds and the refusal path is never entered; it asserts IsError is false on both runs. Re-submitted under the refined bound: this row's P0 never rested on rank or prefix standing, and its warrant cites neither. Outside the greedy prefix (rubric line 48), as it was when first promoted; LmMultiTurn.Tests is not a prefixRuleApplied project, so no guard declaration is needed. The defect named above is the one no P0 row detects.
uncertainties: Holds 7 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: With a collaboration attached and compaction active, the raw request before the first envelope carries a system message starting with the identity preamble, and every enveloped request after it carries the same. The compaction view is built from the prompt the compaction host holds, so a host handed the caller's raw prompt would make the agent forget who it is on the very turn a checkpoint activates - and every turn after, since the view stays in force. P1: the identity contract carried through the one path that rewrites the system prompt.

Every default on the options object is pinned to the value spec 679 hypothesised: the ratios, the reserve margin, the tail bounds, the token caps, the cooldowns, the per-run compaction cap, the cache TTL, the observation ring length and the recall limits. Catches a threshold quietly retuned by an unrelated change, which would move when compaction fires for every host that never configured it. P2: a constants snapshot rather than a behaviour — it fixes values the behavioural rows elsewhere exercise, and it is the boundary-value complement to them.
uncertainties: One assertion in this row is a different KIND of claim from the other thirteen: Mode defaults to Off, which is the feature's opt-in guarantee rather than a tuning constant. It is the load-bearing line here, and it is buried in a constants snapshot whose failure message will read as a numbers drift.

rationale: The kill switch trips from either the config flag or the environment variable, reads '1' and 'true' as set, and reads '0' and absent as clear. This is the operational off-ramp: the environment path exists precisely so compaction can be disabled on a running host without a config deploy, which is what an operator reaches for when compaction is implicated in an incident. A switch that only honoured the config flag would look correct in every configuration test and fail at the one moment it is needed. Reading '0' as CLEAR is the assertion that stops a present-but-disabled variable from being treated as truthy, which would kill the feature for everyone who set it off explicitly. Catches a kill switch that cannot be thrown, or one thrown by accident. P1: important operational failure handling.
requirements: in-process only; the environment reader is injected as a delegate, so no real environment variable is read
uncertainties: Only '1', 'true', '0' and null are covered. Whitespace, mixed case ('TRUE'), 'yes' and the empty string are unspecified, and an operator setting the variable to an empty value is a realistic case the row does not pin.

rationale: Four lookups walk the whole precedence chain: a provider/model pair matching a route override wins, a bare model name matching an override wins, an unmatched model falls to the configured default, and a null/null pair also falls to the default. The chain is what lets an operator run compaction aggressively in general and hold one troublesome route at Shadow or Warn. Getting the order wrong is silent and asymmetric — a default that beat the override would start rewriting provider input on the exact route someone deliberately held back. The null/null case matters because it is the path taken before a route is known. Catches a per-route exemption that does not take effect. P1: the resolution contract the whole option surface is configured through.
uncertainties: The two override keys are shaped differently — one 'provider/model', one a bare model name — and both resolve, but the file never states which form is canonical or what happens when both could match.

rationale: A ceiling applied to Shadow lowers it to Warn but does NOT raise it to Compact. The one-directional rule is the substantive claim: a ceiling is a safety cap applied by something other than the operator's own configuration, so a ceiling that could raise the mode would let that caller escalate a host into rewriting provider input when configuration deliberately said not to. The second assertion is the one that catches it — a naive implementation that simply assigns the ceiling passes the first and fails only here. Catches a cap that behaves as an override. P1: the monotonicity guarantee of the cap.
uncertainties: Only one starting mode (Shadow) and two ceilings are exercised, so the row proves the rule holds at one point on the ordering rather than across it. It also depends on the enum's declared order encoding 'lower is safer'; nothing in this class asserts that ordering.

rationale: The per-run cap outranks even the hard threshold, with its own reason. It is the runaway guard: a conversation that keeps re-crossing the threshold after each compaction would otherwise compact without bound inside one run. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The runtime kill switch on the identical scenario the row above already pins: same tokens, same decision, same reason, a second flag. Its operational consequence is high — this is the field an incident reaches for — but as a test it is a second input to one Disabled predicate. P2 as a variation, with the rule itself held at P1.

Mode Off skips as Disabled even at the hard threshold — the configuration switch outranks every pressure signal below it. A policy that compacted anyway would rewrite the history of a conversation whose owner had turned the feature off. P1 for the first row of the spec 5.3 decision table.

A session whose context the provider owns is skipped with its own distinct reason rather than folded into Disabled. Compacting here would have two parties rewriting one context, and the separate reason is what tells an operator which of the two happened. P1.

The absolute-token fallback for the same unknown window: past WarnAbsoluteTokens the policy still warns, keeping the CapacityUnknown reason. Without it an unmeasurable session would run silently into the provider's real limit. A distinct branch from the skip above, on the same row. P1.

With no window size there is no utilization to judge, so the policy skips and reports Utilization null rather than inventing a denominator. A guessed ratio here would compact on arithmetic nobody can check. P1 for the unknown-capacity row.

A second counter of the same CutBlockingState predicate already exercised by the owed-continuation case — same construction, same decision, same reason, a different field of one record. P2 as an additional input to a guard held at P1.

The live-coordinator guard, which the test notes fires BEFORE any table row is read and comes from the policy input rather than from the loop-state record. A deferred AskUserQuestion or a parked Wait that the coordinator still tracks would otherwise have its own call cut out from under it while the answer is in flight. P1 — a separate input and a separate ordering claim from the loop-state guards.

An owed continuation blocks the cut. Compacting while a continuation is outstanding discards the state the continuation was going to resume from, and this fires above the hard threshold, so it outranks pressure. P1 for the unsafe-state row.

The hard row: at tokens plus reserve equal to the window the policy compacts, for the hard reason, with the target computed as TargetRatio over the usable window. That target is what the cut selector is then asked to reach, so it is part of the decision rather than a report of it. P1.

The same precedence against the other two vetoes at once: a hot cache and deliberately unprofitable economics (a 1000-per-million cache-write rate) must not stop a compaction the window requires. Cost is a reason to defer a discretionary compaction and never a reason to overflow. P1.

The first of the two cross-row precedences the spec names: at the hard threshold the cooldown does not apply. Cooldown exists to stop thrash, but honouring it here would let the conversation overflow the window instead — which is a broken turn, not a wasted compaction. P1.

Cooldown by generation ordinal, with the remaining count reported in the summary. This is what stops the policy compacting on consecutive turns and paying the summarisation cost repeatedly for nothing. The reported remainder is what a caller shows instead of warning again. P1.

The second, independent cooldown condition: too little new context since the last checkpoint. Generations elapsing is not enough on its own — recompacting a conversation that has barely grown re-summarises what was already summarised. A distinct condition, not a variation of the ordinal one. P1.

The release case: with the ordinal reached and the new-token floor met, the policy compacts. Without it an implementation that simply always reported Cooldown would pass both cooldown tests above, so this is what makes them non-vacuous. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 1 exclusive product span, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The rewrite term with caching ON: re-caching the target prefix outweighs three generations of reuse, the savings are asserted negative, and the row declines. This is the term that turns a compaction from a saving into a cost, and omitting it would make every cached conversation compact at a loss. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 1 exclusive product span, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The discretionary row: at 0.80 utilization with a cold cache the policy compacts for the economic reason, and the reported utilization matches. This is the decision that runs on the vast majority of conversations, long before any hard threshold. P1.

The second cross-row case the spec names: a hot prefix cache defers an economic compaction, because cutting invalidates the cache and the rewrite costs more than the discretionary saving. The temperature is echoed in the summary so the deferral is explicable. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The savings formula itself, computed independently in the test from the spec terms — reuse over expected future generations, minus the summarisation cost, minus the rewrite term which is zero with caching off — and asserted to the exact micro. Every economic decision in this table is a comparison against this number, so a formula that drifts moves them all at once while each individual row still looks right. P1.

Savings that are genuinely POSITIVE but below a raised floor still skip. That combination is what pins the comparison as being against MinPredictedSavingsMicros rather than against zero — an implementation testing only the sign passes every other economic row here and fails this one. P1 as the distinguishing case for the floor.

Both directions for a model with no rates at all: it cannot clear a floor of 1, and it still compacts under the default floor of 0. Treating an unpriced model as unprofitable would silently disable compaction for every model missing from the price catalog, which is the ordinary state of a newly released one. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The warn row at 0.70: no compaction, a warning, and the utilization that justifies it. This is the only notice a caller gets before the discretionary row starts cutting. P1.

Below the warn ratio the policy does nothing and reports no reason at all. The quiet row is a real requirement: a policy that warned here would warn on every ordinary conversation and the signal would stop meaning anything. P1.

Shadow mode reports Shadow with the underlying reason and still answers IsCompact true, so a shadow deployment can be measured without acting. If shadow ever actually compacted, the evaluation rollout would rewrite live conversations. P1 for the rollout-safety projection.
Passthrough of tokens, window, reserve, temperature, and the decision and reason already asserted on the decision itself. Diagnostics over rows held at P1 elsewhere in this table. P2.

Warn mode turns a Compact verdict into a Warn while KEEPING the reason that produced it. The preserved reason is the whole point — it is how an operator evaluating the policy sees which row would have fired. P1 for the mode projection.

The rollout dial, run through a real loop: the exact provider/model route enables compaction, the bare model id enables it everywhere, ANOTHER route's entry leaves this one alone, and the exact route wins over the model id — including lowering a global Compact to Off. A key-matching mistake here turns a canary into a fleet-wide enablement, and the negative rows check the whole shape of Off (no state, no policy run, no envelope). P1.
uncertainties: No row in this file is an inP0Prefix member, so no P0 is proposed here.

Every row in this file is P1: each pins a different rollout control or failure cause with its own recorded reason, and the shared 'the raw request still goes out' assertion is the availability property each cause must independently preserve rather than a repeated claim. Recorded rather than forcing a P2 quota.

rationale: The stale-watermark race through a real loop rather than the pipeline in isolation: a foreign writer appends while the summary is in flight, that checkpoint is rejected and NOTHING is activated, the turn still succeeds on the raw history, the next attempt lands cleanly, and the row sequence stays unique and ascending through all of it. The unit-level rejection cannot show that the loop keeps serving the user afterwards. P1.

A summariser outage must not cost the user their turn: the run completes on the raw history, nothing is activated, no checkpoint row is appended, and a CompactionFailed lifecycle event carries the typed summary_call_failed reason so the failure is visible to operators rather than only to the log. P1.

Both kill switches — the config flag and two spellings of the environment variable — stop compaction while the policy STILL RUNS and records Skipped/Disabled, so the kill is visible in the audit rather than silent. No checkpoint row is ever appended and no envelope reaches the provider. A kill switch that also silences the decision record leaves an operator unable to confirm it took effect. P1.

Downgrade safety on live state: an older binary meeting a schema-version-2 state blob writes no checkpoint AND preserves the blob BYTE FOR BYTE, including a field it does not understand. Half-interpreting it would let this build overwrite a newer build's active checkpoint pointer with its own partial reading. Rank 176 with 7 marginal spans. P1.

The three-phase rollback story, and the reason the feature can be switched off in production: after compacting, turning the feature off sends the RAW history again with every covered row back in the request and no checkpoint row leaking into a provider message (the OpenAI converter rejects unknown types), while no persisted row is rewritten or dropped and the audit state is preserved untouched — and switching it back on ADOPTS the retained checkpoint instead of rebuilding it. Rank 177. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 7 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: §8.3: rows handed back without a sequence number — an older binary's rows before the backfill, or a reader that lost it — cannot be cut safely, so the loop records UnsafeState and keeps sending the raw history. Cutting on rows it cannot address by seq would hide a boundary nobody can locate again. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 3 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The hard band ignores economics: a model with no rate card still compacts, because the band exists to keep the request inside the context window, and the cost is reported Unavailable with a null figure rather than as zero. Gating the safety compaction on pricing would let an unpriced model overflow its window; reporting zero would understate a real spend. Rank 194. P1.

The same guard at the second window — between commit and the checkpoint row landing — where the row's own seq is the evidence. Rejected, and nothing becomes active. A separate window from :115 with its own arithmetic, pinned by asserting the concurrent row took seq 4. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 1 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Crash-and-retry idempotence on both writes: a repeated commit changes nothing, not even the timestamp; a repeated activation returns the same state; and a retry after a second row exists is refused by the same guard rather than re-run. History stays a single entry. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 1 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Prepare, Validated, Committed, row, Active — each state read back through a FRESH handle, so 'durably distinguishable' means what it says. Also pins that nothing is active until the checkpoint row exists, which is the invariant every reconciliation row below depends on. P1.
uncertainties: No row in this file is an inP0Prefix member, so no P0 is proposed here.
Every row in this file is a Theory over all store flavours, and nearly every one is a distinct crash window or guard rather than a variation, which is why P2 is almost absent here.

rationale: Bounded history that trims the OLDEST REJECTED entries and never the active one — driven past the bound by design. Trimming the active entry would leave the state pointing at a checkpoint it can no longer describe, which is unrecoverable rather than merely lossy. Fifteen exclusive spans. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 15 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: Downgrade safety: a runtime that cannot interpret schema 2 reads the state as ABSENT and every mutation becomes a no-op, with the raw stored payload asserted byte-for-byte afterwards. Without it, one older process in a rolling deployment silently destroys a newer one's checkpoint state. P1.

At most one checkpoint in flight: preparing a second abandons the first with a typed reason rather than leaving two candidates racing to activate. The InFlight set is asserted, not just the entry statuses. P1.

The crash between the row append and the activation write: canonical history wins and the checkpoint is activated on restart, with the row's seq and boundary recovered. Without it a perfectly good summary stays committed-but-never-active forever and the conversation grows unbounded. The widest sole-cover in the file (rank 66, 31 new spans). P1.
uncertainties: Holds 4 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The crash between commit and the row append reaches the same RowMissing rejection that :386 holds with exclusive spans by a different route. P2.

Reconciliation identifies the row, it does not merely count to watermark+1: an ordinary message sitting where the checkpoint row would be is a rejection, not an activation. Activating on a foreign row would point the boundary at an arbitrary message. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 2 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: A validation rejection records its typed reason, leaves the active and last-known-good pointers alone, and — the invariant that matters most — a TERMINAL entry does not move again: a later commit finds it still Rejected. Reviving a rejected checkpoint would activate a summary validation had already refused. P1.

The recovery ladder in one body: a chained checkpoint supersedes its predecessor, a rollback falls back to the last known good with its boundary restored, a second rollback lands on raw history, and a third changes nothing. This is what the loop does when a compacted view still overflows — landing on the wrong rung serves the model a summary that was already rejected. P1.
uncertainties: Holds 3 exclusive product spans, so the P1 floor applies.

rationale: The watermark guard at its first checkpoint: a row appended while the summariser was running means the summary no longer describes the conversation, so the commit is rejected with a typed reason. A live cp-0 is set up first so the row can show the VIEW was untouched, not merely that cp-1 was refused — committing a stale summary hides turns from the model permanently. P1.

Both readers on a thread that was never observed return null and empty rather than throwing. Catches a reader that requires the metadata key to exist, which would make every first context read on a new conversation fail. P2: the absent-state boundary.

A generation observed twice — estimated before dispatch, measured once the provider's usage arrives — occupies ONE ring entry, and the measured figure wins in both the history and the latest pointer. The comment names the real sequence, which is the normal path rather than an edge: every generation is observed twice. Appending instead would halve the ring's effective depth and, worse, leave the latest pointer showing whichever write landed last rather than the better measurement. Catches double-counted generations and an estimated figure outranking a measured one. P1: the one-entry-per-generation rule and measurement precedence.
uncertainties: The name says 'at the ring tail' and the scenario only re-records the newest generation. Whether an older generation elsewhere in the ring is replaced or appended is not covered by this row.

rationale: One generation has two independent writers — the loop stamps the measurement, the policy stamps its decision — and neither carries the other's fields. The row proves the merge holds in BOTH orders: after the measurement lands, the decision and active checkpoint are still there; after the policy writes again, the measured token count and provenance are still there. Testing both directions is what makes this a lost-update guard rather than a last-writer-wins check, and the two orders really do occur because the writers race on every generation. The consequence of a blanking write is quiet: the record still exists and still reads as a valid observation, so the report shows an estimated figure where a measured one was taken, or a decision-free generation the policy did in fact rule on. The trailing ContainSingle assertion also fixes that three writes describing one generation stay one ring entry rather than accumulating. Catches a silent lost update between two concurrent authors of the same row. P1: the merge contract, and the strongest row in this class.
requirements: in-process only; ConversationStoreHarness, sequential writes only
uncertainties: The two authors are exercised sequentially, not concurrently. The row pins the MERGE rule in both orders, which is the substantive part, but it does not exercise the interleaving that produces the race in the first place.

Was a Compaction P0 contender on a lost-update argument. Resolved after reading all six Compaction classes: the nomination went to ProviderCheckpointSummarizerTests.SummarizeAsync_Throws_WhenTheReplyHasNoJsonObject, because an empty manifest becomes the context the agent ACTS on, whereas a lost update here produces a wrong figure on a report nobody acts on directly. This row stays P1 with no nomination.

rationale: Five observations into a ring of three leave exactly ordinals 3, 4, 5 in that order, with the latest pointer at 5. The bound is the point: the ring lives inside thread metadata that is rewritten on every observation, so an unbounded history would grow the metadata blob for the whole life of a long conversation and make every context read progressively more expensive. Asserting the ORDER as well as the membership is what makes the history usable as a trend rather than an unordered bag. Catches an unbounded or wrongly ordered ring. P1: the retention bound, a distinct behaviour from replacement.
uncertainties: historyLength is passed explicitly as 3; the DEFAULT ring length the production callers get is not pinned by any row in this class.

rationale: Metadata already holding a schema_version 2 ring and latest pointer survives a write from this (version 1) binary byte for byte, and the readers return null and empty rather than misparsing it. Both halves are load-bearing. Preserving the bytes is what stops an older host — a rolled-back deployment, or a second process on the same store — from permanently destroying observations a newer one wrote, which is unrecoverable rather than merely wrong. Reading as ABSENT rather than throwing or half-parsing is what keeps that old host usable instead of crashing on every context read. Catches forward-incompatible clobbering of durable state. P1: the schema-forward-compatibility contract.

An observation with every field populated is written, then read back through a FRESH handle on every store flavour and compared field by field, with the derived utilization recomputed against the window minus reserve. The fresh handle is what makes this durability rather than an in-memory echo. The raw-metadata assertion is the sharper one: provenance must be persisted as the NAME 'Measured', not an ordinal, because an ordinal silently remaps the moment anyone inserts an enum member and every historical row then reads as the wrong provenance with no error. Catches both a field that never survives the round trip and a persistence format that decays as the code evolves. P1: the durable round-trip contract for the observation row.
requirements: in-process only; all store kinds via ConversationStoreHarness

rationale: The temperature rule as a pure function, pinned at its boundary: four minutes into a five-minute TTL is Hot, exactly five minutes is Cold because the boundary is EXCLUSIVE, six minutes is Cold, no activity at all is Cold because nothing is cached, and caching disabled is Unknown regardless of how recent the activity is. This is the only row in the lane that fixes the threshold itself — ConversationContextReportTests exercises the same rule an hour out, which proves the direction but would pass under any TTL. Asserting the exact boundary is what stops the comparison drifting between inclusive and exclusive, and separating Unknown from Cold is what stops a cacheless loop being reported as an expired cache. Catches an off-by-one at the TTL edge and a collapsed Unknown. P1: the cache-temperature rule at its decision points.
requirements: in-process only; pure function, no store

rationale: Last activity is the newest of FOUR independent durable sources, proven by advancing them one at a time — metadata, then a newer row, then a newer run-ledger update, then a terminal run — and re-reading through a fresh handle after each. The class states the point exactly: the activity a cache temperature derives from must come from durable state and never from anything a process remembers.
