The primary externalisation path; asserting the sidecar's bytes and the line's size together is what shows the content moved rather than being duplicated.

After a retitle, replaying every rename over the path a written reference names leaves that path unchanged. Stated as 'the reference still resolves' rather than as an argv assertion, which is the property a reader depends on and the one an argv check cannot see: references are stamped at write time and nothing rewrites a line, so relocating the sidecar hollows out the record.

The single-call tool-result type name externalises as well as the aggregate one, with the two names proven distinct first. The gate matches NAMES rather than types, so the second entry is load-bearing and nothing else in the suite drives it - every other sidecar test uses the plural spelling.

A sub-agent line's reference is anchored at the conversation root even though the line lives one level down in _agents, asserted both by the path written and by the path NOT written. The two plausible anchors differ only for these files and a reader that guesses wrong sees a missing payload rather than an error.

A tool result weighing EXACTLY the threshold is externalised, with the fixture's byte count measured rather than assumed. The one case no other sidecar test reaches, since they all use the threshold plus a margin: a comparison drifting from < to <= leaves every one of them green while the documented boundary means its opposite.

A small tool result stays inline with a null ref and no sidecar write. The below-threshold boundary that keeps the externalisation from being unconditional; the threshold's decisive edge is pinned by the exactly-at-threshold row.

A thread whose sandbox binding was created by an S2S caller gets its transcript written. The background mirror holds no credential, so a raw null-vs-app-id comparison in the registry produced CredentialConflict on every flush forever with no retry that could ever win - an unbounded failure rather than a transient one.

An untitled conversation writes under its bare short id with no leading separator and no invented 'untitled' literal. A naming boundary extending the leaf contract; the S2S case is the ordinary one for a headless caller.

A brand-new writer finds its own file under a stale slug through the directory listing and adopts it by the same move the warm path uses, BEFORE the watermark tail runs. Distinct from the warm retitle: adopting the current title outright splits the conversation into a frozen old file and a second one restarting from zero, with the old _agents directory orphaned beside the wrong name.

With a three-megabyte row on disk the probe's output stays under 4 KiB and the watermark is still found. The bound is asserted in bytes the gateway would have carried, driven through a simulation of the real shell semantics rather than a hand-written window - which is what lets it see that an uncapped tail hands back megabytes, throws at the command-output cap, and wedges every cold start until the retry budget is spent.

A listing that FAILS defers with nothing written and no command issued, and the recovered flush adopts the file that was there all along. The listing is the cold writer's only route to the file it owns, so reading a transport fault as 'nothing to adopt' produces the split transcript permanently - the second file IS the computed leaf from then on, so adoption never runs again.

A non-zero probe exit that is not the private absence code defers, and the recovered flush then reports UpToDate with nothing appended. The exit-code half of the same discrimination, and the reason the probe cannot be a bare tail: GNU tail answers a missing file, an unreadable one and an I/O error with the same status 1. Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 50): inside the greedy front that reaches the 80% target, with 10 spans nothing else covers. Promoted from P1 on that basis. TASK-1 AUDIT: prefix candidate DECLINED to P1. Probe exit-code discrimination is important failure handling on a derived mirror artifact and the duplicated transcript is visible in the output rather than silent; "Promoted from P1 on that basis" cites rank 50. Its 10 exclusive spans hold the P1 floor.

A probe that THREW defers with nothing staged and no splice attempted, and the same writer then appends the history exactly once when the gateway recovers. Reading a transport fault as absence sends the start index to zero, so a host restarting in a loop multiplies the transcript indefinitely; the recovery half is what proves the deferral cost nothing.

When the file ends mid-record the writer refuses the last line's uid as a watermark and re-appends that row in full. Distinct from every other probe branch and the only one whose alternative is LOSS rather than duplication: truncation makes a torn line look like a good row, so exit 43 is the only remaining discriminator.

A window whose watermark line was cut to 256 characters still yields its uid, because the serializer pins schema_version, type then uid at the front of every row. The other half of the per-line cap: a whole-document parse would fail on every truncated line, report no intact record, and re-append the entire history onto a file that already holds it.

A cold writer recovers its watermark from a five-line tail window whose last line is torn, appends only the suffix, and never issues a GET. The five-line window rather than one is the mechanism: a run killed mid-splice must still resolve to the last INTACT record instead of re-appending the whole history.

A listed name containing ../ passes every other filter (typed File, not lossy, .jsonl, correct short-id stem) and is ignored: no argv and no write path anywhere contains '..', and it is not adopted OR renamed onto. The adopted leaf is the one path component this type does not compute, and .. is a real directory rather than a symlink so the ancestor walk passes it - the transcript would land outside the .gitignore at exit 0.

A typed NotFound listing is a definite miss and proceeds as an ordinary first flush. The non-vacuity partner of the deferral row: without it, deferring on every listing failure would leave every new conversation spinning its retry budget.

The private exit 42 means a DEFINITE absence and is treated as an ordinary first flush, so the whole history goes down. The non-vacuity partner of the two deferral rows: without it, deferring on every probe failure would leave every brand-new conversation spinning its retry budget and never writing a line.

Every line parses and carries message_json_ref, uid and parent_uid whether or not the ref is populated, with exactly one of three rows proven externalised. The key set being fixed is the compatibility clause: emitting the field only when populated would give a columnar reader two schemas for one file.

Under a title containing $(touch ...) and rm -rf, EVERY shell call the writer emits runs one of four compile-time-constant scripts with the title-derived path as a positional parameter, and no script text contains any fragment of the title. P0 as the component's injection boundary: the file leaf comes from a user-authored title, so interpolating it would make a title executable inside the workspace container. The closing OnlyContain assertion is what makes the coverage total rather than partial. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Outside the project's 80% greedy P0 prefix and carrying no named exception - the contract argued here is a distinct primary behaviour, a distinguishing/non-vacuity partner of another row, or a component/class baseline, and the rubric's outside-prefix exception applies only where a component would otherwise have no P0 pinning its essential contract. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

A failed main append skips the fan-out entirely, and after recovery the child's first line chains off a row that genuinely exists. The one failure in the pipeline that retrying cannot repair: an anchor is resolved once and pinned for the file's life, so a fan-out beside a failed append pins every descendant to null and the conversation is never one lineage again.

A failed mv keeps this flush writing to the old complete path, retries next flush, and appends nothing extra once the move lands. The watermark being keyed by THREAD rather than by path is what makes the retry free; a path-keyed one would re-append the whole file after every successful rename.

A non-zero splice leaves the watermark unadvanced, so the next flush stages the identical payload again. The failure DIRECTION is the contract - duplicate on retry, never silent loss - and it is asserted by comparing the two staged payloads byte for byte rather than by a status.

The first flush stages the exact projected bytes at the .part path and issues exactly four commands in order - containment guard, watermark probe, staging guard, splice - with every argv pinned. Chosen as this component's baseline P0 because it drives the whole write pipeline in one path and asserts the BYTES and the ARGV rather than call counts, which is the only level at which a reader's uid dedupe and parent_uid chaining can be checked at all. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

A reasoning row survives the projection whole and round-trips back to a ReasoningMessage with its text intact. The deliberate divergence from every other transcript reader, which filters reasoning: this mirror writes into the conversation's own workspace, so full fidelity is the contract rather than an oversight.

When the containment write fails, nothing is staged and nothing is spliced - twice running - and only once it succeeds does the first transcript byte go down, in that order. P0 as the confidentiality invariant of the whole feature: the workspace is often a git checkout and an agent often runs git add -A, so unredacted reasoning on disk with no .gitignore covering it publishes the conversation off-machine. Ordering rather than retrying is what makes the guarantee unconditional against an exhausted budget or a process that exits between the two calls. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

With no rows on the root and a finished child, containment still precedes the descendant's first byte. A distinct reachability claim: both of the flush's brakes are keyed to the MAIN conversation, so the ordering has to be enforced inside the shared append path rather than at a call site, and a sub-agent's reasoning is no less publishable than the root's.

Containment is attempted on a flush that appends NOTHING, covering a transcript an earlier process left behind. Ordering alone covers only what this process writes; tying the attempt to 'this flush wrote rows' leaves an inherited transcript uncovered forever, and a failed attempt is retried rather than accepted as a resting state.
The ignore file is written exactly once across two flushes, with contents '*'. A frequency-and-content boundary on the containment contract whose ordering guarantee is the P0.

No sandbox session yields Unavailable with nothing written, no command issued, and exactly one Debug line. The log LEVEL is the assertion: a non-sandbox conversation is the ordinary case, so warning on it would make the mirror's real warnings unreadable.

A conversation with no bound workspace is settled by the metadata read alone and never reaches the gateway. A short-circuit boundary on the no-session outcome already represented. Raised to the P1 exclusive-span floor (rubric line 46): a front member with exclusive spans cannot sit below P1, and this row is not vacuous.

A sub-agent seeded after the first flush is invisible until NoteExternalTrigger's sibling NoteSubAgentActivity runs, then mirrored. The second trigger is the whole contract: a child finishing after its parent's turn never publishes a run completion, so a mirror listening only for that would never write its file.

When the SDK cannot release a completed command's operation record, the writer warns once per session and drops to Debug for every later occurrence, with several commands proven to have run. The cadence IS the contract: the original outage produced 1508 identical warnings from this one call site, which is how the real signal went unread.

A retitle renames the file and the _agents directory BEFORE anything is appended, with all four commands and their argv pinned in order. The ordering is the contract: a retitle reaches the mirror only through metadata, so appending first creates a second file and re-appends the entire history.

A retitle's moves are exactly the file and the _agents directory, and no shell argument anywhere mentions the blobs suffix. The mechanical half of the sidecar-stranding invariant, said twice so a rename of the helper methods cannot hide a third move; the asymmetry is deliberate because _agents is found by walking while blobs are addressed by written references.

When a new row lands between every pair of stability reads, the flush defers with nothing written and no command issued. The blocker the whole pipeline is built around: history is persisted on discarded unawaited tasks, so appending a truncated list would also land the late row at the tail next flush with a parent_uid pointing at a row it did not follow.

A row that lands during the first read and then stops changing is written in full. The non-vacuity partner of the never-settle row: a probe giving up after one disagreement would truncate the very turn that triggered it.

A second flush appends only the new run's bytes and the distinct uid count across both flushes equals the line count. The watermark being the last appended uid rather than a byte offset is the distinct claim, and the uid uniqueness is the property a reader's dedupe rests on.

A capped pass mirrors one descendant, reports Progressing, covers the rest next flush, then reports UpToDate with no commands at all. The three distinct outcomes are the contract: reporting Deferred on a capped pass spends the caller's FAILURE budget where nothing failed, capping how far one trigger reaches into a large roster.

A change to a descendant OUTSIDE the current slice is still mirrored, because a capped pass whose own slice is current keeps asking. Distinct from the bounded-fan-out row: stopping on the first already-current capped pass ends one step short and the changed descendant's pass never runs, and no cursor ordering avoids it without reading.

Each sub-agent gets its own file - a null name falling back to agent-{shortId}, two agents sharing a display name still landing distinctly - and every file's first line hangs off the main file's watermark, with all five uids distinct across the set. The primary fan-out behaviour, asserted on paths AND bytes so a reader concatenating the whole set still resolves one chain.

With a roster of sixteen and a cap of eight, one transient splice failure still ends with every descendant's transcript written. Marking a descendant covered when it is PICKED rather than when it is written loses it silently and completely - the failing flush did say Deferred and the retry it asked for did run - and the pass bound doubles as a hang detector on a writer that never stops asking.

Each splice observes exactly its own staged write and no later file's, asserted as the sequence 1,2,3. A hard sequencing requirement rather than a style preference: every file stages through ONE temp path, so an interleaved fan-out would PUT over its own bytes and cat the survivor into both destinations.

Over a three-descendant roster with a cap of one, the chain terminates once the sweep has visited everything and never reports Deferred. The termination boundary of the keep-asking rule already represented; asserted only as NotBe on two outcomes.
uncertainties: Every assertion is a negative on one outcome value, so several wrong outcomes would still pass

rationale: Sub-agents of an S2S root land under the _agents directory. A combination of the S2S resolution fix and the fan-out, both already represented; it proves the fan-out is reached once the root resolves.

A real foreign caller presenting a non-owner credential is still refused with CredentialConflict and the owner's app id. The explicit non-vacuity partner of the S2S row: without it the fix could have been implemented by removing the cross-actor guard, letting one app read another app's session.

rationale: A resolve that throws and a credential conflict each warn exactly ONCE, write nothing, and let the next flush append the full deferred history after rebind. Both the once-ness and the recovery matter: the mirror must never propagate a failure into the run, and must not lose the rows it deferred.

A log-cardinality bound rather than a dedup nicety: unknown model ids come from templates and are effectively an unbounded space, so warning per DISTINCT id would let a misconfigured fleet emit an unbounded number of warnings and, depending on the dedup implementation, retain an unbounded set of seen ids. The inheritance path, which is the resource-conscious one: when the sub-agent's model IS the parent's copilot model, the parent agent is reused by reference and NOT owned, while the effort metadata is still shaped for the transport. The resolver's central algorithm in one arrangement: walk the tier's candidates in order and take the first that is both present in the catalog and ROUTABLE. rationale: P0 baseline for the deferred-auth hold. Two concurrent waits on the same provider must share ONE pending entry, prompt the user exactly once, both receive the token when it appears, signal completion exactly once, and never also deny. It subsumes the single-waiter resolve path and adds the coalescing contract on top, and the exactly-once claims are the ones that carry it: an implementation holding one entry per waiter prompts N times for one sign-in, and one that signalled completion per waiter would re-dismiss the banner repeatedly. The empty-denied assertion additionally rules out a hold that both grants a token and reports a denial. Prefix member at greedy rank 42 with 82 new spans and 6 exclusive.
A sign-in failure arriving AFTER the hold began denies immediately instead of waiting out the full 30-second timeout. Greedy rank 398 with 3 exclusive spans.

A cancelled hold throws OperationCanceledException, leaves no pending entry, signals no completion, and still sends the denial that dismisses the prompt. Pins that the abort path cleans up rather than leaking an entry that would suppress the prompt for every later call on that provider.

An expired hold returns null, sends the terminal auth_denied frame so the client banner dismisses, and leaves no pending entry behind. Without the terminal frame the user is left with a prompt that never resolves. Greedy rank 209 with 2 exclusive spans.

A zero hold timeout returns null without prompting and without a terminal frame, because disabled deferral returns before entering a hold at all. Distinct from the expired-hold declaration, which must send the frame. Greedy rank 492 with 2 exclusive spans.

A stale Failed status carried into the call must NOT deny the hold - the wait stays open and still resolves when a token appears. This is the case that distinguishes the fresh-failure declaration from a coordinator that denies on any Failed status at all, which would pass that one and silently refuse every user with a prior abandoned sign-in. Held at P1 as the distinguishing half of the pair despite 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

The snapshot exposes the pending hold's provider and sign-in url while it is open, and is empty once it resolves. P2 as a variation: the snapshot's population and its cleanup are already asserted by the timeout and cancellation declarations, and the two fields it names duplicate the auth_required tuple pinned above. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

A token appearing while the hold is open resolves the wait with that token, and the auth_required notification carries the exact provider, sign-in path and reason tuple. The tuple equality is the part the concurrency baseline does not assert - it only counts the notifications - so a prompt naming the wrong provider or carrying an empty reason fails here alone.

The create-side reservation race - a second create is held in flight on a gated handler while the credential's other session is destroyed, so the reservation is what keeps the shared client from being disposed out from under an in-flight POST. Two credentials produce two cached clients, destroying the last session under one evicts it, and a later create under the evicted credential re-adds a fresh entry. Without the eviction the cache grows monotonically with credential rotation, and without the re-add the second half of the rotation would find a hole. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

The refcount-above-one case, which is where a naive destroy-then-dispose breaks: the first destroy must leave the shared entry alive, and it is proven alive by making a real gateway call on the surviving session rather than by the count alone. The count-only version of this assertion would pass against a disposed transport still present in the dictionary. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

After the rolled-back attempt the store is repaired and the retry creates a FRESH session - post count 2, sess-2 present, sess-1 still absent. Pins that the faulted single-flight evicted and recreated cleanly rather than caching the fault or reusing the destroyed session, which the rollback declaration alone cannot fail on. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

When the secret persist fails after the gateway create succeeded, the failure propagates, the remote session is best-effort destroyed and the reverse session-id map entry is rolled back - three assertions that together rule out a silently half-built session. The failure is injected by replacing the secret directory with a FILE, which is scheme-independent and lands exactly in the post-create window rather than depending on the file-name hashing. The create request is parsed off the wire and the per-session secret must ride under the exact JSON field the gateway reads, must equal THIS session's saved secret, and the legacy field name must be absent. The gateway deserializes that field with a serde default, so a wrong name is not an error anywhere - it parses as absent, the callbacks go out with no authorization, and every discovery webhook is rejected. Three assertions and the negative one is the load-bearing one. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

A digest reporting intermediate states injects a false account of the board into every subscribed conversation; every other row asserts only who was notified or whether anything was. That output contract makes it P0. Coverage records prefix membership, rank 7, 422 marginal and 5 exclusive spans; rank is supporting evidence only.

Construction over a populated board digests nothing, and the first real change afterwards reports only that change with no added lines. The second assertion is the load-bearing one: baseline suppression must come from remembering the hydrated rows, since a service that started empty would announce every pre-existing task as newly added on the first change of every conversation.

Two changes that cancel inside one window deliver nothing, and the same service then digests a real change - so the silence is a decision rather than a dead timer. That second half is what makes this more than an absence assertion; important failure handling on the diff, at P1.
One of the two option gates, asserted on the delivery list: with the primary digest disabled the assignee digest is unaffected. A configuration variation over the represented delivery contract.

The audience rule when the assignee's own conversation IS the root: the primary digest still fires and the assignee is skipped rather than duplicated, so the root does not receive the same change twice. Coverage: rank 616 with 2 exclusive spans, which holds the P1 floor.

The other half of the debounce contract: the window re-opens after a flush and the second digest reports only the second window's change. Without it a service that never re-arms digests exactly once and falls silent for the rest of the conversation, which every single-window row here would still pass.

A combination of the represented subtree rule and per-assignee delivery: a child assigned to agent-b that also lies under agent-a's task notifies both. Extends the prefix-membership contract to an overlapping-ownership shape rather than establishing a new one.

The subtree scoping primary contract: an assigned agent hears a change to a grandchild of its own task and a sibling branch's assignee hears nothing. Membership by dotted-path prefix rather than assignee equality is the whole design, and getting it wrong either silences an agent about its own work or shows it another agent's.

The mutation pin for the prefix guard: membership is id == root or id starts with root + '.', so dropping the appended dot makes '11'.StartsWith('1') true and leaks task 11's change to task 1's assignee. Carries its own positive control in the same body, so the negative cannot pass because assignee digests are off. Coverage: rank 56 with 59 marginal and 7 exclusive spans.

The window is fixed, not sliding: a change landing inside an open window rides the same flush rather than re-arming the timer. Distinct from coalescing - a sliding re-arm still coalesces, it just never flushes while the board keeps changing, so an actively-edited board goes silent indefinitely. Coverage: rank 185 with 10 marginal spans.

With a resolver reporting display name reviewer for agent-3, the primary digest says assigned to reviewer, claimed by reviewer and assignee reviewer across assign, claim and add-with-assignee, and never says agent-3. The digest line is read by the primary conversation, which addresses agents by name, and this is the third writer of that vocabulary after the board's receipts and list-tasks; an ordinal here re-teaches the id the rest of the branch removed. P1.

The per-agent digest is DELIVERED to agent-3, the identity the transport keys on, while its text says claimed by reviewer. Both halves in one test on purpose: a fix that made the text right by renaming the delivery target would route the digest to a name the transport does not know, and the sibling text-only row could not see it. P1: the split between address and vocabulary at the digest's delivery seam.

Every nudge but the assignment notice ships off, each with a stated reason - root-conversation poking needs an explicit opt-in, and the stall pump must not exist under shipped defaults. A default flipped the other way auto-pokes the user's main chat on a build nobody configured. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

The section EXISTS but holds nothing - the empty-array binder trap, where a present-but-empty section is a different state from an absent one and an existence-based guard reads it as configured. Existence must not move a single default. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

With all four flags off both derived predicates go false, which is the gate the host uses to skip registering the service entirely. The distinguishing case for the disjunction - a predicate hard-coded true passes the defaults and explicit declarations and fails only here. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

All seven configured values land, including the assignment notice being turned OFF and both derived predicates recomputed. The non-vacuity partner for every reads-as-defaults declaration here, all four of which a reader returning defaults unconditionally would pass. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

Garbage values across four keys - a non-boolean, a numeric one, a non-numeric threshold and a negative duration - all fall back rather than throwing or landing negative. A different mechanism from the absent-section declarations: here the keys are present and the coercion is what must not fail. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.

A configuration holding only unrelated keys reads as defaults. P2 as a variation on the null-configuration and empty-section declarations, which pin the same outcome from the two harder starting states. 0 marginal and 0 exclusive spans.
A null configuration reads as defaults rather than throwing. Greedy rank 465 with 2 exclusive spans.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 433): 3 marginal and 3 exclusive spans on the refused-delivery arm. Important failure handling at the boundary the service does not control: the sink can decline - the target conversation may be gone or busy - and a refusal must not spend budget, or an agent whose first nudge could not be delivered silently loses a third of the nudges it was owed. Distinguishes attempts from acceptances with two separate counters, which is what makes the claim checkable at all: DeliveryAttempts 3 against Delivered 2 says the refusal happened AND was not charged, where a single counter could not tell the two apart.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 690): 1 exclusive span - the switch's unmatched arm. A fail-loud discipline pin: the target-allowed switch must throw on an enum value nobody mapped, rather than defaulting to allow (nudging a target kind whose policy was never decided) or to deny (dropping nudges for a whole new target kind with no signal). Both silent defaults are plausible ways to write it and both would ship a policy nobody chose; this makes adding an enum member a compile-or-crash decision instead.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 604): 2 exclusive spans. A separate suppression clause from the transition rule, keyed on who acted rather than on what changed: a claim sets the assignee too, but the agent did it, and telling an agent what it just did is noise injected into its own context. Nothing else in the file covers the claim path's notice suppression, and the defect would fire on every claim in the product.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 106): 22 marginal spans - the sub-item-under-an-assigned-parent path. A distinct suppression rule rather than a restatement of the transition predicate: sub-items created under an assigned task INHERIT the assignee, so they are the assignee's own breakdown and not a dispatch. Strictly stronger than the unrelated-board-change case, because a predicate keyed on "a row with an assignee appeared" passes that one and fails this one. Without it, decomposing a task notifies the agent once per sub-item it just created.

Important failure handling around a lifecycle event the service does not control: FromSnapshot restores assignees (#590), so a recreate or a restart must not re-notify every pre-existing assignee - which would be a notification burst proportional to board size on every restart. Seeding BEFORE Build() is exactly the hydrated-baseline shape rather than a stand-in for it. Reads as a pair with AssignmentNotice_StillFires_ForAGenuineAssignmentAfterHydration, and that pairing is load-bearing: on its own this test is satisfied by a service that suppresses everything.

Additional variation on the transition predicate: a standing assignment must not re-notify when some unrelated row is added. Its stated purpose - catching a predicate broadened from "assignee CHANGED" to "task HAS an assignee" - is also caught by AssignmentNotice_DoesNotFire_ForANewRowBornWithAnAssignee, which arranges the same standing assignment and additionally covers the inherited-assignee case, so it fails on a strict superset of defects. Kept as the simplest statement of the rule; not the row to run first.

The N1 positive, and the only test in the file that asserts the MESSAGE rather than the count: target, notify kind, label, and three separate substrings of the detail including the tool name the recipient is meant to call. Everything else in the assignment family is a suppression rule, so without this one a service that never notified anybody would pass all of them. Carries its own internal negative in the first three lines - adding an unassigned task delivers nothing - which is what makes the single delivery afterwards attributable to the assignment rather than to the board changing at all. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

A cross-tier contract nothing else covers: an N1 assignment notice must not spend any of the two stall nudges, so an agent that was just dispatched still gets its full budget if it then goes quiet. Arranged so the miscount is visible - one notice followed by three run-ends must yield exactly three deliveries, and a service that charged the notice to the budget yields two. Easy to break by accident, because both tiers deliver through the same sink and the obvious counter is the sink.

The non-vacuity half of the hydration guardrail, and its comment states the argument exactly: baseline suppression must come from REMEMBERING the hydrated state, not from forgetting it, because a service that starts with an empty baseline also passes the no-refire test and yet silently swallows this legitimate dispatch. That swallow is the worse of the two failures - a missing notice looks like an agent that simply did not pick up its work - and this is the only test that catches it. Asserts the target and the task id, so a notice fired for the wrong row does not satisfy it.

Additional variation: the N1 tier's copy of the root-conversation opt-in, which the N3 and stall tiers already hold at P1 - and both of those assert BOTH directions in one body, while this one only asserts that nothing is delivered with the opt-in off. Raised to the P1 exclusive-span floor (rubric line 46): a front member with exclusive spans cannot sit below P1, and this row is not vacuous.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 27): the only declaration in this lane's classified set so far that sits INSIDE the project's greedy 80% prefix, with 136 marginal spans and 36 spans nothing else in the project covers - the artifact-attach path on the board itself is reached from here alone. The structural case is a semantic-conflict pin (#596): artifacts became board content in a separate PR, so a change fingerprint that ignores the field misclassifies visible progress as a heartbeat and keeps the agent marked stalled with its budget spent - the opposite failure to its pair partner's, and equally silent. Counted with Budget_Resets_OnARealBoardChange_ButNotOnAHeartbeat as ONE P0 unit: that test holds the negative side of what counts as a real change, this one holds a positive the fingerprint is most likely to miss. TASK-1 AUDIT: prefix candidate DECLINED to P1. Misclassifying an artifact attach as a heartbeat leaves an agent marked stalled with its budget spent - a functional defect in an advisory nudge service, not a component-baseline contract. Its 36 exclusive spans hold the P1 floor.

The broadest negative for the OnChanged subscription: five different board mutations - two adds, a claim, a status change and a note - and the service must attempt no delivery at all. The DeliveryAttempts assertion is what makes it stronger than the other suppression tests: they check that nothing was DELIVERED, which a service that tries and is refused would also satisfy, while this one checks the sink was never called. That distinction matters because the sink is a real conversation injection in production, and an attempt has cost even when it fails.

The distinguishing negative for the breakdown tier, and the one whose failure is the file's own theme: nudging an agent to decompose a task that is already decomposed asks for work that exists, so the agent has nothing to do that would stop the nudge - a loop with no exit that the two-per-period budget bounds only after it has already fired twice. Advances the clock two hours, well past the window, so the suppression is attributable to the sub-items rather than to the lease still being fresh.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 104): 23 marginal spans, 13 of them exclusive - the breakdown evaluator's positive path, reached only here. The N4 tier's sole positive, and it is time-driven: the same call delivers nothing while the lease is fresh and one message after the clock advances past the configured window, so the threshold is pinned by contrast within one body rather than assumed. Uses FakeTimeProvider, so there is no wall-clock wait and no flake surface. Asserts the task id and the tool name in the detail.

The anti-perpetual-motion contract itself, and the class docstring calls it the load-bearing test for good reason: it walks the budget being spent, a heartbeat failing to re-arm it, and a real board change re-arming it, in one body, asserting the stalled marker at each step. The failure it prevents is an unbounded nudge loop - an agent that is nudged, produces nothing, gets nudged again forever - which costs tokens on every cycle and stops only when someone notices. Its comment names the two mutations that must go red against it, and both are real: an unconditional reset in HandleBoardChangedAsync re-arms on the heartbeat step, and a reset keyed on delivery makes the cap never bind. The heartbeat is not synthetic - re-claiming an in-progress task by its own holder refreshes only the lease timestamp, so the change hook fires while nothing the board SAYS changed. Half of a P0 unit with AttachingAnArtifact_IsARealBoardChange_AndResetsTheBudget, which supplies the positive this negative needs. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Outside the project's 80% greedy P0 prefix and carrying no named exception - the contract argued here is a distinct primary behaviour, a distinguishing/non-vacuity partner of another row, or a component/class baseline, and the rubric's outside-prefix exception applies only where a component would otherwise have no P0 pinning its essential contract. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 561): 2 marginal spans. The only test covering the service's lock discipline (#599 review F-002), and the race is real rather than hypothetical - TaskManager fires OnChanged after releasing its own lock and sub-agents share one manager, so two hooks genuinely interleave. If the board read happens outside _sync, a losing thread commits a snapshot OLDER than the winner's, rewinding the baseline so an assignment already notified is re-detected as a transition. Built on a deterministic seam rather than sleeps: the loser's read parks on a gate, and the comment is explicit that both outcomes are deterministic - with the fix the winner is lock-blocked and the one-second wait simply elapses. That is the right way to write it, but the timeouts are still wall-clock bounds, so it is the most flake-exposed row in the file and it is not cheap. Below P0 on consequence: the defect duplicates a notice rather than losing or looping one.
uncertainties: wall-clock-bounded-gates

rationale: Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 608): 2 marginal spans, none exclusive. Additional variation: the N3 counter's copy of the reset-on-real-change rule that Budget_Resets_OnARealBoardChange_ButNotOnAHeartbeat holds at P0 for the stall tier - and unlike that test it does not exercise the heartbeat side, so an unconditional reset passes here. Real behaviour, weaker statement.

The N3 tier's whole behaviour in one body: silence below the threshold, a nudge at it with the turn count in the message, the counter re-arming for a second nudge, and then the same two-per-idle-period budget binding across further turns with the agent marked stalled. Distinct primary behaviour rather than a variation - the idle-turn counter is a different trigger from run-end, and the re-arm step is what separates "nudge every turn after the third" from "nudge every third silent turn". Below P0 because the budget that bounds it is already pinned at P0 through the run-end tier.

A distinct suppression rule with its own rationale: a run that errored or was cancelled is surfaced to the user through the error path, so nudging on top of it adds noise to a conversation that is already reporting a problem - and would nudge an agent to continue work its run just failed out of. Covers both flags in one body. Nothing else exercises the errored or cancelled arms of HandleRunEndedAsync.

A second distinct not-a-stall rule, and a different predicate from the terminal case: waiting on a NAMED blocker is a correct stop. Nudging here would tell an agent to proceed on work it has correctly declined to start, and the agent's only available response is to either ignore the nudge or break the dependency. Arranges a real blocking relationship between two rows rather than a status flag, so it exercises the dependency read rather than a shortcut.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 607): 2 marginal spans. The done-is-not-stalled rule, and the most common shape in normal operation - an agent finishes its work and its run ends, which is every successful turn. If this regressed, every completed agent would be nudged to keep working on a board with nothing left on it, which is the perpetual-motion failure arriving through a different door than the budget.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 252): 6 marginal and 4 exclusive spans on the tier-disabled guards. The shipped-defaults gate: with the default options every stall tier is OFF, and this drives all three stall entry points - run-ended, turn-completed and breakdown - to prove none of them delivers. It is the counterweight to the P0 positive above, and the failure it prevents is the one that reaches every deployment at once: a tier that defaults on starts injecting messages into every agent conversation in the product, and the nudges look like ordinary output, so nothing reports it as a fault. Three entry points in one body is what makes it a gate rather than a spot check - a default flipped on any single tier fails here. TASK-1 AUDIT: demoted to P1. Outside the project's 80% greedy P0 prefix and carrying no named exception - the contract argued here is a distinct primary behaviour, a distinguishing/non-vacuity partner of another row, or a component/class baseline, and the rubric's outside-prefix exception applies only where a component would otherwise have no P0 pinning its essential contract. Kept at P1 so it still runs in the primary-contract tier.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 154): 13 marginal spans, all 13 exclusive - the root-run-ended entry point is reached from here alone. Asserts BOTH directions in one body: with the opt-in off nothing is delivered, and after rebuilding with it on the same event delivers to the named root assignee. That two-sidedness is what makes it a gate rather than a suppression check - the off case alone is satisfied by a service that can never nudge the root at all. The default matters because the root conversation is a person, not an agent: nudging it by default turns an internal scheduling mechanism into unsolicited messages to the user.

Measured (coverage-facts, greedy rank 80): 37 marginal spans and 13 exclusive - the root turn-completed entry point, covered by nothing else. Asserts both directions of the opt-in on the N3 tier the way the stall tier's root test does, and the pair of them is what establishes the opt-in as a policy across triggers rather than a check in one handler. Threshold of 1 so a single tick decides, which keeps the test reading as a gate test rather than a counting test.

Additional variation covering the message copy rather than the mechanism: the first nudge must not claim to be final and the second must say so. The counts it depends on are pinned by the budget tests, and the escalation itself is a wording contract with no behavioural consequence beyond how the agent reads it. Real, cheap, and not the row to run first.

Additional variation on the cap: five run-ends yield the documented maximum and the agent is marked stalled. Both assertions appear inside Budget_Resets_OnARealBoardChange_ButNotOnAHeartbeat, which reaches the same spent-budget state and then goes on to test the reset, so a broken cap fails there first. Its one distinct property is that it asserts against TodoNudgeService.MaxStallNudgesPerIdlePeriod rather than a literal, so it follows the constant if the cap is ever retuned - worth keeping for that.

The reported defect's own regression: sandbox, sub-agent and workflow tools were absent from the catalog entirely, so there was nothing for the Modes editor to tick even once gating stopped keying on the mode id.
Every qualified group must offer a wildcard row, which is the escape hatch from an incomplete or growing listing. Asserted per group rather than for one example.
Every row must carry the label its group defines, so a newly added group cannot reach the editor as an unheaded section. Front member with exclusiveSpans=1 at greedyRank 340, so the P1 floor applies.
Catalog-wide invariant: two rows sharing an id make a mode's stored selection ambiguous. No per-group test can observe a collision across groups.

The id/name split for qualified groups: the prefix is a selection id while Name stays bare, because Name is what the model sees and a prefixed one would advertise a tool that does not exist. Front member with exclusiveSpans=1 at greedyRank 694, so the P1 floor also applies.
Sandbox rows come from the live gateway listing, including a plugin-provided tool no static list could know about, and carry no warning while the gateway is up.
A conversation gets the legacy set or the collaboration set, never both, but the editor must offer both because choosing between them is how a mode picks its surface.

Exactly the legacy names are pre-ticked for a mode with no capability selection - pre-ticking a collaboration tool would silently upgrade that mode's surface. Front member with exclusiveSpans=1 at greedyRank 695, so the P1 floor also applies.

Deliberately not a name list: the group is populated from the same object the conversation registry uses, so adding a task tool cannot skip the editor. A hard-coded list would pass a name-based test forever.

Compatibility contract with modes already persisted: every unqualified row must address itself by bare name, which is the form sitting in their EnabledTools. Qualifying them would silently unselect every stored tool.

Degraded-mode handling: with the gateway unreachable every sandbox row - the wildcard included - carries the warning, because an unlabelled fallback has the user build an allow-list that silently omits tools their workspace really has. Front member with exclusiveSpans=3 at greedyRank 52 (marginalNewSpans=68), so the P1 floor also applies.
Exactness companion to the wildcard-availability contract: no ordinary row carries the flag.
Group-content assertion that the workflow group carries both provider families; a membership check over the grouping already pinned at P1.
Constructor argument validation.

Pins the accepted gap rather than papering over it: work pending at Dispose is dropped, not written, because an awaited shutdown flush loses a race with the session registry's disposal guard and is swallowed anyway. A later well-meaning shutdown flush would change documented behaviour and fails here.
uncertainties: a 300ms negative window; it can only weaken the assertion, never produce a false failure

rationale: Idle disposal must be safe and repeatable, since the host may dispose along more than one teardown path. Front member with exclusiveSpans=2 at greedyRank 499, so the P1 floor applies.

The shutdown wait is BOUNDED, proven with a callback that ignores its cancellation token, so host teardown cannot hang on a gateway call that never returns. Cooperative cancellation would satisfy no part of this.

Starvation contract: a key that re-schedules itself - the mirror's normal traffic on Progressing and Deferred - must go behind a key that has been waiting longer. Against a HashSet.First() drain the re-scheduled key deterministically retakes its freed slot and the waiting key never runs; only a FIFO order passes.

The lost-wakeup race: a Schedule landing between the drain deciding to stop inside the lock and that decision becoming observable adds a key nothing will ever pick up, so a conversation whose last turn just ended silently ends one turn early in the transcript. Contended for over 2000 rounds by spinning on the flush counter rather than waited on.
uncertainties: a 2000-round spin loop; each round is bounded by a 5s failure timeout, so a genuinely lost key fails rather than hangs

rationale: The reason pending work is a SET rather than one bool slot: scheduling conversation B while A's flush is in flight must not consume A's re-arm. With a single slot A's newest turn never reaches disk.

The regression this copy exists for: the UsagePersistenceWriter shape catches once and aborts the drain, so one permanently broken conversation strands every other one and the re-armed failing key aborts each restarted drain again. Here the catch is per key and the error is reported against the key that failed. Front member with exclusiveSpans=1 at greedyRank 644, so the P1 floor also applies.

Exactly-one coalescing for an in-flight key: neither lost (new lines never written) nor multiplied per call (a burst of turn boundaries multiplying gateway calls). The exact count is only observable because Dispose waits on the drain first.
A best-effort mirror must not throw into the subscriber loop after disposal, and must not flush either. Front member with exclusiveSpans=2 at greedyRank 505, so the P1 floor applies.
uncertainties: a 300ms negative window for the no-flush half; it can only weaken the assertion

rationale: Argument validation for null and empty keys, as a two-case theory.

AC 8: Schedule must not put I/O on the subscriber's thread, proven two ways at once - the callback never completes until the test releases it, and the flush provably runs on a different managed thread. A blocking Schedule would stall the subscriber loop that calls it.

The error channel must not be able to kill the loop: a throwing onError would fault the drain task and leave the fault unobserved, stopping every conversation's mirror. Front member with exclusiveSpans=3 at greedyRank 168 (marginalNewSpans=11), so the P1 floor also applies.
Baseline two-key smoke over the pending-set behaviour whose real failure modes (drop, loss on exit, starvation) are pinned separately at P1.

The CAS-loss contract at a second site: the reconcile pass runs its own compare-and-swap and can lose one, in which case it must retire its own candidate and leave the winner published rather than destroying a session the registry is actively handing out. The service is a singleton and the workspace id is caller-supplied, so a per-id gate allocated for an id that names nothing is a permanent leak - gates are never removed and the semaphore is never disposed. A lost-update on the retry budget across generations: a fresh trigger clears the budget from the subscriber thread while a previous generation's flush is still inside a gateway call, and counting that older Deferred when it returns starts the new generation one attempt down - so a workspace recovering from an outage gets fewer retries exactly when it needs them, with nothing reporting that the budget was spent on a result the caller had abandoned. The arrangement is disciplined: the in-flight flush is genuinely parked on a gate rather than assumed to be, and the test ASSERTS the drain is still parked - flush count exactly 1 - before releasing, so a gate that failed to hold is reported as such instead of silently invalidating the result. Two properties in one test on purpose, and the reasoning is the best in the file: the cheap way to guarantee termination is to mark every descendant the sweep merely LOOKED at, which loses the failing one silently, and the cheap way to guarantee the retry is to keep asking while anything is uncovered, which spins forever on a descendant that can never be written - only an implementation doing both passes. The bound is derived rather than guessed, from window tiling over the roster, and the doomed descendant is chosen as whichever the first slice reaches so the test does not encode the scanner's ordering. Settling is the real termination check: a non-terminating chain never goes quiet and fails as a timeout. Coverage: rank 238, 7 marginal, 0 exclusive.

Attachment must be COMPLETE when Attach returns, not merely requested, and the consequence is total for the commonest shape: the agent's replay buffer is opened by a run assignment and closed by the completion, so a completion arriving before the subscriber exists is neither delivered live nor replayed - a conversation that runs once and stops is then never mirrored at all.
