rationale: Concurrent bulk initializations complete without throwing and the board is non-empty afterwards. Catches an outright crash when two agents initialize at once. P2: with the clear flag in play the final content is not deterministic, so the assertions are weaker than the add test's exact count.
requirements: in-process only; runs concurrent bulk operations
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The echo lines are asserted in order with their dotted ids and their per-level indent, and the parent-versus-child indent is then checked as a relation rather than only as a literal. Catches an echo that omits nested rows or renders them at the wrong depth, leaving the model no way to see it built the wrong shape. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it covers bulk creation and its whole echo format in one path, which is the widest single reach in this component.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Two rows past the cap, the header still carries the true totals, the elision names how many it hid and how many it showed, exactly fifty rows are listed, and the hidden row really is absent. Catches a silent cap, which reads to the model as a complete list and is the same false-completeness failure this echo change exists to prevent. P1: the truncation branch, with its own count and absence assertions.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Two initializations agreeing on the root titles but differing in how many children hang under the first produce different text, and each names the ids it actually minted. Catches the reported regression where the two came back byte-identical, giving the model no signal it had built the wrong shape. P1: a differential contract the single-shape echo test cannot express.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: With three of four subtask entries blank, the header counts one and only that row is listed. Catches a header counting the input rather than the rows created, so the model believes four subtasks exist and addresses ids that were never minted. P1: the count-matches-reality rule is distinct from the skip rule its sibling covers.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The clear flag announces itself, removes the prior row and adds the new one. Catches a flag accepted and ignored, so a requested reset silently appends to the old board instead. P1: a distinct destructive branch of the bulk path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The clear announcement leads the output, ahead of the richer listing. Catches the two messages being ordered so the clear is buried. P2: an ordering variation combining two behaviours already covered separately.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Blank subtask entries are skipped and the one real subtask appears exactly once. Catches blank entries minting empty rows. P2: the subtask-side counterpart of the same input boundary.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Blank, whitespace and null task titles are skipped and the one real task is created, with no error emitted. Catches a whole bulk call failing because one row was blank. P2: an input boundary over the bulk path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A flat initialization keeps the shorter header with no zero-subtask clause. Catches a needlessly noisy header on the most common shape. P2: a formatting variation over the echo the P0 pins.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A null list and an empty list both return the same exact error. Catches an empty bulk call reported as a successful initialization of nothing. P2: an empty boundary over the bulk path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Two tasks with subtasks and notes are created and all appear in the listing. Catches a bulk call that creates the roots and drops the notes, which the echo-focused P0 never supplies. P1: it is the only bulk test that exercises the note-creation branch.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Claiming a second task releases the first back to not-started while keeping the ownership record on it, and says so. Catches one agent holding two active leases, which breaks the one-in-progress-per-assignee rule the whole coordination model rests on. P1: a distinct cross-row invariant no single-task test can reach.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: At exactly the threshold a foreign claim is refused and the original holder keeps the task; one tick later the same call succeeds and the holder changes. Catches an inclusive-versus-exclusive comparison error that would either let a live lease be stolen or wedge an abandoned one, and it is the only case that distinguishes the two. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because both arms of the staleness decision are pinned at the single instant where they differ, which the five- and sixteen-minute tests cannot do.
requirements: in-process only; a FakeTimeProvider supplies the clock, so no wall-clock or sleep dependency

rationale: Past the threshold the takeover succeeds, names the previous holder in its message, and leaves the task in progress under the new one. Catches a permanent lock that lets a crashed agent wedge a task forever. P1: it carries the takeover message and the resulting status, neither of which the threshold test asserts.
requirements: in-process only; a FakeTimeProvider supplies the clock, so no wall-clock or sleep dependency

rationale: Five minutes in, a foreign claim is refused and the original assignee stands. Catches a lease that is not a lock at all. P2: the same arm and the same assertions as the first half of the threshold test, at a non-distinguishing instant.
requirements: in-process only; a FakeTimeProvider supplies the clock, so no wall-clock or sleep dependency

rationale: A successful claim reports the holder and writes the status, the assignee and a claim timestamp. Catches a claim that echoes success while recording no owner, which leaves every ownership and lease rule downstream with nothing to work from. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the lease subsystem's baseline write and the only test covering all three stored fields together.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A holder re-claiming their own task after it was blocked out from under them is refused with the blocked code. Catches the same-holder refresh fast path skipping the block guard the ordinary claim path enforces. P1: a distinct interaction between two subsystems.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: The test comment states this scenario currently reaches the general claim path rather than the fast path, because block-task always flips the status in the same call; the fast path's own guard is defence in depth that no reachable input exercises today.

rationale: Running exactly the sequence the refusal prescribes does complete the task. Catches guidance that names steps which do not actually work, and it is what stops every completion-gate refusal test passing for a gate that refuses unconditionally. P1: the non-vacuity control for the whole gate family.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The refusal message spells out the three-step recovery: claim with an agent name, move to in progress, then complete. Catches a refusal that states the rule without saying how to satisfy it, which is what turns one refusal into a retry storm. P1: the message content is a distinct contract from the refusal itself.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A dependency recorded from a padded id is confirmed stored canonically and then released when the blocker completes. Catches the release matching on an id that was never normalized, which would leave the dependent blocked forever behind a satisfied blocker. P1: it ties canonicalization to the release path specifically, where the failure is silent and permanent.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Completing a blocker announces the unblock, returns the dependent to not-started and empties its blocker list. Catches a dependency that is recorded but never released, leaving the dependent blocked after its blocker is done. P1: the release path is distinct from the block and guard paths.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Deleting a depth-three leaf removes exactly that row while both ancestors survive and remain addressable, and the leaf's absence is asserted by exact error text rather than a substring. Catches a delete that reports success and detaches nothing, and equally one that detaches the root ancestor, which every absence assertion alone would accept. P1: the positive control is what distinguishes the two failure modes.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Deleting a parent removes it and its subtasks, and the row is then unreachable. Catches a delete that detaches the parent while orphaning its children in the tree. P1: the destructive path, distinct from the mint and the update.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Deleting an unknown id returns an exact not-found error. Catches a no-op reported as a successful delete. P2: a not-found boundary on the delete path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Omitting the ordinal still deletes the top-level task. Catches the delete carve-out being widened until the ordinary top-level delete is refused too. P2: the partner that keeps its sibling from being fixed the wrong way.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Delete alone treats a sentinel ordinal as an error and the board is unchanged. Catches the tolerance rule being applied uniformly, which on delete would silently widen a subtask deletion into a parent deletion. P1: the deliberate carve-out, and the board comparison is what proves nothing was destroyed rather than only that a message came back.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Deleting one subtask leaves its sibling in place. Catches an over-broad delete that takes the whole child list, which the parent-delete test cannot see because there everything is meant to go. P1: the scoping rule is what makes delete safe to call.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: JSON written before the coordination fields existed still loads, with the absent fields defaulting rather than throwing. Catches a deserializer that rejects every board saved by an earlier version, which loses the user's existing work outright. P1: backward compatibility is a distinct contract the round trip cannot exercise, since the round trip only ever reads what it just wrote.
requirements: in-process only; deserializes a literal string, no filesystem or network dependency

rationale: Edit, list and delete on a depth-three row each resolve, ending with the exact empty-notes message. Catches the depth limit on the remaining note tools. P2: further tools applying the deep addressing rule.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Every tool exposing a subtask ordinal is checked against a roster built from the registry, and each description is required to carry the verbatim guidance about omitting the parameter, with delete's differing carve-out handled explicitly. Catches guidance missing from a newly added tool, which is the condition that produced the observed failure storm. P1: it is the fullest of the description tests, but it asserts attribute text rather than product behaviour, so it does not qualify as a P0.
requirements: in-process only; reflects over tool metadata
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Verbatim phrase matching means an equivalent rewording of the guidance would fail this test without any loss of guidance.

rationale: Every subtask ordinal parameter's description states it is one-based. Catches the same omission on the ordinal side. P2: the ordinal counterpart of the same description assertion.
requirements: in-process only; reflects over tool metadata
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Every task id parameter's description states the ids are one-based. Catches a tool whose description omits the base, leaving a model to guess zero. P2: a description assertion over the registry roster, with no product path exercised.
requirements: in-process only; reflects over tool metadata
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The registry exposes fifteen tools and every one of them declares a string return, so the failure marking travels alongside a payload the caller can actually read. Catches a tool added with a shape the error-signalling contract does not cover, which would silently leave a hole in the two sweeps that iterate this roster. P1: it guards the roster the P0 depends on.
requirements: in-process only; reflects over the tool registry
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: A count of fifteen does not say which fifteen, so a tool swapped for another would still pass.

rationale: The same fifteen tools driven into success carry no failure marking. Catches an implementation that marks everything as a failure, which the failure sweep alone would pass, and it prevents the error signalling being a constant. P1: the non-vacuity partner for the P0, over the same roster.
requirements: in-process only; drives tools through the reflective registry
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: All fifteen tools are driven into a domain failure through the registry and each result is asserted to be marked as a failure carrying an error code, with the roster derived from the registry so a new tool joins automatically. Catches a refusal returned as a successful string, which the caller reads as the operation having worked. P0 because it covers the failure exit of every tool on the surface in one path and is the widest single test in the class.
requirements: in-process only; drives tools through the reflective registry
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Across an add, a claim two minutes later and a completion three minutes after that, all three timestamps carry their own distinct instants. Catches stamps written from a single moment or from the wrong transition, which would make every duration derived from the board wrong. P1: three distinct write points asserted at three distinguishable times.
requirements: in-process only; a FakeTimeProvider supplies the clock, so no wall-clock or sleep dependency

rationale: The markdown accessor and the list tool return the identical string. Catches the two rendering entry points drifting apart, so the panel and the model see different boards. P2: an equivalence between two callers of one renderer, with the renderer itself pinned elsewhere.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Both sides come from the same implementation, so two identically wrong renderings satisfy this; the byte-exact rendering tests are what fix the content.

rationale: The detail view resolves a three-segment dotted id. Catches the same depth limit on the read path. P2: a second tool applying the deep addressing rule.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The detail view shows the attached paths under their own heading. Catches artifacts stored but invisible when inspecting one task. P2: a second reader of the artifact field, with the board-level rendering covered separately.
requirements: in-process only; validates strings without touching the filesystem

rationale: The detail view carries the id and title, the status, a counted notes section and a counted subtasks section. Catches a section dropped from the one view the model uses to inspect a single row. P1: the detail rendering is a distinct surface from the list rendering.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The detail view through the parent-plus-ordinal form names the subtask and its parent. Catches the pair address failing on the read path. P2: an addressing variation over the detail view.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Attached paths reach the wire node in order. Catches artifacts that live only in memory and vanish on persistence or on the client, so a restart loses the evidence trail while the board still claims the work was done. P1: the wire projection is a distinct surface from the two rendered ones.
requirements: in-process only; validates strings without touching the filesystem

rationale: A blocked task maps to the blocked status on the wire node. Catches the newest status member mapping to something else, so a blocked row reaches the client and the persisted board as in-progress. P1: the status mapping onto the wire is a distinct surface, and this is the only test in the class exercising the snapshot for it.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Snapshots taken while the tree is being extended are each checked against structural invariants rather than merely for absence of an exception. Catches a torn read that produces perfectly valid JSON describing a board that never existed, a failure no exception-based test can see because nothing throws. P1: a distinct failure mode over a narrower set of paths than its sibling.
requirements: in-process only; runs concurrent serializers and writers with a bounded duration
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: The invariant helper decides what counts as inconsistent, so the test is only as strong as that set of checks.

rationale: A genuinely unknown filter is still refused. Catches the all tolerance being implemented as accept-anything, which would silently return the whole board for a typo. P2: the negative partner for the tolerated value its sibling establishes.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Attached paths render as plain bullets under their task, and the assertion checks the exact bullet text so a link or a code fence would fail. Catches artifact paths rendered as markup that a downstream reader would try to resolve, and catches them not rendering at all. P1: a distinct rendering branch for a field the other two rendering tests do not set.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: With the clock advanced a fixed amount, the rendered board carries the assignee, the blocker list and an elapsed suffix, again compared as a whole literal. Catches coordination state that is recorded and enforced but invisible on the board, so a human watching cannot see who holds what. P1: a distinct rendering branch, kept deterministic by the injected clock rather than by wall time.
requirements: in-process only; a FakeTimeProvider supplies the clock, so the elapsed suffix is deterministic

rationale: The whole rendered board is compared byte for byte against a literal expectation covering all four statuses, three levels of nesting, notes and line endings. Catches any drift in the one artifact the model and the panel both read, including changes no substring assertion would notice. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because this rendering is the component's primary output and this is the only test that pins it whole.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The word all is accepted as a filter and returns every row rather than being rejected as an unknown status. Catches a natural spelling of no filter turning into a hard error on the most frequently called read tool. P1: a tolerated value on the filter path, distinct from the status aliases on the update path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A filter matching nothing also keeps the header, with a message distinguishing no-matches from no-tasks. Catches the two empty outcomes collapsing into one. P2: the filtered empty boundary alongside the unfiltered one.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The main-only listing shows the parent and omits both subtasks, compared against the full listing that shows all three. Catches a flag accepted and ignored, so a caller asking for a summary gets the whole tree. P1: a distinct projection with its own control in the same test.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An empty board still emits the titled header before the empty message. Catches a bare sentence that leaves the model unable to tell which tool answered. P2: an empty boundary over the list rendering.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Three status filters each return their own rows and exclude the others, asserted in both directions. Catches a filter that matches everything, which the exclusion assertions are what detect. P1: filtering is a distinct read path from the unfiltered listing.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An added note is echoed and reads back through the note listing. Catches notes accepted and discarded, which is where an agent's working context lives between turns. P1: the note subsystem's baseline.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Concurrent note operations complete without throwing and the task still has notes afterwards. Catches a crash in the note list under contention. P2: the closing assertion is a lower bound of at least one note, so it cannot detect notes lost to a race.
requirements: in-process only; runs concurrent note operations
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: A lower-bound assertion of this shape passes as long as anything survives, so most lost-update outcomes would go unreported.

rationale: Deleting note one removes it and leaves note two. Catches a delete that clears the whole list, which the surviving-note assertion is what detects. P1: a distinct note operation with its own scoping rule.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Editing note one replaces its text, asserted both by the new text being present and the old being gone. Catches an edit that appends instead of replacing. P1: a distinct note operation with a paired presence and absence assertion.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Index zero and index past the end are both refused, and the error states how many notes exist. Catches a one-based index treated as zero-based, which would edit the wrong note. P2: a range boundary tested from both sides.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An unknown note action returns an exact error naming the three legal ones. Catches an unrecognized action defaulting to add. P2: an argument boundary on the note dispatcher.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A note failure whose message is rewritten on the way out keeps its failure marking. Catches a rewording step that rebuilds the result and drops the marking, which is exactly how a failure quietly becomes a success in a layer that only meant to improve the wording. P1: it separates the message from the marking, which every message-only assertion in this file conflates.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An unknown note action is marked as a failure. Catches the note dispatcher's default branch returning an unmarked string. P2: one tool's instance of the property the fifteen-tool sweep already covers.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Adds, updates, notes, listings and searches run together without throwing and every call returns something. Catches a deadlock or a crash from interleaving different tool paths, which single-operation tests cannot produce. P2: the assertions are a result count and non-null, so nothing about the resulting board state is checked.
requirements: in-process only; runs mixed concurrent operations
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: A count plus non-null says only that every task returned; it would accept every call having failed.

rationale: Reads through the listing, the detail view, search and the snapshot run against continuous nested adds, and any collection-modified exception on either side fails the test. Catches an unsynchronized enumeration over a mutating child list, which is the crash a board shared between a panel and a working agent hits first. P0 because it covers the widest set of read paths under mutation of any test in this class, and its failure mode is an exception rather than an assertion, so it discriminates by construction.
requirements: in-process only; runs concurrent readers and writers with a bounded duration
no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Like every race test, a pass shows the race did not occur on this run rather than that it cannot occur.

rationale: A board carrying assignee, claim timestamps, blocker lists and nesting survives serialization and comes back with every coordination field intact. Catches a field that is enforced in memory and lost on the wire, which silently voids every lease and block the moment the board is persisted or handed to a client. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the widest single path through the serialization component and the only test asserting the fields in both directions.
requirements: in-process only; serializes to a string, no filesystem or network dependency

rationale: Three casings of the same term all match. Catches a case-sensitive search that misses whatever casing the model happens to use. P2: a matching variation over the search path.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Total, completed, pending and removed counts are each asserted by exact string equality over a board holding all four states, including a subtask so the counts cover the whole tree rather than roots only. Catches a count that omits nested rows or miscategorizes a removed one. P1: the counting branch is distinct from the search branch of the same tool.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A term matches two of three tasks, with the count stated and the non-matching row absent. Catches a search that returns everything, which the absence assertion is what detects. P1: search is a distinct read path from listing.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Across five tools and ten cases, non-positive ordinals are compared differentially against the same call with the parameter omitted, and the whole board is compared afterwards so an equal message over a differently mutated board still fails. Catches the reported pattern where a model passes zero or minus one to mean not applicable and gets a refusal, which drove a very high error rate on this tool surface. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because the differential form covers every one of these tools' resolution paths in a single test and asserts equivalence rather than a message.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A third level mints its dotted id. Catches a depth cap on the add path. P2: it asserts the same thing as AddTask_ToSubtask_ShouldAddNestedTask in the same class, with different titles.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Structurally the same scenario and assertions as AddTask_ToSubtask_ShouldAddNestedTask. This is an observation from reading both bodies, not a measured redundancy claim.

rationale: A thousand adds complete inside a wall-clock budget and the total count is exact. Catches an accidental quadratic in the add path, for instance a full-tree scan per insertion. P2: a performance smoke test whose count assertion is the only deterministic part.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
asserts against a wall-clock stopwatch, so it is machine- and load-dependent
uncertainties: The five-second budget is generous enough that a substantial slowdown could pass, and a loaded machine could fail it with no product change.

rationale: Seven titles carrying quotes, angle brackets, ampersands, embedded newlines and tabs, and an emoji all round trip through the add and the listing. Catches escaping or encoding damage to a title the model supplied. P2: an input-domain sweep over the add and list paths.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Titles containing a newline are asserted only after trimming, so what happens to the embedded newline inside the rendered list is not pinned.

rationale: A thousand-character title and a five-thousand-character note are stored and returned whole. Catches a silent truncation that would lose the tail of a long note without any error. P2: a size boundary over the add and detail paths.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A malformed id and a well-formed but absent one produce different outcomes rather than one shared not-found. Catches the two cases collapsing, which sends a model into retrying a syntactically broken id as though the row might appear. P1: it makes the failure classification discriminating, which no single-case assertion can.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A not-found result arriving through the handler layer is a failure at that layer, not a success carrying an apology in its text. Catches the marking being lost between the tool and the handler, so an agent's failure detection sees a clean call. P1: it pins the signalling at a different layer from the registry sweep.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A successful call through the handler is not marked as a failure. Catches the handler marking indiscriminately. P2: the local non-vacuity partner, with the same property covered across all fifteen tools by the registry sweep.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Eight threads race the guard in two deterministic phases: while the last child is definitely open every attempt is refused for the same reason and nothing moves, then after the child is finished a second race lets exactly one attempt win. Catches the guard and the completion it gates not sharing a lock, and the phase split closes the hole the class comment records, where a single-phase race could run every completer before the finisher and pass against an implementation with no guard at all. P1: a distinct concurrency contract, with every wait bounded so a scheduling failure fails rather than hangs.
requirements: in-process only; spawns eight threads twice with a thirty-second bound on every wait
no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Concurrent status updates complete and every result is one of the accepted message shapes. Catches a crash or a corrupted status field under contention. P2: the per-result assertion is an alternation over several allowed shapes, so it accepts a wide range of outcomes including refusals.
requirements: no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Because a refusal is an accepted shape, an implementation that refused every concurrent update would still pass.

rationale: A claim-then-complete sequence reports each transition and the stored status ends at completed. Catches an update that echoes success without writing. P1: the status write is the second most used mutation after the add.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: The same transition through the parent-plus-ordinal address form. Catches the pair address failing to resolve on the update path. P2: an addressing variation over its main-task sibling.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Setting blocked through the status update is refused and the message names the right tool, with the status unchanged. Catches a blocked row with no blocker recorded, which nothing could ever release. P2: an argument boundary on the update path whose value is the redirect it prints.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A task assigned but never claimed, so its assignee already satisfies the other half of the gate, is still refused. Catches a mutation dropping the status check, which the headline case would not detect because that task is also unassigned. P1: it isolates the second conjunct.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A task moved to in-progress without an agent, so its status already satisfies one half of the gate, is still refused. requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A blocked child refuses the parent's completion too. P1: it pins the rule's intent rather than its enumeration, which neither named-status case can.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A parent with an unfinished child is refused with a dedicated error code naming the open row, and the parent's status does not move. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the guard's direct case and the smallest test covering refusal, error code, named row and unchanged state.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An in-progress child, claimed by a different agent so the parent's own lease survives, also refuses. Catches a guard that checks only for not-started rows. P2: a status variation over the guard the P0 establishes.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A grandchild added under an already-completed child still refuses the top-level parent, and the intermediate child is left untouched by the refusal. Catches a guard that checks direct children only, which is reachable by an ordinary sequence since nothing forbids adding a subtask under a completed row. P1: the subtree walk is a distinct property from the per-child status check.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: With one completed and one removed child the parent completes. Catches a guard that treats removed as unfinished, which would make an abandoned subtask block its parent forever, and it is the positive that stops all four refusal tests passing for a guard that refuses everything. P1: the terminal-status rule plus the family's non-vacuity partner.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Completing a task that was never claimed is refused with a dedicated code. Catches work marked done with no record of who did it, which makes the whole ownership trail unenforceable. P1: the completion gate's headline case.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: Both halves of the gate would refuse this task, so on its own it cannot tell which half is doing the work; the two sibling tests below are what isolate them.

rationale: The agentless in-progress transition on a blocked, assigned task is refused, the status stays blocked, and completion remains unreachable. Catches the reported back door where that transition bypassed the claim path and so inherited none of its guards, letting block, assign, start and complete walk a blocked task to done. P1: a distinct entry point into the same state machine.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Three hyphenated spellings normalize correctly. Catches a separator the alias table omits. P2: a spelling variation over the alias rule its underscore sibling establishes.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: An unrecognized status returns an error naming all four legal values. Catches a typo silently mapping to a default status. P2: an argument boundary whose error text doubles as the model's recovery hint.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: Ten spellings across four statuses each normalize to the canonical form, covering underscore, space and colloquial aliases. Catches an alias dropped, which turns an ordinary model phrasing into a hard refusal. P1: the alias table is a distinct rule from the status write itself.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency
uncertainties: The ten cases run in a foreach inside one test method rather than as a theory, so the first failure hides the rest.

rationale: Ordinary parent-plus-ordinal calls across the tool surface still resolve to the row they name, checked against the board rather than against the message. Catches a tolerance change that quietly makes the ordinal advisory, so every well-formed nested call starts landing on the parent. P1: the control that stops the whole tolerance family passing for an implementation that ignores the parameter outright.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: A positive but wrong ordinal is refused with a message stating the one-level-below rule and naming how many children the parent actually has. Catches tolerance being extended to positive ordinals, which would silently address the wrong row, and catches a refusal that gives the model nothing to correct with. P1: it draws the line between tolerated and meaningful values, which the sentinel test alone does not.
requirements: in-process only; no filesystem, network or clock dependency

rationale: One specific proposed-and-rejected tool name is absent from the built surface. Catches that tool being reintroduced, when it duplicates an existing status update and was dropped deliberately. P2: a single named absence over the surface its sibling counts.
requirements: in-process only; builds a function registry over a fresh TaskManager
uncertainties: An absence assertion over a name that was never added; it is kept honest only by the sibling count test, which shows the built surface is non-empty.

rationale: Registering the board and building the registry yields exactly fifteen contracts. Catches a sixteenth tool added without a decision: every mode that enables the board pays for all the contracts in each turn's input tokens, and the evaluation corpus hashes the vocabulary, so a silent addition invalidates recorded runs. P1: the number is the deliverable here, and the class doc is explicit that this is a pinning test whose value is the mutation rather than a proof of any fix.
requirements: in-process only; builds a function registry over a fresh TaskManager
uncertainties: A count alone does not pin which fifteen: renaming a tool, or removing one while adding another, keeps this green.

rationale: On a live board, two added rows leave nothing owed, and deleting one still leaves nothing owed. Catches a ledger that reports ordinary present or deliberately deleted rows as missing, which would make every capture claim data loss. P2: both assertions are emptiness checks over the same capture.
uncertainties: The name promises a row is owed until deleted, but both assertions expect an empty set, so nothing here observes the ledger actually owing anything. The owed state is only exercised by the tests that start from a snapshot with pre-populated missing ids.

rationale: A requested reset clears the ledger so the renumbered board does not report every reused id as vanished, while a control manager that was not reset still reports the same loss. Catches a reset that leaves stale entries behind, turning every post-reset board into a false data-loss alarm, and the control rules out a detector that simply stopped working. P1: a distinct ledger-lifecycle rule with its own non-vacuity partner.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: delete-task resolves subtasks through its own lookup, carved out of the shared tolerance rule, so that fourth exit is wired and pinned separately, with the warning naming the operation. Catches a loss discovered during a delete going unreported. P1: a distinct exit, the last of the four.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: Deleting a parent removes its children from the ledger too, asserted through the captured snapshot because a lookup of the child stops at the missing parent and can never reach the retained entry. Catches a subtree walk removed, which would publish and then persist a deleted child as a row the board still owes. P1: a distinct ledger-maintenance rule, and the comment records that the obvious lookup-based assertion stayed green under exactly that mutation.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: A dotted nested id resolves through the path-walk not-found exit rather than the shared subtask lookup, so it gets its own warn-and-be-silent pair. Catches a loss reported on the flat route but not on the nested one. P1: a distinct exit whose probe, per the recorded mutation, could be removed with every other test still green.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: An id the agent itself deleted is silent, with the same paired positive. Catches the second false-positive class, where every ordinary delete followed by a stale reference reads as data loss. P1: a distinct ledger-removal mechanism from never-minted, on the same discrimination rule.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: An id the board never minted is silent, and the same manager through the same call still warns for an id it really held. Catches a detector that fires on every not-found, which would bury the real losses under model typos and make the signal worthless, and the paired positive rules out the opposite failure of a detector that never runs. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because the discrimination rule is what makes the warning usable and no amount of warn-correctly testing detects its absence.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: A lookup of a row the board owes emits exactly one warning whose single line carries the task id, the thread id and the last-seen instant, under the expected event name. Catches silent board loss, the reported failure where twenty rows disappeared and the server logged nothing while agents discovered it through not-found errors. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the detector's baseline and the assertion deliberately requires all three facts on one record rather than scattered across the log.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: Four spellings of the same id that lookup resolves identically all warn. Catches a probe made against the raw input rather than the parsed id, under which a real loss goes unreported purely because of how the model typed the number. P1: a distinct rule about which value the ledger is probed with, not an input boundary.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: The capture carries the owed id with its last-seen instant and not the surviving one, and a manager rebuilt from that capture still discriminates and still reports the original timestamp. Catches a ledger rebuilt from surviving rows alone, under which every row lost in a previous process reads as never-minted and the loss is unreportable exactly when it matters most. P1: the durability path, distinct from in-process detection.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: Four call shapes are run against a watched and an unwatched manager and compared on both error code and text, then the literal wording and error code are asserted outright. Catches an observability feature that changed the answer the model receives. P1: a distinct behavioural-neutrality contract, and the differential comparison would otherwise be satisfiable by two identically wrong results were the literal assertions not there.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: Three lookups of the same lost row produce three warnings. Catches a report-once detector, which would have sized the reported 48-call storm at one and hidden how much work the loss actually cost. P1: a distinct no-self-silencing rule that the single-warning tests cannot express.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: The ordinal subtask lookup is a third not-found exit, and its warning names the dotted id addressed rather than the parent. Catches a loss unreported on that route, and a warning that points at the wrong row. P1: a distinct exit with its own message contract.
requirements: in-process only; a CapturingLogger stands in for the logging pipeline, timestamps are fixed constants

rationale: A manager built with no logger neither throws on the detector path nor changes its answer. Catches an unguarded logger dereference in every throwaway construction site the host has. P2: a null boundary over the detector path.

With the caller's token already cancelled, the same exception propagates instead of being converted into a timeout message. Catches a tool that swallows a real cancellation and returns text, so a cancelled turn keeps producing tool output. P1: the distinguishing half of the cancellation pair.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network
uncertainties: The fake throws OperationCanceledException unconditionally, so this pins how the handler classifies the exception given the caller's token state, not that the token reached the provider. That threading is covered only by the sibling token-identity test.

rationale: With a small cap, the returned text ends with the truncation marker and its total length stays within the cap, so the cap applies to the final framed output rather than the raw content. Catches an oversized page blowing the context budget despite a configured cap. P1: a distinct output-size contract, and the marker assertion keeps the length bound from standing alone.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A valid URL reaches the provider and the page content comes back inside the untrusted-content frame, with both the opening and closing banners asserted. Catches the tool's primary path broken and, separately, fetched page text delivered to the model without its injection warning. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the component's baseline contract and the only test covering the whole success path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A 404 becomes a message naming the status and the condition, with the upstream body absent. Catches an exception message pasted into the model's view, which is how an upstream that echoes a request header leaks a key. P1: the mapped-status error path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A transport failure with no status yields a short generic error: the prefix is fixed, the upstream detail is gone, and the whole message is under a hard length bound. Catches an unbounded exception string reaching the transcript on the one path where no status code exists to key a friendly message off. P1: a distinct branch from the mapped-status path, and the length bound is paired with a positive prefix assertion so it is not an upper bound alone.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A malformed URL, a non-http scheme, an empty string and a localhost address each produce an error with the provider never called. Catches the tool validating and then calling anyway, which every WebInputValidator test would still pass while the SSRF gate did nothing. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is what makes the validator load-bearing, and the not-called assertion is the part no other test makes.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A reset URL carrying an email and a token is fetched in full but echoed with only host and path. Catches both halves of the split at once: a secret displayed in the source line, and a minimized URL wrongly used for the request so the fetch silently returns the wrong page. P1: a distinct display-versus-request contract.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A selector one character past the cap is dropped. Catches an unbounded header value. P2: a size boundary over the option-forwarding path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A URL supplied by the provider rather than the caller is also minimized before it reaches the output. Catches minimization applied only to caller input, leaving an upstream-controlled redirect target free to carry a secret into the transcript. P1: a second, untrusted source of the same field.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A selector and a no-cache flag arrive on the provider options. Catches options accepted from the model and dropped, so the tool quietly ignores what was asked and may serve stale content. P1: the option-forwarding path, distinct from the URL path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A selector containing a line feed is dropped rather than forwarded. Catches a CRLF injection into the selector header, which the provider adds without validation, letting a model-supplied string append arbitrary headers to the upstream request. P1: a named injection vector, not a generic input boundary.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: The token the provider receives is the same token the caller passed. Catches a handler that creates its own token and drops the caller's, leaving a cancelled turn waiting on an upstream. P1: the only test proving the token threads through, which neither cancellation test can show because the fake throws regardless.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network
uncertainties: Token identity is asserted, so a handler that correctly links the caller's token into a combined timeout token would fail here even though its behaviour is right.

rationale: A cancellation raised while the caller's token is untouched is reported as a timeout rather than rethrown. Catches an internal timeout surfacing as a cancelled turn instead of a message the model can act on. P1: half of the pair that distinguishes the two sources of the same exception type.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: The URL handed to the provider keeps the query and loses the fragment. Catches a fragment forwarded upstream or a query stripped, either of which fetches the wrong resource. P1: the request-side normalization, distinct from the display-side minimization.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A query with an embedded control character is refused and the provider is not called. Catches a control byte reaching the upstream request body. P2: a character-class variation over the input gate its sibling establishes.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: Count, country and language all arrive on the provider options with their exact values asserted at tests/Misc.Tests/Utils/WebSearchToolTests.cs:146-148. This is the only test proving any option reaches the provider at all, so it is the non-vacuity anchor for the three negative option tests (CountOutOfRange_ClampedBeforeReachingProvider, MalformedCountry_OmittedFromProviderOptions, MalformedLanguage_OmittedFromProviderOptions): each of those asserts an option is absent or clamped, and absence assertions pass just as well against a forwarding path that was never wired. P0: the option-forwarding contract of the web-search tool, without which a request for three German results quietly returns ten English ones and every negative sibling still passes.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: Negative and zero counts clamp up to the minimum, an enormous count clamps down to the maximum, and an in-range value passes through unchanged. Catches a model-supplied count reaching the upstream unbounded, and equally a clamp that pins every request to one value. P1: a distinct sanitization rule covering both directions and the identity case in one theory.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A query containing an email address and a national identifier never appears in the output, while the provider still receives it verbatim. Catches a tool that echoes the model's query back into the transcript, and the second assertion stops the fix being a query that is silently dropped instead. P1: a distinct output-hygiene contract with its own non-vacuity guard.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network
uncertainties: The identifiers in the query are synthetic literals defined in the test.

rationale: An empty result set yields a fixed message, asserted by equality. Catches an empty frame or blank string the model cannot distinguish from a failure. P2: an empty boundary over the success path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: Two results render with their titles, URLs and snippets inside the untrusted-content frame, with the provider confirmed called. Catches the tool's primary path broken and search results delivered without their injection warning. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is the component's baseline contract and the only test covering the whole success path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: An empty or whitespace query produces an error with the provider never called. Catches a blank search reaching the upstream, and pins that validation gates the call rather than merely running beside it. P1: the input gate, lower consequence than the fetch tool's because the search endpoint is fixed and carries no SSRF surface.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A three-letter, a non-alphabetic and a one-letter country code are each dropped rather than forwarded. Catches junk reaching the upstream parameter. P2: a format boundary over the option-forwarding path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: Four malformed locale strings, including an underscore separator and a trailing empty subtag, are each dropped. Catches an unvalidated locale reaching the upstream. P2: a format boundary alongside its country sibling.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: With no key configured the tool returns an exact message naming the variable to set and never calls the provider. Catches a keyless deployment sending doomed requests upstream and reporting an opaque failure instead of the actionable one. P1: the up-front configuration gate, distinct from the input gates.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network; the key is a literal defined in the test

rationale: The token the provider receives is the same token the caller passed. Catches a handler that drops the caller's token, leaving a cancelled turn waiting on an upstream search. P1: the only test proving the token threads through this tool.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network
uncertainties: Token identity is asserted, so a handler that correctly links the caller's token into a combined timeout token would fail here even though its behaviour is right.

rationale: A cancellation raised while the caller's token is untouched is reported as a timeout rather than rethrown. Catches an internal timeout ending the turn instead of returning a message the model can retry from. P1: a distinct error classification from the mapped HTTP statuses.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network
uncertainties: Unlike the fetch tool, this class has no paired caller-cancellation test, so nothing here shows a genuine caller cancellation is rethrown rather than also becoming a timeout message.

rationale: A 401 becomes a message naming the status and the invalid-key condition, with the upstream body absent from the output. Catches an unauthorized response reported as a generic failure, and an error body echoed into the transcript. P1: the mapped-status error path.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: A well-formed region-qualified locale is forwarded unchanged. Catches a pattern tightened into rejecting every locale with a subtag, which the malformed-input tests would all still pass. P1: this is what keeps those two theories non-vacuous.
requirements: in-process only; the provider is an in-memory fake, no network

rationale: The built fetch contract exposes a non-empty description and three parameters with the expected required flags and JSON types. Catches a required parameter turned optional or a boolean declared as a string, either of which makes the model emit calls the handler rejects. P1: the model-facing schema is a distinct contract from the runtime routing.
requirements: in-process only; the providers are in-memory fakes, no network; the key is a literal defined in the test
uncertainties: Each parameter is looked up by name with Single, so a parameter added or removed is only detected for the three named here; the parameter set itself is not asserted.

rationale: The built search contract exposes a description and four parameters with the expected required flags and JSON types, including count as an integer. Catches a numeric parameter declared as a string, which makes the model send a quoted number the handler then drops. P1: the schema contract for the second tool.
requirements: in-process only; the providers are in-memory fakes, no network; the key is a literal defined in the test
uncertainties: Each parameter is looked up by name with Single, so a parameter added or removed is only detected for the four named here; the parameter set itself is not asserted.

rationale: Registers the tool, builds the registry, invokes the handler the registry hands back, and requires the provider to have been called with the normalized URL and the content to reach the result. Catches a tool registered with a mismatched name or a handler that never reaches its provider, which no unit test of the tool itself can see because they call the handler directly. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it spans registration, dispatch, validation, provider call and rendering in one path.
requirements: in-process only; the providers are in-memory fakes, no network; the key is a literal defined in the test

rationale: The registered search handler reaches its provider with the caller's query. Catches the search tool registered under a name the built handler dictionary does not carry. P1: the same wiring contract applied to the second tool.
requirements: in-process only; the providers are in-memory fakes, no network; the key is a literal defined in the test

rationale: A fully populated fetch result renders its title as a heading, a labelled source line, the body and a quoted warning. Catches a field dropped from the rendered page the model reads. P1: the fetch rendering path, distinct from the primitives.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: With no title, url or warning the output is exactly the content, asserted by equality rather than containment. Catches empty headings or a bare source label emitted for absent fields. P2: the sparse-input variation of the fetch rendering path.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: A result URL carrying an email, a token and a fragment renders with only scheme, host and path. Catches the renderer emitting the raw URL, a defect the minimization P0 cannot see because it tests the primitive and not whether this caller uses it. P1: a distinct integration of the primitive into the rendering path.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: Two results render as numbered markdown links with the snippet, and the second has no snippet so the optional field is exercised in the same pass. Catches broken numbering or a link target that is not the result URL. P1: the search rendering path, distinct from fetch.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: An empty result set renders a fixed message rather than an empty string. Catches a blank tool result the model cannot distinguish from a failure. P2: an empty boundary on the search rendering path.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: Five URLs reduce to scheme, host and path exactly: a reset link carrying an email and a token, a query-borne secret, embedded credentials, a non-default port that must survive, and an authority-only URL that gains a root path. Catches the redaction primitive leaking a token or a password into anything the model or a log sees. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because every echoed URL in both tools passes through this one function and the failure is a secret disclosure.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: Null, blank, unparsable, non-http and relative inputs all collapse to a fixed placeholder rather than the original string. Catches a fail-open path where an input the parser rejects is echoed verbatim, which is exactly where a secret-bearing malformed URL would slip through. P1: the fail-closed half of the primitive the P0 covers.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: A secret occurring in text is replaced by the redaction marker, asserted both by its absence and by the marker's presence. Catches a redaction that finds nothing, which is what stands between an upstream error body and the transcript. P1: the redaction primitive the secret-hygiene tests depend on.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings
uncertainties: The secret here is a literal defined in the test, not a real credential.

rationale: A null or empty secret leaves the text untouched. Catches an empty-string replace that would shred the output character by character when no key is configured. P2: an empty boundary on the redaction primitive.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: A cap below the marker length yields a cut marker rather than a negative-length substring exception. Catches an arithmetic underflow on a misconfigured cap. P2: a degenerate boundary of the truncation rule.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: An oversized string is cut to the cap with the marker appended, and the assertion on the retained prefix pins that the marker counts toward the cap rather than being added past it. Catches an output that overruns the cap by the marker length on every truncation. P1: a distinct primitive from URL minimization.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: A string under the cap is returned unchanged. Catches a marker appended unconditionally. P2: the pass-through boundary of the truncation rule.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings

rationale: The wrapper carries the source, the untrusted label, the do-not-follow instruction and the body unchanged. Catches the prompt-injection banner silently dropped, which would hand fetched page text to the model with no marker that it is attacker-controlled. P1: a distinct model-facing guard from the redaction primitives.
requirements: in-process only; pure functions over strings
uncertainties: The assertions are case-sensitive substring checks on banner wording, so a reworded banner that still warns correctly would fail here for a cosmetic reason.

rationale: A padded query is accepted with the surrounding whitespace removed. Catches a validator that rejects everything, and pins that the returned value is the trimmed form the provider will send. P1: the accept path of the query validator, and the partner that keeps its three reject tests non-vacuous.

A query with an embedded control character is rejected with an error naming the reason. Catches a control byte reaching an upstream request body or header. P1: a distinct rejection rule with a specific error, not a size or emptiness boundary.
Null, empty and whitespace queries are rejected with no value. Catches a blank search reaching the upstream and burning quota. P2: an empty boundary on the query path.
A query longer than the supplied cap is rejected with an error naming the length, proving the cap is the parameter rather than a constant. P2: a size boundary on the query path.

Twenty-four disallowed targets are rejected in one theory: non-http schemes, embedded userinfo, loopback, every private IPv4 block with its 172.16/12 boundaries, link-local including the cloud metadata address, the IPv6 unspecified, loopback, unique-local and link-local forms, the IPv4-mapped IPv6 spellings of all of those, and the internal and reserved suffixes. Catches an SSRF hole that would let a model-supplied URL reach the host's own metadata service or an internal address. P0 because this is the security gate the whole web tool surface rests on and the single test with the broadest reach in the component.
requirements: in-process only; pure string and IP parsing, no network and no DNS-dependent assertion
uncertainties: The IPv4-mapped IPv6 and boundary cases assume the validator parses the literal rather than resolving it; a hostname that resolves to a private address is out of scope here and no test in this file covers that DNS rebinding shape.

rationale: Null, empty and whitespace URLs are rejected with a non-empty error and no value. Catches a blank URL reaching the Uri parser. P2: an empty boundary over the reject path the P0 establishes.
requirements: in-process only; pure string and IP parsing, no network and no DNS-dependent assertion

rationale: A URL past the length cap is rejected with an error naming the length. Catches an unbounded URL forwarded upstream. P2: a size boundary over the reject path.
requirements: in-process only; pure string and IP parsing, no network and no DNS-dependent assertion

rationale: Four ordinary public targets are accepted, including the addresses immediately below and above the 172.16/12 private block. Catches a validator tightened into rejecting everything, and pins that the private-range check does not overreach by one octet. P1: this is what stops the disallowed-targets P0 passing vacuously, and it is the only test holding the accept side of the boundary.
requirements: in-process only; pure string and IP parsing, no network and no DNS-dependent assertion

rationale: An accepted URL comes back with the fragment removed, the query kept and no error. Catches a fragment forwarded upstream, and pins the shape of a successful result across all three fields. P1: the normalization contract is distinct from the accept-or-reject decision.
requirements: in-process only; pure string and IP parsing, no network and no DNS-dependent assertion

rationale: Holds the deterministic staging path with FileShare.None, standing in for another writer's in-flight temp file, and requires the write both to not throw and to actually land. Catches a fixed staging name, under which every writer to one key contends for a single path — and this store is a shared on-disk cache, so several instances over one directory is its ordinary deployment. P0 because the per-instance semaphore cannot cover this and the failure corrupts or loses a write. Coverage caveat: addsNothingNew means ordinary writes traverse the same Set path, but they do not hold a competing staging file open and cannot detect fixed-name cross-instance contention, so overlap is not assertion redundancy.
requirements: filesystem: creates a temp root under Path.GetTempPath() and deletes it in Dispose; opens a file with FileShare.None
uncertainties: The held handle is a deterministic construction rather than a race, which is the point; but it therefore proves the unique-staging-name property specifically, not general concurrency safety.

rationale: A reader holding the destination with FileShare.Read withholds delete access, which is enough to make a replacing rename throw; the handle is released partway through the write so the test asserts the store waits out a transient holder rather than tolerating a permanent one. Catches a missing rename retry, which a cache read concurrently with its own refresh meets constantly. Argued pre-coverage as a P0 because it is a second, independent hazard on the same write path with its own fix, not a variation of the staging-name case.
requirements: filesystem: creates a temp root under Path.GetTempPath() and deletes it in Dispose; holds an open FileStream on the destination
uncertainties: The claim that the rename got at least one attempt against the live handle rests on a fixed Task.Delay(60) before release; nothing observes the attempt itself, so on a slow start the release could precede the first try.
released.Should().BeTrue() cannot fail: the flag is set unconditionally on the same thread before the assertion.

rationale: Whole-system journey: spawns the real Claude Agent SDK CLI against a TCP-bound mock host and asserts both that a scripted turn was consumed and that the marker text surfaced as a TextMessage through SendMessagesAsync (issue #29). Regression: a drained queue that renders nothing.
